name: Davis Co - Sanitary Spill
incident_summary: Caller reports South Davis Sewer District was contacted by North Salt Lake City to inform of a sanitary sewer overflow emerging from a manhole cover at the approximate address 430 South Village Center Drive North Salt Lake.  Caller estimates approximately 2,000 - 2,500 gallons exited the sanitary line.  Cause is due to power failure feeding lift station pumps.  Waste flowed 30-50 feet across the street surface to a storm inlet box which is believed to flow to, and daylight into the Salt Lake City sewer ditch (aka oil drain canal).  South Davis Sewer District pumped down the box and sanitized the path of overland flow between the sanitary manhole and storm drain inlet.

name: Utah County -- Dumping farm waste near Utah lake
incident_summary: A truck labeled "HADCO" was seen dumping a 30-foot trailer full of what appeared to be animal manure or farm waste on the ground next to the Jordan River as it flows out of Utah Lake near the locks on the north end.
title_eventname: Utah County -- Dumping farm waste near Utah lake

name: S&S Express - Diesel Spill on I-80
incident_summary:
Called stated that 300 Gallons of diesel fuel was released on I-80 when road debris tore open the belly tank of an 18-wheeler semi-truck.  The release location is at MP-168 on I-80 EB.

Summit County Health responded.  125 gallons of diesel contained in pools and recovered.  Remaining 175 gallons impacting roadway and soils.  County Hazmat contained the impacted are to approximately 30' x 60' area.  No waterways impacted.  

Cleanup is underway and an insurance claim is being processed.
title_eventname: S&S Express - Diesel Spill on I-80

name: South Salt Lake -- Fire chemical disposal
address: 2255 S. West Temple St., South Salt Lake, UT 84115
address_location: 2255 S. West Temple St., South Salt Lake, UT 84115
incident_summary: Complainant stated that the company is disposing of old or excess kitchen and restaurant fire suppression chemicals down the sink and indoor drains, and that this is a regular practice.
title_eventname: South Salt Lake -- Fire chemical disposal

name: Unknown
incident_summary: Caller informed DERR that due to road construction in the residential subdivision, traffic was reduced to a single lane.  About 7-10 days ago a truck with a solid closed container-bed hauling an unknown material apparently passed beneath a tree.  One limb of the tree ruptured the top of the container as it passed beneath.  The caller arrived home about 15:00 hours that day and observed that a swath of foliage had died.  This swath which the caller said is fairly uniform in wide (18 inches) extended from the tree at 650 East for about four blocks to Canyon Road.  The caller believes the contents from the truck may have been under pressure and sprayed upward at an angle of about 30 degrees off the centerline of the route travelled by the truck into the trees killing the foliage.   The caller did not actually see the truck but arrived home soon after the incident.  A Provo City road crew was present and may have additional information.  The caller only recently made the connection between the damaged tree limb, the truck, and the dead foliage, hence the delay with contact.

name: Halls Crossing - Release from sewer line
incident_summary: Caller reported that Park Rangers observed that an unknown amount of sewage had released to the surface after a suspected clog developed in the sewer line. Sewage released out of a manhole ran into a drainage. Drainage area was observed to have a large amount of algae and mold growth, indicating the release may have been on-going for a long time and that a significant amount of sewage had been released. Sewage had entered into a main channel of Lake Powell. Release is described as slow but contained. Park Service is awaiting authorization to conduct further investigation of the release.
title_eventname: Halls Crossing - Release from sewer line

name: Chevron-Texaco Refinery (Enviro Office) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller notified DERR duty officer of a flaring event.  The flare is burning SO2 and NOX in unknown amounts.  The caller did not know when to expect the flare to stop burning the increased amounts of sour gas, repairs are underway.

24 Hr UPDATE#1: Chris Mitchell notified the UDEQ at 09:58 on 10/19/05 that the refinery continues to release sour gas to flare.  Facility has exceeded permitted SO2 and NOX emissions.  The release will continue until the facility can be brought back on-line which was estimated to be at least 1 day out.

UPDATE NO. 2: (10/20/05, 09:45) Caller reports the flaring continues, exceeding emissions of permitted NOX and SO2.  The release will continue until the facility can be brought back on-line which was estimated to be at least 36 hours.

name: Fuel Release at Landfill
incident_summary: Approximately 40 gallons of hydraulic oil spilled from a trash hauling truck hydraulic line to soil at the landfill.  The spill has been contained and is being absorbed with kitty litter.

name: Tri-County - Newfield treated injection water
incident_summary: Caller reported a pipeline leak resulted in the release of of 116 barrels (bbls) of treated injection water. The treated injection water surfaced in the pipeline right-of-way and ran down a dry-drainage. No surface waters were impacted. Clean-up crews are en-route to remediate contaminated soils and the pipeline will be repaired early next week. Caller notified DOGM, BLM, and the DEQ District Engineer of the release.

name: AMOCO OIL COMPANY (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: CONTACT PERSON RAY FARR PH. 580-3796 AMOCO OIL REMED. SERVICES. STANDING WATER AND FREE PRODUCT IS BEING COLLECTED INTO A DITCH AND THEN VACUUMED INTO A VACUUM TRUCK TO BE RECYCLED ON SITE.  FREE PRODUCT, BENZENE ENRICHED JP-4 WAS FLOATING ON THE PERCHED GROUND WATER. PRIOR TO THE SPILL THE JP-4 RECEIVED AN ADDITIVE TO INCREASE THE VAPOR PRESSURE NAMELY NAPHA. APPROXIMATELY 150 GALLONS HAVE BEEN COLLECTED THUS FAR AND MORE FREE PRODUCT WILL BE COLLECTED OVER THE WEEKEND.  PROBLEM:  LEAK IN PIPELINE AND ANOTHER LEAK IN FLANGE.  MATERIAL SPILLED WAS A COUPLE OF HUNDRED GALLONS OF JP-4 JET FUEL. BURIED PIPELINE ONE-TIME INCIDENT.  DISTILLATE LEAKED WHILE TRAVELING TO REMOTE FACILITY.  8 INCH TO 4 INCH LINE.

name: Dumping in Salt Lake City Storm Drain
incident_summary:
Caller reported a white person with a black teeshirt dumping two buckets of what looked like paint into the storm drain.

Salt Lake City Storm Water personnel and Salt Lake County Health Department personnel have been unable to locate the dump or a storm drain opening at the reported location.

name: Kennecott Utah Cooper - Hydraulic Oil
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a release of 250 gallons of hydraulic fluid inside their MPC building.

A fitting on a hose failed and released the product.  The spill was contained inside the building on the concrete floor.  No floor drains or process drains were impacted and there was no impact to the environment.

An incident number was requested.

name: SLC - Diesel Release at Roper Yard
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 1 gallon diesel fuel from a malfunctioning fueling valve at the UPRR Roper Yard.  Release was contained to the waste-water treatment system on-site.  No soils or waterways were impacted.
title_eventname: SLC - Diesel Release at Roper Yard

name: Price -- Sewer line break
incident_summary: A broken culinary water line caused the collapse of a utility construction trench, breaking an 8-inch sewer line which then discharged sewage into a storm drain that flowed into nearby Mead's Wash.  The discharge continued for an estimated 15 hours. Repairs to the line have been completed.  City Engineer estimates as much as 15,000 gallons were discharged during that time.  SE Utah HD responded and collected samples.

name: Pacific Corp. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a motorist lost control of their car and collided with a pad-mounted transformer.  Accident released 25 gallons of transformer oil into the Ogden River.  Testing was done to determine PCB content of transformer oil.  Release was secured but no information given to how it was secured.

name: Chevron Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Called answering service at 23:02 to report a fuel gas violation; answering service called me at 23:17.  Had upset in their plant, resulting in breakdown and gas fuel spill violation.  Spike was up to over 900 ppm for 15-20 minutes; anything > 160 ppm must be reported as violation.  At 9pm, their 3-hour rolling average was 264 ppm; at 10pm = 275 ppm, at 11pm = 252 ppm.  It takes a while to get the rolling average down. Hourly average is in the normal range at this time, 20-30 ppm.

name: Treated Injection Water - Newfield - Myton
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a release of treated injection water that left the location.  A dry drainage was impacted with water flowing into a stockwatering pond.  

Newfield will flush the drainage and empty and clean the pond.

Sid has contacted DEQ Scott Hacking, UDOGM Richard Powell and BLM Randy Bywater.

Water on west side of building runs down to street near other homes that have been converted to apartments - this runoff displays red & white staining on concrete.

title_eventname: Clearfield -- Burning gasoline and diesel fuel

Free product would be removed with vacuum truck.  Expect to treat soils on-site.  Spill was contained in the tank dike area near the 190 tank.  The release was from a corroded hole in a pipeline use to carry hydrocarbons.         All the material was contained to s small area within the refinery. Free liquids were vacuumed up and recycled through the refinery.

The water came to the surface of the ground, ran down an culvert and entered a dry drainage.  The total path of the leak is 10,175 feet.

No water bodies are threatened.

Driver deployed a boom and absorbents.  Lincoln Environmental was called to respond.  Personnel do not believe there have been any impacts to surface water or storm drains at this time.

Volume of diesel release is estimated at 50 gallons to soil.  No impact to waterways or sewers.  Crew is en-route with a backhoe to perform cleanup.   Plan to deliver contaminated soil to Point East facility to be recycyled with asphalt.

They also indicated they called Tri CHD last week about it, and reported it two years ago.

Staker Parsons is requesting assistance finding a contractor to pull the tank. Contact is Brian Jorgensen (801) 648-5483.

name: Steelco (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports an employee of Steelco was filling a portable propane tank when the valve broke releasing 200 gallons to the soil and unlined ditch (five feet from the spill).  The ditch had water in it, and  is possibly a closed system (an investigation of the ditch found no outlet).  The area is industrial and all persons were evacuated.  The SLC incident command post was established with the FD Station No. 6 Hazmat team with the lead (Paul Poulson) assisted by the SLVHD.  PID readings detected the LEL was near 100 percent.  Air temperatures were low and the spill continued to off gas.  By 03:00 the vapor level readings were near 10 percent.

name: UST release in Huntington
incident_summary: Stewart Beling with the consulting firm Antea Group is reporting a release from UST facility 5000401. A PID gave a reading of 3,000 ppm in soil collected using a Geoprobe from the soil/groundwater interface. Samples of soil and groundwater have been submitted to Pace National Laboratory. Results should come back next week.

name: Kennecott - Oil release from Concentrator
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of 25-100 gallons of oil released from an unsecured oil screw at the Kennecott Copperton Concentrator. Oil released to a sump on-site and was recovered in the process stream (flotation ponds). Release did not impact the environment.

name: Unknown Tenant (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a landlord found a tenant dead in his apartment.  It appears tenant may have been growing fungus to collect spores for sythesizing LSD.  Caller is asking if UDEQ has the equipment to provide monitoring for spores.  DERR Duty Officer advised that the UDEQ does not have that monitoring capability.

name: Emery - I-70 Semi-truck accident
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a semi-truck carrying a load of almond milk crashed over the the side of the Eagle Canyon Bridge and into the canyon below.  Incident resulted in the release of 150 gallons of diesel fuel, mixed oil, and antifreezes from the damaged semi-truck. BLM was reportedly on-scene following the crash. No water was reported in the canyon at the time of crash. One fatality was reported as a result of the crash.  STTI (Grand Junction, Colorado) is the contractor for incident clean-up and is en-route to the scene.

Alternate contact  for STTI is Blaine Garwood (970) 243-1642.

name: 80 gallon diesel spill in Erda
incident_summary: The autostop on a fueling truck failed causing the release of about 60-80 gallons of diesel fuel to a church parking lot. The parking lot was under construction. The impacted soil will be excavated.

name: HVH Transportation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller (Bill Rynes, WMHD) reports that a semi-truck, hauling 17 pallets of new car batteries, hit the guard  rail at MM 110.9, eastbound on I -84.  The truck caught fire, the tractor, trailer, and freight were consumed by the fire.  The driving team (and pet dog) escaped.  The load of batteries released battery acid (H2SO4) to the fire control waste water.  Lincoln Environmental mitigated and remediated.  The water was neutralized with soda ash and the waste water was strained to take out residue material.  WMHD gave okay to release the treated water to the Weber River.

The Trucking company will submit an event report via fax or E-mail to DERR and this will be added to file and copies forwarded to recipients directly involved.

name: Union Pacific Railroad (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that approximately 15-20 gallons of diesel fuel was released onto a truck flatbed and a dirt parking lot from a rail heater when a fuel hose disconnected.  No waterways were impacted by the release.  An environmental contractor for UPRR has been notified to clean up the contaminated soil.

name: Safety Clean (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: About 33 gallons of paint was spilled from a 55 gallon drum. The paint was spilled into secondary containment and is being cleaned up.

name: Spiral Jetty Oil Seep
incident_summary: Caller is reporting that over the weekend they were out at the Spiral Jetty and walking their dog along the shore and down to the boat ramp and pier. They discovered when they were done that tar had gotten all over the dog's paws and legs. Caller is reporting that they attempted to contact authorities but had no luck.

name: Hill AFB - Petroleum in soils
incident_summary: Caller reported that petroleum contaminated soils were first identified at a construction site on base in December 2019. The contamination was initially believed to associated with a nearby underground storage tank (UST) site. Further excavation at the construction site identified two additional areas of stained soils upgradient of the UST site. The source of the petroleum is now believed to be associated with above ground piping in the area. Approximately 400 cubic yards of contaminated soils are staged on-site on an impermeable barrier with storm water controls. Quantity of petroleum released is unknown.

name: Springville - Ammonia Release
incident_summary: This incident was reported to the DEQ via an email from the NRC.  Caller is reporting a leak from a freezer that resulted in a release of anhydrous ammonia to the air.  Amount released is unknown at this time.  The release has been secured.

name: FedEx Ground (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller is reporting that the highway was closed for 6 hours when FedEx truck had head-on collision and fire.  Police, Fire & EMS responded.  Truck was carrying ammunition which went off during the fire.

incident_summary: Caller notified DERR duty officer of a release of SO2 (sulfur dioxide) through the flare stack as a result of a planned unit shut down for maintenance.  Amount of  SO2   being released is 125 – 150 pounds per hour.  The ongoing release of  SO2 will continue until about April 28th when the maintenance will be completed.

Caller wished to remain annonymous and did not leave a number or give the operations name. The RP comes up at the address on the map.

upomn calling Davis County Health, they have had at least one call similar to this in their area today, and they directed the report to the same officer as the previous report.

name: Duchesne Co - Crude Oil - 60 bbls

A secondary containment has been put in place and a pump truck attempted to remove crude but not successful.  Owner is enroute to determine best way to clean up spill and remove cracked pup.  DEQ District Engineer inspected site.  Estimated volume of release is 60 barrels (75-80 barrels being hauled in the pup).   Response crew constructed secondary berm containment to capture the release.

name: Salt Lake Co - Sewage Release
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a release of raw sewage that occurred yesterday.  Contractor ruptured a sewage line that passes from the tailings impoundment offices to the treatment plant near the refinery.  Location is about 1/2 mile northwest of intersection between SR-201 and SR-202.  Estimated volume is less than 500 gallons.  All sewage remained within the trench. There is no impact to storm lines or surface waters.  Site of construction work is within a wetland area.  All requisite permits are in place.  Crews responded to neutralize the material with sodium hypochlorite.  They pumped and transported the waste to a KUC on-site sewage treatment plant.

name: North Ogden -- White stains in creek
incident_summary:
Reporting Party observed the water in Coldwater Creek next to his house was cloudy and had a gray-white color.  He said he collected samples and took pictures of the discharge.  Creek is running clear today but still has some white residue on the banks and vegetation.

Reporting Party said North Ogden PD was notified; responding officers were unable to find the source of the discharge.

North Ogden Storm Water was notified; employee was not able to find the source.
title_eventname: North Ogden -- White stains in creek

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: DFCM personnel informed DEQ that a pickup truck parked at the Utah State Tax Commission building on the south side lot of the front entrance.  DEQ dispatched to the Tax Commission Building.  The vehicle leaked diesel fuel which was held in a truck-bed tank that typically sites atop the side rails of the bed of the pickup immediately behind the rear window.  DFCM had been informed by the driver that he had just topped off the tank.  The driver parked in a spot which is inclined causing the fuel to spill out from the tank filler into the bed of the truck and then flowed out to the asphalt.  The parking stall is directly upgradient from a storm drain in the parking lot.  DFCM personnel, whom estimated the release at 2 quarts, dispatched a petroleum-only absorbant material (Mantek Spillmate) onto the fuel.  There was no direct impact to the storm sewer as the sorbent was placed before any of the fuel reached the storm grate.

name: Tooele Co - Benzine Sulfide
incident_summary: During transfer/consolidation of loads for final delivery, crew discovered material from a leaking drum.  Drum was on a pallet and material was observed beneath.  Leak was contained to the truck.  The crew repacked the drum and all materials used to clean it into an overpack drum.  Material was then delivered to it's final destination for disposal.  Material is benzene sulfide (AN 3077, Hazardous Waste Solid; class 9, Group 3) Estimated volume is 1/2 quart.

LHD is onsite.  Cleanup is almost complete.  FD will contain into over-pack barrels pre-staged on site by PRP.  PRP will coordinate final disposal of wastes.   With obsrevation of crack in concrete dispenser island, LHD believes potential exists for impact to groundwater.  Facility will monitor groundwater with existing on-site monitor wells.  Caller advised PRP of need to make notification, DEQ may anticipate call.

UPDATE 5/7/09 14:16:  Kathy Clements (Flying J - (801) 296-7717) notified the DEQ on behalf of the responsible party.

name: Newfield Water release
incident_summary: Caller is reporting that there was a release from an injection line near the GBU 13-27-8-17 injection well. ~70 bbls of the treated water left the site and went down a dry drainage. Workers were able to berm the drainage and recover ~55bbls of the water. Line was secured and the drainage will be flushed with approximately 250 bbls of fresh water which will be recovered. Soils samples to be collected next week for submittion to LHD.

name: Jay Brazier Auto Auction (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported the illegal dumping of paint thinner and paint waste into the facility's drainage system which leads to the city's storm water system.  Caller stated this was the second time this company has dumped waste through the storm water system.

name: Duchesne Co. - Two injection water spills
incident_summary: Caller reported two injection water spills into dry drainage ditches that occurred yesterday.  The first spill was 50 barrels at 6 a.m. and the second spill was 5 barrels at 7 a.m.  These occurred south of Myton about 3/4-miles apart from one another.  Caller said they will flush the impacted area with clean water and then sample the area for lab analysis.  GPS coordinates that caller provided did not provide a valid location on map; therefore, location on map is approximate.
title_eventname: Duchesne Co. - Two injection water spills

name: Brown liquid from treatment plant
incident_summary: Caller reports that the little Cottonwood water treatment plant is releasing a thick brown liquid into the Willow Creek golf course pond (which is now dry).  The caller reports that she previously called the treatment plant when this occurred and was told that they were unaware of the release and would determine how to prevent future releases.

name: Chevron-Texaco Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller notified DERR duty officer of a release of petroleum product (Jet fuel) to cooling system water as a result of a small leak in tubing inside heat exchanger.  The exchanger repairs are scheduled to start at 04:30.

incident_summary:

name: Breakdown at Chevron
incident_summary: A power outage resulted in the release of an estimated 2,000 pounds of sulfur dioxide and greater than 100 pounds of hydrogen sulfide to the flare. The release is ongoing. No off-site effects are anticipated.

name: Tri County - Production water release
incident_summary: Caller reported a 30 barrel spill consisting of 5 barrels of oil and 25 barrels of produced water.  This occurred at the RW13-24B redwash field location.  The spill was fully contained and did not leave the location.  Caller said there was a crack in the well.  The well has been watched and will be repaired.  Only surface soils were impacted; no waterways.  Clean-up is underway.

name: Corrosion Inhibitor Spill
incident_summary: About 330 gallons of a corrosion inhibitor was spilled when a tote was broken.  The material is 30 percent methanol and was discharged into a tributary of the White River near Seven Sisters Road 0.5 miles south of Fiddler Road.  The district health department has been notified.  Their spill report with the MSDS of the material are attached.   The location map has been corrected and verified.  Coordiantes given are 40.01996, -109.38436.

name: Amoco (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Sulfur Recovery Unit malfunctioned releasing 1000 pounds of Sulfur Dioxide to the atmosphere.

name: Duchesne County Gycol Leak
incident_summary:
The caller reported a leak of approximately 83 gallons of glycol to the soil at a remote wellhead.  No water bodies were threatened or impacted by the leak.  At the time of the call the leak was contained and isolated.

The wellhead is UTE FEE 2-20C5, API 43-013-30550.

The latitude and longitude coordinates provided by the caller were incorrect.  The UTM coordinates listed above were obtained by looking up the wellhead on the UDOGM website.

name: GenPack (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that an electrical power outage hit the plant (maker of styrofoam products) caused the production line to shut down.  Start up problems persisted through the night.  With no power the “thermal oxidizer” unit released an unknown amount of isopentane gas.  Repairs were completed and the production unit and air pollution control unit were brought back on line.

name: Taylor Contracting (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Leak in the fuel tank of one of their trucks released from 20-50 gallons of diesel fuel.  Some of the fuel may have gone into a ditch which leads to Farmington Bay.  They have placed booms at several points down the ditch and have notified the Farmington Bay Bird Refuge and Davis County Health.  They have not found evidence of diesel fuel in the refuge.  The impacted soil will be excavated and taken to ET Technologies.

name: Anhydrous ammonia release,  Nestle Springville
incident_summary: Caller stated due to a hole in a suction pipe at the facility there  was a release of anhydrous ammonia.

name: Diesel Spill in Echo Creek Near Echo
incident_summary: A pickup truck carrying a trailer swerved and hit a semitruck causing it to hit a side rail and rupture a saddle tank, releasing about 100 gallons of diesel fuel. An unknown amount of fuel entered Echo Creek. The local hazmat team placed six booms into the creek to contain the spill. Lincoln Environmental is responding today to clean up the remaining fuel.
title_eventname: Diesel Spill in Echo Creek Near Echo

name: SLC - 1 gallon Pesticide
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 1 gallon of Dichlorvos (Toxic Pesticide).  Quantity exceeded the RQ.  Release was discovered when 3 shipping boxes were found wet inside the trailer of a semi-truck.  Lincoln Environmental was contracted for clean-up.  Release is contained to inside the trailer.

name: Farmington - Diesel Release from Semi-Truck
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a semi-truck was traveling along I-15 when it went off the road through a fence and into the railway right-of-way  The semi-truck clipped a train causing a roll-over and the release of approximately 50 gallons of diesel fuel to the soils and road ballast.  Incident caused delays of 1 hour along the rail line.

All information for this report from National Response Center Incident Report #1222879

name: Small release of polymeric beads expandable in SLC
incident_summary: Caller reported a five-gallon release of UN2211 (polymeric beads expandable) to the interior of a trailer.  He said that this hazardous substance is highly flammable.  It was completely contained inside the trailer and did not impact any waterways.  A clean-up contractor has been called.  Caller said absorbents will be used.
title_eventname: Small release of polymeric beads expandable in SLC

name: Not Reported (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Crews have uncovered an underground storage tank located at 471 West 500 South under a building.  The tank contains about 2000 gallons of liquid.  Field test indicate that the material has a flash point of under 140 degrees.  The material has not been fully characterized.  About 100 gallons of the liquid spilled during the excavation.  The spilled material has been contained and drumed.

name: Diesel Spill - Orem
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a spill of diesel from a saddle tank at the Foundation Building Materials yard when the tank caught the gate rail and split open.  The product generally flowed back into the private property with some in the street and gutter.  

Impacts are to asphalt and soils on the edge of the yard.  Clean Harbors responded and cleaned up the spill.  Asphalt was pressure washed and impacted soils at the edge were excavated.

The responsible party did not call last week, thinking Clean Harbors would call in the incident for them.  They were just calling today to check if the spill had been reported?

name: Chevron Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Exceedance of UPDS permit 7 day average BOD concentration limit.  Value was 48 ppm; 35 is their concentration limit.  They know cause, which was disruption in their waste water treatment system, which has been fixed.   Written report will follow within 5 days to Don Ostler - DWQ.

name: Brenntag West (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Driver was prepared to unload a 300 gallon tote containing a 12.5% solution of sodium hypochlorite when the tote slipped off the back of the truck breaking the container.  300 gallons total material was released (375 pounds of sodium hypochlorite by weight).  Driver was able to contain the spill with soda ash to the asphalt parking lot where spill occurred.  Clean up crews are en-route to the spill.  Mark Williams @ Davis County Health Department has responded to scene.

name: Sulfuric Acid Spill - Skull Valley
incident_summary:
THE CALLER IS REPORTING THAT A DRAIN LINE VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN DURING
  LOADING AND RELEASED SULFURIC ACID ON CONCRETE AND SOIL. THE MATERIAL IS
  CONTAINED INSIDE THE PLANT.

The impacts are contained to the operational unit and no water impacted.  Standing acid was pumped into containers and a bicarbonate neutralizer has been applied and more limestone will be applied.  No injuries were reported and no damage to equipment.  

Caller will report to Tooele County LEPC whose director is the local health dept director.

name: Uintah - Dumping Limestone

Caller States that trucks are hauling processed limestone and spilled powdered limestone all over the road near the intersection of HWY 191 and Diamond Mountain Road. Caller states that in some places it is two inches thick and 100 yards long and they are concerned that the powder will get or already had gotten into a waterway. The caller states that it has been there for a few weeks.

NRC# 1199663

name: Ed Crapo (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Resident rinsed remaining paint from a used paint bucket (bucket was less than half full) onto the street. The diluted paint ran down the street entered a storm drain that crossed the street and daylighted on the other side.  Bountiful City and Davis County Health Department responded and cleaned up the diluted paint with a mop.

name: Caolville Diesel Release
incident_summary: A truck jack-knifed on I-80 between milemarker 169 - 170 and spilled 7-8 gallons of diesel in the median.  Four bags of kitty litter were spread to absorb diesel.  Lincoln Environmental was contacted and will be responding to incident.  The caller reported that no storm drain or waterway was affected.

name: Amoco Oil (Null RP Substituted)

Soils will be excavated and recycled.             The diesel fuel was contained to a small area within the refinery.  All free liquids were recovered using a vacuum truck.

The caller initially reported that the spill occurred between midnight and 4 AM but called back and updated the information.

name: SLC-
incident_summary:
Caller reported 20 gallons of mercury was dumped into a storm drain.

All information for this report was transcribed from the federal National Response Center Incident Report #1106918.

UPDATE 1/29/2015:  Salt Lake County Health Department (SLCoHD) was in contact with the Reporting Party.  The Reporting Party provided a detailed report to SLCoHD and produced a jar of mercury reportedly taken from the facility.  Based on the available information, the SLCoHD investigated the facility on 1/30/2015.  The SLCoHD investigation found other containers of mercury at the facility but no evidence of dumping to the storm drains or that the containers had released to the environment.  The containers were removed from the facility.  Contact for this report at the SLCoHD is Ron Lund.

The caller stated that the acid was being neutralized and the spilled material cleaned up.

No waterways or drains were threatened.

LHD will check in the morning that it has been cleaned up and will follow up from there.

name: Wellington - Diesel Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported that while refilling a group of ASTs at the Savage Trucking facility, a cap blew off the fuel delivery truck releasing between 50-300 gallons of diesel to the surrounding soils.  Released diesel was  initially contained with sands and by burning.  STTI is sending personnel to assist Savage Trucking with the excavation and disposal of contaminated soils.  Savage Trucking will do the excavation work and soils will be disposed of at ECDC.  No storm drains or surface waters were impacted.

name: Bill Barrett Corporation (Null RP Substituted)
address: Southwest of the intersection of Dry Canyon Rd and Nine Mile Canyon Road
address_location: Southwest of the intersection of Dry Canyon Rd and Nine Mile Canyon Road
incident_summary:
David Hackford with DOGM first called Scott Hacking to report the event. Initial Reports are that there was an explosion ot the Dry canyon compressor Station in Nine Mile Canyon. Cause unknown. Released amounts unknown. Emergencty personel are in route responding. DWQ has started preperations to obtain water samples when access to the canyon is restored. Scott Hacking and David Arrotti are waiting to respond to the site.
DDW has been notified, and they have notified the down stream drinking water plants.
Update 15:00 11/20/2012
A preliinary site visit by Scott and Dave was unable to veryfy any release. Company representatives (Jeff Strigham) indicated there had not been anything yet. They recommend that a return visit be done on Wednessday if access is resoterd, and that confirmation of any release be gatherd prior to any sampleing being done. Fire is mostly contained at this time.
BBCorp update by Scott Donato,
Fire occurred at Dry Cyn compressor station in Nine Mile area at approx. 830am today 111912. Cause is unknown.  Two BBC employees burned and flown to SLC burn unit.  Injuries are not thought to be life threatening at this time.  No other injuries known. Field has been all shut in as far as we know. Tanks remain burning and some remaining small fires onsite.  Fire Dept is onsite.  BLM is assessing fires offsite. No spills or releases observed either.  We will ensure no runoff to creek as soon as we can get onsite.

name: Weber River Wetlands
incident_summary: Asphalt resurfacing company had parked truck.  Valve leaked contents that flowed about 300 yards along gutter and entered a storm drain (vehicle departed scene w/o of spill).  The drain empties into wetland that flows through pipe into a second wetland that empties into the Weber River.  100-200 yards of the first wetland are impacted.  Investigators have not yet determined how far the material has traveled.  South Ogden Fire Dept is on-scene and deploying booms, etc.  Lincoln Environmental is en-route.  Volume released has not yet been determined.

No surface water or storm drains were impacted by the release.

name: US MAG - Acidic water release
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a leak of acidic water under the dike of their wastewater pond.  The leak was discovered this morning, but likely occurred over the weekend.

The release is being contained by the natural high topography and is not impacting any waterways and no injuries.

The leak will be plugged and the material will be returned to the pond.  Impacted soils will be remediated.

They will notify DWQ under a groundwater permit requirement.

The map location is approximate with given address or 15 miles north of Exit 77.

name: Metropolitan Water District (Null RP Substituted)

address_location: Terminal Reservoir at 3300 South I 215 junction

They have placed BMPs along the construction site and he reports that overflow water is draining into Parley's Creek.  The incident  occurred today and he stated that they are implementing chlorine removal measures.  13:10 notified Stan Miller that he should also contact the NRC and provided the phone number.  15:19 received incident report #1001260 from NRC for this incident.  I contacted John Whitehead at DWQ to verify he received the phone message and DWQ has responded to this incident.  The repair for the reservoir will require it to be fully drained thus corrective action will take place over the next several days.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)

Caller said it looked like a car had lost an entire amount of antifreeze.  Caller would like to know the associated hazards.  Caller notified the grocery store but saw no action taken to mitigate.  Caller mentioned first hand knowledge of having a pet die from consuming anti-freeze - "dog took one lick and it killed it."  Caller did not know if any storm sewers were nearby.

name: Murray - Fuel Spill In Parking Lot
incident_summary: Leaks were identified from the fuel tanks of two vehicles, one carrying gasoline and the other carrying diesel.  Fuel leaked from both vehicles onto the parking lot.  It is estimated that 10-20 gallons of gasoline and approximately 10 gallons of diesel fuel entered the storm drain in the parking lot.  Murray City public works has pumped the primary affected storm drain.  The next drain down the line was inspected, but no fuel was found.  After pumping the primary drain, the line was rinsed and pumped at the second drain.  Cleanup appears to be complete.
title_eventname: Murray - Fuel Spill In Parking Lot

name: Washington County - Former Shooting Range

The property is currently being developed with site materials processed for fill material.  There is a concern that potentially impacted materials are being transported into the air and surrounding areas.

address: 3.5 Miles S of Exit 49, I-80 W
address_location: 3.5 Miles S of Exit 49, I-80 W
incident_summary:

A total of 3 gallons of liquid was recovered inside the trailer and no material hit the ground or escaped the trailer.  

The field service group from Tooele remediated the trailer and repackaged the compromised container.  

The contamination is listed as NA3077 - Hazardous Waste Solid - Class 9 - Packing Group 3 and the manifest does not list any specific compounds.
title_eventname: Clean Harbors - Haz Liquid Spill - Tooele Co

name: Salt Lake City -- Fuel spill and fire
incident_summary: A truck hauling an estimated 8,400 gallons of gasoline and diesel fuel was involved in a crash, causing a release of fuel from the trailer tanks and a large fire which caused damage to the road and shut down the freeway.  An unknown amount of fuel flowed into the soils on the sides of the road and contaminated several storm drains.  No sheen has been noted on nearby drainage ponds to the south and east. title_eventname: Salt Lake City -- Fuel spill and fire

name: Chevron Refinery (Null RP Substituted)

No reportable quantity releases at this time.  Chevron has commenced the process of taking the reformer plant off-line, and they estimate it will be down by 15:00 today.  Chevron anticipates the shutown will extend for 8 hours.

Company inspection includes pulling a portion of the line out after installation.  While pulling the line, a petroleum product was released from the hole.  No oil or other petroleum product is used as part of the installation; it is unknown where the product originated. The POC inspected the site today and found no oil staining and no VOC detection on his PID.  The petroleum product may have affected the 3' deep trench that was dug for the installation, but it is not suspected to have entered the storm drains.  A contractor has been contacted for investigate and cleanup if necessary, but the source and volume are still unknown.

name: Fruit Heights Mercury Thermometer
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a mercury thermometer broke inside the home at the base of the stairs.  She stated she cleaned up the mercury on the tile floor according to online guidance, however tiny shards of glass were found on the carpet creating concern that it may be contaminated with mercury.  UDEQ notified Davis County Health Department to discuss the situation and the need for mercury monitoring with the Lumex meter.

Met with Davis County at the residence to screen the interior for mercury.  Breathing zone concentrations were below EPA action level of 1000 ng/m3 (between 80 (at entrance) -350 nanograms/cubic meter -ng/m3 (above contamianted carpet).  However concentrations in the carpet were elevated (between  2,500-3,500 ng/m3).  Tien Nguyen (EPA/OSC) was contacted to provide assessment of the mercury concentrations.  Tien stated that the amount of mercury in the carpet was not enough to initiate a response and that homeowner be advised that removal/replacement of carpet is the best remedial alternative.  Homeowner was advised of EPA recommendation.  Homeowner elected to heat/ventilate the home to try to bring down concetrations.  Homeowner was advised to not vacuum and not enter the room until further evaluation.  UDEQ and Davis County will coordinate follow-up.

UPDATE 5/16/13 13:10:  DERR returned to the residence with the Davis County Health Department to evlauate mercury levels.  Levels detected near the carpet surface continued to indicate the presence of mercury at approximately 2,500 ng/m3.  Highest level detected was 6,000 ng/m3.  Breathing zone concentrations for children were below action level at around 500 ng/m3.  Mercury persists in the carpet.  Homeowner was advised at this time that removal/replacemnet of the carpet is the best remedial alternative.

UPDATE 2 6/19/13 10:38:  DERR arrived on-site at 09:10 to meter the home.  Homeowner had sought advice from an environmental company (Envirocare) regarding remediating mercury in carpets.  DERR discussed cleanup details with homeowner and  ran initial test on mercury meter and waited for DCHD (Kell Platero) to arrive before entering the home.   Formerly contaminated areas in the carpet monitored clean.  Low detections (~450 ng/m3) of mercury were detected in a few areas of the carpet.  Higher detections (~1800 -  2000 ng/m3) were detected in the crease between carpet and tile floors.  As this area may be difficult to clean further, homeowner was advised to refrain from vacuuming near this area for the time being.  Hoem declared clean by DERR and DCHD.

name: Thatcher Chemical Co. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Due to over-tightening the valve on top of a chlorine cylinder, the valve came loose causing a release of 35 pounds of liquid chlorine onto the ground (RQ for Cl = 10 lbs.).

Response: Thatcher employees put on their PPE and entered the facility.  They stopped the leak, and used scrubbers to neutralize the chlorine (with caustic soda).  The facility is back to normal now.  The spill was contained within a building and no chlorine reached any storm drain.

UPDATE 4/16/07 22:30: Brian Bennion (SLVHD) received a call from Salt Lake City Fire Dept. regarding a chlorine release from the Thatcher Chemical Company.  Initial report was that 20 lbs. of chlorine had been released from a 150 lb cylinder inside a building and that the release had been sufficiently contained.  A follow-up call from the SLCFD came at 11:00 stating that the situation had worsened and that chlorine was still releasing from the facility.  DERR contacted the SLCFD for further information.  Detections for chlorine were at 1.5 ppm at a distance of 75 feet from the building.  Winds were only at a slight breeze.  An Entry Team was sent into the building to investigate.  Entry Team found the release coming from a 400 gallon canister of chlorine inside the building and the air scrubbers not working properly.  The caustic soda used in the scrubbers was refilled but the scrubbers still did not appear to operate.  Entry team left the area after instruments had become saturated but did report the chlorine had stopped releasing from the container and the chlorine concentrations appeared to have tapered off.  Fire Dept. was in the process of getting new instruments to the scene and sending the Entry team back to conduct clearance monitoring.  On-scene contact was Ed Demano (SLCFD HazMat 6) cell: (801) 550-0121 station: (801)596-5246.  No injuries were reported.

via the NRC report:  While cleaning outside of a residence an individual discovered what seemed to be mercury on the sidewalk.  The source is undetermined at this time.  Tests done by the public safety department confirm the material is mercury.
Update from DERR:  The Battalion Chief, Hugh Conner (801-369-0146), reports that the spill was caused by a broken thermometer, which was apparently dropped onto the sidewalk.  There were many people in the area from a nearby church who were cleaning the residence of a deceased person.  Several children walked through the spill area and went into the church.  One child touched the mercury with his hands.  The FD has secured the area.  The Poison Control office was called and under their direction the FD decontaminated the children with soap and water.  The children were sent home.  The FD kept the shoes of the children on scene for further analysis.  A contractor, TW Company, has been called to complete further testing and remediation of the spill.  The EPA has called concerning this spill and offered assistance.   At this time the Battalion Chief is not requesting additional assistance.  DERR contacted TW Company and forwarded contact information of the EPA.                      2nd update: 08/19/04, 15:07, there is a second NRC Report #732388 for the same spill.  The callers name is Barbara Moosman, 801-224-1959, 4 oz. Mercury spilled from a glass jar while cleaning out the garage.

Paul Washburn indicated he would call the number he has for DEQ and report it tot he SLC office also.  The number he had is 801-536-4408, not sure who that is. Paul Washburn's phone number is 979-5920.
John Chartier is going to call the UDOT project manager for the work that is going on up there right now and get him involved and see if he can get someone down there tomorrow to clean it out.

incident_summary: #34 W. 1300 South Car Wash has excavated sump and spread along fence.  2-3 feet wide, 6-8 inches deep. Soaking into ground.  Is in Salt Lake City.

name: SLC - Release of resin solution
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a forklift punctured a 55-gallon drum inside a trailer releasing approximately 20 gallons of UN1866 (resin solution). Caller stated that 10-15 gallons were contained inside the trailer and that 2-3 gallons released to the concrete with an unknown amount entering a nearby storm drain. Lincoln Environmental (Lincoln) was contracted to clean-up the release. Absorbant material was used to contain the release inside the trailer and on the concrete. Lincoln observed a sheen on the water at the bottom of the storm drain box with a visible trail down the sides of the storm drain. Lincoln determined that one ounce of the resin solution entered into the drain. 

Contact for Lincoln Environmental is Rusty Grover (801) 589-1400.

Rough estimate as to amount is ~5 gallons.

name: Mark's Trans Service (Null RP Substituted)

The Bear River District Health Department is providing cleanup oversight.  A Google Earth placemark is attached.

name: The Kellog Co. - Process Water Relese
incident_summary:
Caller reported approximately 15,000 gallons of treated process wastewater from the on-site pre-treatment plant was discharged to the surplus canal and Great Salt Lake.  No hazardous materials and no sanitary waste was released.  

A power bump at approximately 8:40 PM caused the treatment system to go down.  The system automatically resets, but at 9:40 PM they had a high level alarm.  By 1:00 AM a plant operator discovered the air compressor that keeps the actuator valve open had failed.  The air compressor was restarted and the plant is functioning properly. 

The Kellog Co discharge permit is #UTR258375, SIC Code 2038.

The caller did not report to the NRC.  I notified Matt Garn in DWQ and Matt will follow up the RP.

MPA Corrected the contact information for Davis County Health Dept.  Dave Spence is the correct contact.
title_eventname: The Kellog Co. - Process Water Relese

Further root cause analysis determined that 280-gallons of the 5K gallon spill went into the storm drain on their property/campus which resulted in a direct discharge to the Jordan Riverl.  DEQ. DWQ, DWMRC, SLC Public Works were not notified of the release on the day of.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
While a farmer was burning his field on the afternoon of 4/3/02 in Pleasant Grove, the fire got away from him and burned a neighbor’s barn at the incident address.  The Pleasant Grove Fire Department responded to the fire and tried to extinguish it.  A large plume from the fire hung low and moved south southeast toward the Provo area, and against the Wasatch Front.  When the fire was nearly out, the owner of the barn came forward and said he had stored 25 four foot tall by three foot wide pre-1950's transformers in the barn.  It is not known exactly what damage the fire did to the transformers.  A UHP Hazmat Team and the personnel from the Utah County Health Department will conduct an inspection of the site on 4/4/02 at 10 a.m.  Some of the firemen believed they had been exposed to the smoke and the fire department was going to write up a report on the incident.  The nearest residence to the barn was 2000 feet away.

13:30 Update - U.S. EPA contacted DEQ to determine if DEQ had been notified.  Once piece of add'l info per EPA: the Plume migrated over a nearby school.

14:22 Update - After conversation between UDEQ DSHW and Utah County Health Dept, today about the presence of PCB transformers (25 in number) and that it looks like they may have been breached by the fire, EPA R8 TOSCA rep. was contacted by DSHW.  TOSCA was concerned about the potential for dioxins to have formed from hot fire and will be passing on the event information to the Region's Response Team.  DERR requested that the EPA contact us first so that we can coordinated our efforts and resources.

name: Orem - Chlorine Odor
incident_summary:

name: Ogden Fish Kill
incident_summary:
Chris Penne from the Division of Wildlife Resources (DWR) called this morning to report a fish kill on the 21st Street Pond (also called Goode Ski Lake). The report came in to DWR yesterday, March 14th, that there were dead fish on the south shore of the pond. Species included young of year gizzard shad (5" size) and rainbow trout that were stocked last fall (approximately 9-10" in size). Chris said that it isn't unusual to lose gizzard shad at this time of year because they don't tolerate the cold well, but it is unusual to have difficulties with trout. Chris also stated that the trout appeared to be trying to get oxygen, and that since there is no ice on the pond a low dissolved oxygen condition would be unexpected. 

The pond had a history of contamination with PCBs; however, remediation was completed at the site over 5 years ago and is inspected regularly by Ogden City, DERR, and EPA. There are no tributaries to the pond other than the Ogden River.

The contact person at DWR is Chris Penne: 801.656.8694.

address: 245 East 1100 North NW1/4 of SE1/4 Sect 11 T1N R1W
address_location: 245 East 1100 North NW1/4 of SE1/4 Sect 11 T1N R1W
incident_summary:
Conoco operates the facility on Chevron property.  Release initially discovered at 14:45.  Failure of an O-ring on a pipeline scrapper trap caused release of 3 to 5 barrels of high-sulfur diesel.  Stained soils were excavated, but excavation started filling in with ground water.  They brought in VAC trucks to recover the water and product.  Excavated ~7 yds of soil.  Will sample and then dispose off-site.

Update July 8, 99 15:30 Chevron called to be sure we had been notified.  Volume of the release compared to the initial report is significantly larger and estimated to be between 150 to 200 barrels.  Chevron has determined that this release likely began on July 1, 1999 when the scrapper trap was serviced.  It is Chevron's belief that damage to an O-ring seal on the trap occurred at this time.  Crews currently have an excavation with dimensions of 8 x 11 feet.  Currently crews are VACing product off the water table.

Update 26-July-00  Per letter received on this date, the revised estimated release amount is 10 to 15 barrels.  Investigation work is on-going.  A follow-up report will be submitted to DERR and DWQ upon completion.

On 11/9/16, SITLA was notified of a large spill on its property by a neighbor in Cedar Fort, Utah.  Pictures were provided.    
On 11/14/16, Sonja Wallace and Special Agent Ron Barton (AGs office) went out to inspect. Sonja took samples of what appears to be concrete slurry.  Sampled for RCRA 8 metals, VOC, DRO and PH.  All samples can back clean except for PH which was measured at 11.7.  
It is estimated (by lessee) that about 2 million gallons of concrete slurry has been disposed of by lessee on the property. This was not approved by SITLA.  Berms were built by the lessee to hold the slurry on-site.  However, 2 slurry berms broke and some of the slurry left the site. and traveled approx. 1/4 mile down a 2 track dirt road.  Adjacent to the two track is a dry ditch.  It appears that no material has gotten into the ditch.
title_eventname: Utah County -- Concrete dumping on state land

name: Chevron (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Approximately 13:00 VRU machine went down.  It has not yet been restored on-line.  Don't need call back til Monday.  over on SR-40 near the 52nd mile marker, approximately 1 mile west of Current Creek.  Both tanks
 exploded and caught fire resulting in a brush fire covering approximately 5,000 sq. feet.  

 By request of UHP dispatch DEQ was notified at 1:30 AM.

 Rick Carlile, UHP Hazmat trooper was contacted at the scene by the ERO. After Trooper Carlile had
 an opportunity to access the incident he determined that all of the remaining product carried by the
 truck burned before it could get into the soil or a nearby stream and the incident had been handled by
 the local fire department, police and EMT's.

 The driver, a Mr. Scott Broadhead was taken to the Uinta Basin Medical Center where according to
 the ER nurse he was released shortly thereafter with only minor injuries.

 DEQ was notified of the progress at 2:38 AM.

 National Park Service Glen Canyon Recreation Area dispatched vessel w/three park rangers that are on-scene.  Leak has stopped.  Amount unknown.  

Location: Last Chance Bay 
@ Lat 37.1075062, Lon 111.2772425.

name: Salt Lake Co - Waste Water
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a spill of waste water from tank.  Material is effluent from process sewer system.  Contains hydrocarbons, light ends and heavy ends and solids.  Facility stated the material spilled contains heavy ends and some solids.  Cause and volume are being investigated.  the release was all contained in secondary earthen containment.

incident_summary: SULFURIC ACID LEAK FROM PIPE ONTO THE GROUND. SULFURIC ACID: ESTIMATED ABOUT 240 GALLONS. INTERNAL CORROSION OF AN ELBOW IN PIPING ASSOCIATED WITH THE TRANSFERRING OF SULFURIC ACID SPILL CONTAINED ON SITE AND NEUTRALIZED WITH SODA ASH AND PROPERLY DISPOSED OF.

name: Not Reported (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Semi-truck went into Weber River off of I-84 at milemarker 108.  Released 400 gallons of diesel into river.  Info via voice msg. From Brian Cowan.             Update:  8/3/98  When they pulled semi-truck out of the Weber River both saddle tanks were intact.  Most fuel was in left (lower) tank.  It was assumed that the fuel flowed via cross-over line into lower tank when it (semi) over turned.  Release came from crank-case oil.  Better estimate is now putting volume at approximately 200 gallons.   Trailer in river created a backeddy in river flow.  Lincoln Environmental was called - they placed booms to capture.  WMHD notified Weber Basin Water District.  They responsed per their ER plan - Brian thinks that likely consists of placing booms upgradient of their intake and monitoring.  Intake is used for irrigation and drinking Water.

name: Frito Lay Inc. - Mr. Larry Perry (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Frito Lay Inc. - Mr. Larry Perry
incident_summary: Ms. Russo spoke w/ UT Trooper Witake.  110 gallons of diesel fuel spilled on Hwy 89.  Rock slid down hill in front of driver during rain storm and he had no choice but to hit rock.  Ruptured saddle tank.  No known injuries.  Frito Lay sent out EnviroTech from Farmington, NM.  No water impacted.  Soil and roadway only.
title_eventname: Frito Lay Inc. - Mr. Larry Perry (Null RP Substituted)

name: Chevron Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: IAF float and sludge oil was released due to a tank breach at the wastewater treatment plant.  The release was confined in the concrete containment pad and was cleaned up.

name: Salt Lake County - Suspected Fish Kill
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of an unknown chemical to a pond that periodically drains to the Big Cottonwood Creek. The chemical was put in the pond to kill algae but it is killing fish, ducks, and turtles. Kids and dogs often play in the vicinity of the pond. The caller has not observed this in the 35 years at the property.
title_eventname: Salt Lake County - Suspected Fish Kill

name: West Valley City - Residence with brown water
incident_summary: Caller reported the water running out of the faucets in his residence turned brown in color. The brown discoloration continued for a while before returning to normal. Caller requested assistance to know if his water was safe to use.
title_eventname: West Valley City - Residence with brown water
