incident_summary: Caller reported that a refrigerated rail car has released diesel fuel at Salt Lake Intermodal Hub.  Exact amount unknown, but rail car holds a maximum of 50 gallons.  Car has been moved from concrete to hazmat area.  Pacific West is in route to remediate spill.
title_eventname: Diesel Spill, Salt Lake Intermodal Hub

name: Uintah County -- Produced Water Spill
incident_summary: Company discovered a 15 barrel discharge of produced water at the WV-31 well site (API# 43-047-15460).  Discharge was contained on site and did not affect any waterways.

name: Weber county - Asphalt Dumping
incident_summary:
The caller reported that Hooper City and Staker Parsons were performing road maintenance near his home. On the incident date, the drum rollers were parked on the parking strip of his property. Workers proceeded to wipe down the drums using sponges and threw them to the ground. Other fluids like hydraulic fluid were also leaked onto his property during this time. The depth of impact is about 2 inches and extends about 2 feet in two areas.

No impact to waterways was reported.

name: Chevron-Texaco Refinery (Enviro Office) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller notified DERR duty officer of a release of benzene, hydrogen sulfide and sulfur dioxide through the flare stack as a result of the loss of two cooling water pumps.  A fuse blew cutting power to the pumps. The fuse has been replaced and system startups are underway.

name: Oil Spray from Rail onto Private Property
incident_summary: Caller notified EPA through the NRC that an oil spill from a Union Pacific engine sprayed all over the sound wall, his property, a swimming pool and some cars.  Union Pacific's cleanup contractor will not tell Mr. Gonzalez what is in the oil and is not cleaning up the oil completely.  EPA is referring the event to DEQ for oversight.  The EPA contact is Thun-Ping Chan 303-884-0437.  Savage Services called at 15:45 to report overpressurization of a railcar resulted in about 3.6 barrels of black wax crude to shoot out the top of the rail car and spray on a residential area.
title_eventname: Oil Spray from Rail onto Private Property

name: Clearfield - Dielectric fluid release
incident_summary: Caller reported a 50-gallon release of dielectric fluid to soil.  No waterways were impacted.  Clean-up has been completed.

name: Stericycle (as assertion) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller alleges the facility releases, or has in the past released pollutants to atmosphere beyond air pollution permit limitations.  Caller alleges releases tend to occur at night when the system "pops the stack-cap" (term derives from system actuated event) and bellows thick black smoke.  Caller alleges holes have been drilled through concrete areas when spills of hazardous chemicals occur to allow chemicals to drain through.  SLVHD stated the facility may have hydrochloric acid identified by the caller which may be used in relation to stack acid scrubbers.  When pressed for addition chemicals, however, SLVHD said the caller did not cite additional chemicals.

name: Chevron (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 500 lbs. of SO2.  Caller stated that the flare header froze on the Till Gas Unit.  Facility was knocked out until the Till Gas Unit could be restored.  Incident began at 22:00 on 01/03 and system was brought back online at 06:00 on 01/04/12.

name: Herriman - Diesel spill at construction site
incident_summary: Caller reported a diesel release to soils at a construction site for Riverton City water tanks.  A rock punctured the fuel tank on a dump truck releasing 100 gallons of diesel to the soils.  Impacted soils were excavated and a soil sample will be collected.  The excavated soils will be placed in the rap pile and run through the asphalt batch plant at the Staker Parsons facility.
title_eventname: Herriman - Diesel spill at construction site

name: flammable spill in Lake Point
incident_summary: Xylene drum leaked about seven gallons to asphalt cleaned up with absorbents.

name: American Fork - Tibble Fork Dam Release
incident_summary: Caller reported that sediments containing heavy metals were released from the Tibble Fork Dam.  The release occurred while the dam was being drained by a contractor as part of ongoing rehabilitation project. Sediments discharged during the release entered into the American Fork River. The sediments entering the river likely resulted in a fish kill. The release reportedly began on the afternoon of 8/20/16.  The USFS was notified of the release and impacts to the river on 8/22/16. UDEQ advised the USFS to notify the NRC of the release.
title_eventname: American Fork - Tibble Fork Dam Release

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller stated that last night Bountiful Irrigation (B.I.) was excavating to find a broken water line.  B.I. Observed petroleum oozing from the banks into the excavation.  The crew pulled a 55-gallon drum from the excavation and just reported (10:00 am 10/12) having pulled a second 55-gallon drum out of the excavation that is full of oil.  The repair crew also uncovered rubber tires.  The crew is still attempting to locate the break and were digging northward to find it when they found the second drum.  The full drum was punctured by a tooth on the excavator; the crew was able to remove the drum and place it into a dump truck.  DERR indcated that the drum needs to be secured to prevent further spillage of its content.  B.I. Planned to find and repair the break and have it backfilled by this afternoon.  DERR advised that the environmental agencies (i.e. DEQ and local environmental health) may need to maintain the excavation until a more thorough assessment of the situation has been completed.  The oil is contained in the excavation.  The caller reports based on institutional knowledge a belief that this sub-division may be the site of a former (60-70 year old) garbage dump/landfill formerly known as "B.A.R.D.(?)"  To the best of the caller's knowledge surface water pathways have not been impacted.  DEQ suspects that a SUPERFUND site is nearby.  DERR advised the caller that materials excavated may be evidenciary if it is determined that the site was subject to some manner of illegal dumping vs. a former regulated municipal landfill.  UPDATE: 12/13/05 DWQ reports that B.I. Placed a layering of geofabric topped with gravel up to 12" below grade.  It was stated that they would install a french drain style mechanism with an "access portal" to enable the ability to visual observation and/or for collection of environmental samples.  Excavated materials were segregated and staged at the existing landfill until they can be characterized.

name: Uintah County - Treated Injection Water
incident_summary:
The caller reported a 75 bbl treated injection water release which surfaced on the right-of-way then traveled down the road about 1,000 feet into a drainage with frozen snow and ice. 

The caller stated that the release was contained by damming. The release also contained black iron oxide material. Water samples were collected. This area contains a critical species of cactus.

Notifications were to the following people: Nathan Hall (DEQ DE by phone), Randy Bywater (BLM by phone),  Jessi Brunson (BLM by e-mail), Rita Reisor (USFWS by e-mail), and Lisha Cordova (DOGM by e-mail).

name: Unitah Co - Hydraulic Spill
incident_summary: Caller reports a release of approximately 45-50 gallons of hydraulic fluid from a ruptured line on a haul truck.  Spill, to shop overburden, was cleaned up.  No impact to surface waters.

name: UPRR Diesel Spill Ogden
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a spill of 1/4 gallon of diesel from a locomotive due to mechanical failure.  Impacts are to the track ballast.  A spill kit has been used to contain the spill and will be cleaned up.

name: Uintah County -- Produced water release
incident_summary: 3 barrels of produced water was released from a failed produced water line.  All material was contained on site.

name: Kennecott Utah Cooper - Used Oil
incident_summary:
Map location is approximate, given address does not come up on the map.

Caller is reporting a release of >25-gallons of used oil.  The spill was contained to concrete floor and within a process drain on-site.  No impacts or release to the environment.

A fixed hydraulic oil pump seal failed for the turbine generator and has been stopped and repaired.

name: Delta Midpoint Block Valve - Holly - Diesel
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a spill of 42 gallons of diesel from the Delta Midpoint Block Valve.  

They were running a pig though the line and when they opened the valve, diesel came out.

The release has been isolated and contained and cleanup is in process.

Caller will report to BLM.
title_eventname: Delta Midpoint Block Valve - Holly - Diesel

name: St George Golf Course Fish/Bird Kill
incident_summary:
Caller reported to local DE that yesterday evening reports started coming in about dead fish and bird at the Saint George Golf Course. There have been a couple  dead goldfish/small Koi located in the pond, and 20 to 30 waterfowl located. Mostly Coots but a couple Grackles also. They have started their fish-kill protocol and gathered several bird to be analysed. Reports are that this is an area where the birds have grown accustomed to being fed and DNR wants to rule out it being something fed to them or possible avian botulism. Wild life officers are on site continuing their investigation.
DE Paul Wright has been on site and reports back that the pond is very brown in color, other fish, birds and turtles have been located in the pond and are unaffected. 
.
title_eventname: St George Golf Course Fish/Bird Kill

name: Vernal - Hydraulic fluid spill
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 30 gallons 10 weight hydraulic fluid to soil.  No waterways were impacted.  The spill was contained immediately and was cleaned up 1/2-hour later.

name: ANSCO WINDOWS (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: UST SOIL UNDERNEATH DIESEL FUEL

name: Unidentified (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports construction crew is tearing up old asphalt parking lot on the east side of the Head-Start Pre-School in Rose Park.  Work is being done in preparation for repaving.  Caller reports the smell is really bad and several individuals report being nauseous.  Work started two days ago but today the odor is really bad.  Caller said she was told of historical spill or underground storage tank in the area.  Caller expressed concern for children.
15Nov07 13:44 - SLVHD made inspection and interviewed the Morgan Asphalt crew PM.  Several days ago they excavated the lot down to a depth of 12 feet to install a storm box (other areas have been excavated down to a depth of four feet in preparation for new asphalt).   All soils initially excavated for the work were placed back into the excavation.  The SLVHD & PM reported blackened soils.  SLVHD reported an acrid odor like fresh asphalt.  The crew plans to pave soon.

name: Ceflon Corporation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: 50 square foot equivelent area of oil released to ashpalt was contained with booms and absorbants.  An irrigation ditch 200 feet away was not impacted.

name: Werner Enterprises (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Driver was traveling (east?) on Interstate I-70.  Driver swerved and exited the roadway at mile marker 13.  The truck landed in a ditch in a wooded area.  Saddle tank was ruptured and released an estimated 150 gallons of fuel.  UHP reported there is a standing creek nearby.  Fuel entered the creek but it is unknown how much entered.  Driver was transported to the hospital with injuries.  Reporting party stated that corporate personnel were not notified until just recently hence the delay in making the notification.  V.J. Environmental out of Salt Lake City has been dispatched to assist in the cleanup and is currently enroute.

name: 1 gal epoxy spilled to trailer floor near Delta
incident_summary: One gallon of epoxy resin spilled to the floor of a tractor trailer. No exterior release.
title_eventname: 1 gal epoxy spilled to trailer floor near Delta

name: Hunter Power Plant (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: At 13:00 the facility investigated surfacing water and discovered a failure in an 8-inch line that transfers water from No. 1 irrigation basin to No. 2 irrigation basin.  Water was flowing to Rock Creek at estimated rate of 100 gpm.  Pipes and pumps were shut at 13:30; this slowed rate down to 5-10 gpm.  A pump was deployed at 15:45 to divert flow back to reservoir: this action stopped flow to Rock Creek.  Facility is getting a confined space permit to access and close an additional valve before line repairs can be made.  Flow is waste water from process system.  Discharge permit is not involved; water is used to irrigate research farm at the facility.

name: Salt Lake Co - Oil
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a release of an estimated 10-15 gallons of oil to the ground from a locomotive.  No drains or surface waters are impacted.  Cause is unknown at this time.  UPRR Hazmat manager has been notified.

name: Crude Oil Pipeline - Montezuma Creek
incident_summary:
The caller is reporting two pin-hole size leaks in their 8-inch crude oil pipeline.  

Up to 3-barrels have been released to the surrounding soils.  The leak has been stopped and the soils are being excavated by company personnel.  The soils are being disposed at Environmental Services Landfill (San Juan County?)

name: EDO Corp (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Spray nozzel in scrubber portion of spray dryer unit malfunctioned and released ceramic powder,  containing .2% nickel oxide into the air.  The incident lasted 5 -15 minutes and released an estimated 5-20kilograms of ceramic powder, which covered the facility's roof and the roof of neighboring business.  West Valley Hazmat team responded and determined that EDO could clean up the powder.  Clean up was done with Hepta vacuums and wet mops.  Caller questioned what the reportable time allowance was for this material and if he had to report the incident.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller witnessed white tanker trucks dumping an unknown liquid substance into what he referred to as "Kids" canal at 1500 West near 500 South (behind a movie theater complex).  He saw trucks doing this on at least two occasions: Thursday (Oct 16) at 6:30 pm and again the next day Friday (Oct. 17) at 12:30 pm.  The white trucks were the rounded tanker-type that backed up to the canal and released a liquid the caller described as strong, pungent, and possibly "sulfurous or solvent-like."  Trucks had no visible names or numbers on them that the caller could see.  The caller believes the canal eventually flows into Steinaker Reservoir.

Caller said he contacted dispatch with the County Sheriff's office (435-789-2511 / or -4222) and left his call back number but never got a return call from them.  He attempted to call the Ashley Valley Water Conservancy District (435-789-3212, or 435-789-1651) but said their office was closed.  Caller says so far there has been no response to his query.

Caller speculated that the liquid wastes being dumped may be oil-field related.

name: 9000 gal Road Oil Spill Update
incident_summary: A tanker carring a load of a water based road oil went over the edge of the road and down a steep embankment spilling the entire load (9000 gallons).  The spill is about 150 yards from any surface water.  About 200 gallons of diesel fuel was also spilled.  A cleanup contractor has been called and the driver taken to the hospital.  In the company called at two a.m. on July 2, 2013 to update information concerning the release.

name: Chevron USA (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Vapor recovery unit down at this time.  Power outage for the area knocked out thermocouple.

name: Nickerson Company Inc. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that about 30 days ago, free mercury was found on asphalt paving in the company yard.  The source of the mercury is thought to have leaked from a submersible water pump.  Quantity is uncertain but is thought to be about 2-3 tablespoons.  The company is a supplier of pumps to utilities, etc, a pump may have been source of the mercury.  Caller called SLVHD that day and Steve Beach responded.  Steve advised the company how to clean up the mercury, using a turkey baster, rubber gloves, broom and dustpan.  The mercury was cleaned up and the mercury plus all the cleanup tools and materials were placed in a closeable container.  This container was not transported to the county landfill until today.  Steve Beach had told the company representative to call the spill in to DEQ.  This was not done until today following the taking of the mercury to the landfill.

name: Unexploded Ordinance - Draper
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting that Adult Probation Parole was called out and discovered an unexploded rocket ordinance in a home in Draper.

Unified Bomb Squad called Hill Air Force Base EOD Tech and determined it was a live rocket military piece that needs to be counter charged.  The bomb squad transported the rocket to the Geneva Rock quarry in Draper and is seeking an emergency permit number.

I stated I was unable to provide a permit and the caller stated they just needed to report they were counter charging the device and would not be transporting it anywhere else.  They will get a permit number tomorrow morning.  He will call Katie Crane with DERR.

The ordinance is not hazardous other than the explosive.

The owner stated it was purchased at an Army/Navy store years ago.

name: Duchesne County - Injection Water Release
incident_summary: Caller is reporting that there was a release from a 3 inch injection line near the  9-25-8-16 injection well. The  treated water left the right of way and enter a dry drainage. The release was secured. They will flush the drainage with fresh water and collect soil samples to verify cleanup.

name: South Salt Lake - Paint dumping at Auto Body Shop
incident_summary:
Caller reported that the owner of the facility has engaged in multiple environmental violations. Owner has covered up an area of soil contamination at the southeast corner of the building.  The area us currently covered with gravel and chairs and made to look like a break area. Wastes are reported improperly stored and dumped in secondary buildings at the property. Caller reported that activated primer which is only for use inside paint booths is routinely sprayed in the open body shop area.  Owner of the facility also disposes of gallons of used paint in the dumpster.  Caller stated that he has pictures available to share.

Caller stated that there is a crew drilling on the property but could not identify if they were working on behalf of a state agency.
title_eventname: South Salt Lake - Paint dumping at Auto Body Shop

name: Produced water release near Bluebell
incident_summary: An estimated 5,000 barrels of drilling brine with zinc salts spilled from a collection line to a grass field and an irrigation pond. Oil Gas and Mining is on-site. The spill is being pumped up and oil collection booms have been placed at the outlets in case a sheen is identified in the water.

name: Piedmont Of Michigan (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: On call back, spoke to John Osterbaan of Piedmont.  60 gallons of diesel spilled from fuel tank of tractor at Port of Entry, Utah I-15 in Brigham/Ogden.  Traveling down road drive shaft broke loose & punctured fuel tank.  Lincoln Environmental is on-site performing clean-up.  John Osterbaan will be calling EPA as well (provided phone # to Region VIII duty officer).

name: H2S Gas Odor - Duchesne
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a recurring hydrogen sulfide gas odor.A at her home that is likely coming from a nearby blue bench disposal extraction well.  

She called a couple weeks ago (March 4th) and reported the same issue, but no incident found in the database.

Nathan Hall came out on March 7th with Dennis Ingram of DOGM for a preliminary inspection and talked Bernise's son Greg, then visited the surrounding wells on March 14th with Brian Speer of DAQ to look for VOC plumes using their IR camera.  The injection well was not in use at the time, but the thief hatches on tanks for both oil wells north and south of the house were leaking.  He left a card with Greg. I called Nathan on his cell and left a message.    Also, called Duchesne County after hours number and they said the would contact Mrs. Pilling tonight.

Mrs. Pilling called back and indicated the wind has shifted directions and they are able to breathe again and the odors have subsided.

name: Amoco Oil (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A pipeline broke at the point the pipeline penetrated a burm around an above ground storage tank.  About 1000 gallons of JP-8 jet fuel was spilled into the burmed area.  Most of the fuel was recovered.  The contaminated soil will be excavated, tested (TCLP) and will disposed of appropriately.

name: Chevron Products Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: 25 gallons of remediation waste water overflowed from a ground leaching pipe when a system pump failed.  This caused the waste water to  back-up and overflow the system.  Media impacted is soil.  A VAC truck is being employed to remove the waste water, and a contractor has been hired to repair the pump.  The spill has been secured.  Duration of the release was 45 minutes.

name: Hydraulic oil spill to soil at Logan Landfill
incident_summary: A hydraulic line broke on a knuckle boom releasing an undetermined amount of hydraulic line. Much of the spill was absorbed but it is estimated about 75 gallons of oil was lost to the soil. The spill occurred on January 15, 2018, but the release to soil was discovered on January 29, 2018.
title_eventname: Hydraulic oil spill to soil at Logan Landfill

name: Sandy - Small transmission fluid spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a one gallon transmission fluid spill at the Costco gas station in Sandy.  The spill has been completely cleaned up.  No waterways were impacted.

name: SLC - Anhydrous Ammonia
incident_summary: Caller reported the the alarm for the anhydrous ammonia system sounded at the facility.  The facility is currently investigating the situation.  Caller stated they believed the alarm was related to a small leak and that assistance of first responders is not required at this time.

name: Duchesne County Produced Water Release
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of produced water from the disposal facility.  Volume is unknown at this time.

name: Weatherford Wireline Transporting

The source was in transit at the time of the call. Information was forwarded to DRC and they were going to handle the authorization.

name: Weber County Diesel Spill
incident_summary:
The caller reported that due to a mechanical issue approximately 50 gallons of diesel fuel leaked from a refrigerated trailer onto the asphalt located in the parking lot at Treehouse Foods, 215 N. 700 W., Ogden.

At the time of this report the caller believed that no water bodies or drains were threatened or impacted but he did not have anyone on the scene yet.

Lincoln Environmental has been dispatched for clean up.

name: Ongoing gasoline release in Blanding
incident_summary: Caller reports that an ongoing release of gasoline is occurring at the unmanned gasoline service store located at 100 East and Center Street as you come into Blanding. There are four sets of dispensers at the location. The leaking dispenser is the inside dispenser on the southwest quadrant of the store. Each time you pick up the dispenser, a cup or two of gasoline spills out on the ground. This spill has been ongoing for at least three months. Both the City and the owner have been notified and no action has been taken.

name: PHILLIPS PETROLEUM (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: ONGOING SULFUR DIOXIDE RELEASE

name: Triple P Trucking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A manhole cover ruptured a truck fuel saddle tank.  About 100 gallons of diesel fuel was spilled.  60 gallons was recovered.  Lincoln Environmental will clean up site located near a warehouse.

name: Murray -- Gasoline in storm drain
incident_summary:
From the report:  "Admin Manager at Costco Store 764 in Murray Utah, called to report a gasoline spill at the gas station pump #2.  5 gallons was spilt and .5 gallons went into a storm drain.  The facility was able to clean up the remaining material that did not enter the drain.  There were no injuries or exposures."  Verisk 3E Incident #1360131

Followup report:  "*Rapid Response* called Verisk3E to provide the onsite and offsite times for the ER crew. The ER crew, Environmental Restoration, arrived on site at 2257 hrs EST, and off site at 2348 hrs EST. No fuel went passed the storm drain, no environmental impact. Fuel and debris was left onsite in Costco gas station waste disposal barrels at the request of the manager. The material was consolidated into the store's existing drum. There were no injuries or exposures. This incident was reportable to the state of Utah."

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Regina called to inform of return of odor at their facility.  She said she had symptoms of feeling faint and feeling nauseous.  Other employees vomited or felt nauseous or felt faint.  Wind was from the North at 6 mi. per hour.  This is an ongoing incident with reported odors at this facility or other nearby facilities.  The Weather Service building nearby reported similar odors  and collected samples with summa canisters.  These samples will be taken to Air Quality for analysis.

name: Kennecott Utah Copper Mine Concentrators and Power Plant (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Kennecott Utah Copper Mine Concentrators and Power Plant
incident_summary: Spill of fuel #2 oil occurred inside Building #1 Monday 4/23/12 at 17:30.  Release is estamiated at 25 gallons and was caused by fuel burner malfunction.  Release was to the floor was cleaned up.  A visual inspection of a storm water retention pond today revealed observation of fuel oil.  Facility inspectors traced the path of release back and found that fuel oil exited the building through a side vent, flow across asphalt and into a storm drain, and in to the clay-lined retention pond.  There is not discharge out from the pond and it terminates the the line for storm water.  North American is cleaning the pond and storm water piping.  KUC will file a written report to DWQ.
title_eventname: Kennecott Utah Copper Mine Concentrators and Power Plant (Null RP Substituted)

name: Chevron (Null RP Substituted)

An unknown amount of SO2 was released during shut down/startup procedures.  Estimated duration of release 39 minutes and both NRC and LEPC were notified as a precaution.  Information for this report was collected from John Hadley phone notification to DEQ and Tom Dahmen notification to NRC.

name: Double D Distribution (Null RP Substituted)

Accident happened next to an unidentified creek and is described as "very quick moving water."  Crude is still flowing from the vehicle and into the creek.  Volume estimated released is 1,500 gallons.  The release continues.    Resources enroute include: Kanab fire with defensive regional response trailer, Regional Hazmat out of St. George; and a team out of Colorado City.  Caller believes the creek eventuall drains to the Virgin River near Springdale.

++++++++++++++++++++++Update++++++++++7/14/09 via NRC+++++++++
Double D Distribution estimates that 500 gallons or less of liquid asphalt was spilled on the shoulder and into the stream.

UPDATE 7/14/09 @12:55 - PRP made voice notification to Utah DEQ.

incident_summary:
Caller is unsure if spill is in Colorado or Utah?  UTM coordinates given were not within Utah.  He said he would try to verify UTM info and either call back or call CDPHE in Colorado to report the spill.  

Map location shown is approx. only pending further info from caller.

name: Anadarko NBU 922-31N
incident_summary:
Yesterday at approximately 12:00 pm a tank leak was discovered at the NBU 922-31N location.  A condensate/water tank developed a hole in the bottom due to corrosion which lead to the release of 295 bbls.  290 bbls were recovered inside of the secondary containment.  There appeared to be a bent area in the northwest corner of the steel containment where approximately 5 bbls leaked out side of the secondary containment berm.  2 bbls of produced water seeped through the location and ran approximately 700 ft. down a dry drainage.  All released product was recovered except the 2 bbls that left location and due to the terrain and steepness of the area it was not possible to recover the released produced water.  Out of the 295 bbls release there were approximately 2 bbls of condensate that were contained inside of the secondary containment.  
 
The cleanup for this release started at 12:30 pm.  West Rock was able to control and contain the produced water that was leaking out of the damaged portion of the containment.  They were also able to stop the produced water from seeping through and leaving location.  Savage was able to drain out everything inside of the secondary containment and haul it for disposal.  All liquid and contaminated soil outside of the secondary containment is being collected and taken off for disposal.  All tanks were closed and drained so no farther produced can be released.

name: North Salt Lake Hazmat
incident_summary:
Caller reported that SLC Fire Dept. Haz-Mat responded to a residence at  915 West 1500 North and found a large quantity of leaking containers of hazardous materials.  SLC Fire is requesting UDEQ response.  SLVHD has also been notified and is responding.

UPDATE 6/4/13 11:34:  After the DERR Duty Officer discussed the situation with Jeremy Roberts (SLVHD), Craig Barnitz (DERR) and Chris Martin (DERR) responded to the site.  Dan Stevens (801) 244-4338 identified himself as co-trustee to the estate of Mr. Norm Fife (property owner).  Dan stated Mr. Fife was a defense contractor who accumulated the hazardous material through his work.  DERR personnel observed a large quantity of 5-gallon containers (~ 500 containers), 55-gallon drums and other containers of hazardous materials in various conditions.  Many appeared to be in poor condition and  at risk of leaking.  Containers were stored on the property with little regard to securing the contents or isolating incompatibles.  Many containers had no labels or labels were not visible.  Various containers were marked flammable, oxidizer, and Methyl-isobutyl ketone.  Property had a strong solvent odor.  After discussion between UDEQ and SLVHD, EPA was notified of the situation.  Duc Nguyen (EPA/OSC) will respond to the site on 6/5/13

UPDATE 6/5/13 14:08:  Craig Barnitz and Chris Martin (UDEQ/DERR), Jon Parry (DSHW), Jeremy Roberts (SLVHD), Greg Archuleta and Jason Draper (SLC), Duc Nguyen (EPA) visited the site.  Duc Nguyen discussed with Dan Stevens (property owner) entering into a UOC to facilitate clean-up.  Duc Nguyen will have EPA contractors visit the site to be inventory of the on-site materials

name: Maverick Country Stores (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports a southbound semi hauling gasoline (tank capacity 2700 Gal) had its’ trailer tank punctured by road debris while exiting I-15 (Meadow exit).  Driver stopped and temporarily plugged hole with a rubber glove.  Driver then drove to north bound entry ramp (east side of I-15), stopped and checked leak and found the plug failing, so he pulled into nearby Shell Station and off-loaded gasoline to stations storage tanks.  About 100 gallons of gasoline was lost to ground with some possibly reaching a storm drain near the southbound exit ramp.  UHP responded and called the Fillmore FD.  The FD called a regional Hazmat crew to scene.  The spilled gasoline was mitigated.  TW Company has been called in to remediate affected soils and storm drain.  Possibly water has been impacted.  UHP, FD, and Hazmat responded to scene.

UPDATE: 12/29/05: Wade Tolbert, a Delta based environmental health scientist, for the Central Utah Health Dept. visited the site and reports that TW Co. was actively remediating the spilled gasoline in soils, a storm drain culvert, and ditch.  The amount spilled is now in the range of 450 gallons, Wade reports.  There are no state waters, streams, ponds, or lakes to be affected in the area of the storm runoff collection system, the lead is therefore changed to Central Utah HD.  Check with Wade if you have questions: 435-864-3612.  

Attached are photos Wade took at the site.
Picture 01 is coming off the freeway at the Meadow exit.  Apparently he got the hole a couple of miles ahead of this but didn't leak much until he stopped at the bottom of the offramp. 
02 is part of the gutter. 
03 looking west to the freeway the gas and several hundred gallons of water flushed down the gutter. 
04 and 05 part of the gutter before picture 03. 
06 and 07 the spot were the driver patched the hole.  The spot off the road is one of the more contaminated areas.  This is looking south with my back to the Chevron. 
08 is just a little to the north of picture 06 and 07 this is the highest part and were most of the gas and water got into the gutter and culvert. 
09 is looking into a underground culvert which is west of the freeway into the field.  
010 is at the end of that culvert.  It was flushed past this point. 
011 is the end result.   It appears to have contaminated this dirt ditch at least to the fence past the workers.  
012 is looking at the ditch just before the workers.

name: UPDATE - Eureka - UPRR propane release
incident_summary: UPRR called to report a 23-car train derailment 6-8 miles south of Eureka.  One of the cars flipped over and released propane, quantity unknown at this time.  Workers in the area reported smelling propane.  The Juab County Fire Dept. responded and collected air samples.  A UPRR Hazmat team is en route to assess the release.  The incident location on attached map is approximate.  UPDATE (3/31/19,12:35):  Richard Moseley (801-696-8511 and 801-554-7576) with the Deputy State Fire Marshall’s Office reported that it is now believed that more than one propane tank may have been compromised in the derailment.  Any attempts to move the tanks may detonate them so for safety reasons, it’s been decided that all the tanks will be blown up at one time so that they’ll vent and burn, making the area safe to work in.  An explosive’s expert is en route to coordinate the detonation.  A Federal OSC is currently on-site.  UPDATE (4/01/19, 11:00):  Martin McComb, EPA OSC reported that the burn went well yesterday so the EPA is demobilizing and leaving.  He said that one tanker car with phosphoric acid remains.  It was protected during the burn and is intact and not leaking.  For updates, go to: response.epa.gov/juabcountyderailment.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports a Mr. Devon Dymon called complaining of waste oil in the irrigation ditch behind his house.  The quantity of the oil is unknown at this time, DWQ is investigating at the site.  Mr. Dymon reports there are several businesses in the area that may have dumped the oil.  The manager of the irrigation water is Larry Hartley.

Update from Tom:  Tom Rushing, DWQ, and Tracy Richardson, Wasatch County Health, (Inspection Representatives) conducted an investigation of the complaint on 4/28/05 at 1400 hours.  

A sheen was observed in the canal adjacent to the residence at 677 S. 200 W. in Heber city.  Inspection representatives also noted a heavy black sludge which appeared to be degraded oil.  An odor of petroleum product was also noted in the canal.  It was noted that the canal did not discharge to surface waters but terminated shortly after flowing past the residence.

Inspection representatives followed the irrigation ditch east (upgradient) and observed the sheen and sludge up to a block east of the residence.  It was noted that a resident at this location had multiple vehicle parts in the back yard, mostly car transmissions.  A trailer and truck were parked in front of the residence loaded with vehicle parts and an old vehicle.  A storm drain inlet was observed directly underneath the trailer.  Wasatch Co. Health will investigate the flow pattern of the storm drain inlet.  It was determined that this was the probable responsible party for the contamination to the canal. 

Wasatch Co. Health will follow-up with the residents and notify SHW and DWQ of their findings and actions.
Photos taken during the site visit are available through the DERR Duty Officer or Tom Rushing, DWQ.

name: Salt Lake County Residential Dumping

He has heard that drugs may have been manufactured at the home.  Recently the police were at the property and cars were being chopped there.

The home is currently vacant.

He would like someone to take a look at the property.

A soil sample will be collected to determine if further remediation is warranted. Release was caused by internal corrosion in the injection water line. name: Ogden School District (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: EPA reports that a representative of JBR Environmental contacted EPA to determine: (1) cleanup levels - specifically - re-occupation levels for faculty and students, and (2) the test methods required to ensure safe reoccupancy of a classroom subsequent to a release of 1/2 pound of mercury.  JBR stated that after the release the impacted room was locked down.  Qualified personnel only are currently allowed to make entry for the purpose of remedial action.   The container was still in the room and has been secured.  The floor which consists of "battleship linoleum" along with desk and chair feet were treated with "Mersorb" (a zinc based sorbant) and cleaned.  The floor was then wet-wiped.  JBR referenced mercury cleanup guidance documentation found on the EPA website.  JBR stated that monitoring is being done with a Jerome mercury vapor monitoring unit.  JBR is currently venting the room to determine if cleanup actions have been adequate or whether additional action will be required.

name: SL Airport Dewatering
incident_summary:

This activity appears to not fall under a Construction Stormwater permit coverage and should qualify to go under a Construction Dewatering permit. The house being torn down is an old Pioneer home and caller believes it likely contains asbestos and lead siding.  The wind is blowing in the direction of the caller's house and he is very concerned that his children are being exposed to airborne asbestos. He investigated the complaint and found that the contractor does have a demolition permit and no lead or asbestos was seen in the house.  DERR contacted the RP and informed him of these findings.

The impact ignited a fire which destroyed the tractor.  Leeds fire Dept. extiguished the fire.  UHP reports - despite the fire, there still remains a considerable amount of diesel fuel on both the roadway and soils. name: Alumax (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Laidlaw trucking picked up a mobil, solid waste dumpster at Alumax that, unknown to the trucking company, held 6 drums previously containing sulfuric acid.  While dumping the load into a Springville transfer station, several drums rolled onto the ground.  One of the drums was run over by the truck.  An estimated 15-20 gallons of acid were still in the drum. About 5 gallons of acid was released. Three Laidlaw employees were exposed and transported to the hospital, one suffering breathing difficulties.  Springville Fire Department responded and neutralized the spilled acid.  Two other drums reportedly had similar amounts of acid.  Russel J. Black informed the local authorities that he had given instructions for the drums to be washed out before being placed in the dumpster.  Photographs of the incident are available from Springville City Police.  Copies of the Springville City incident report are available from DERR.  DERR is unaware of this incident being reported by Alumax to any division in DEQ.

name: Salt Lake County - Unused Oil

Approximately 40 to 80 gallons of unused 15W-40 oil has been released. Total quantity remains to be determined.

name: Salt Lake Co - Petroleum in SLC Storm Drain
incident_summary:
Caller reported that Tesoro workers were checking on restoration wok in the park that was being done when they checked a storm box and witnessed sheening. They deployed containment measures and proceeded to investigate the source. They confirmed it was from an upstream location and not connected with a recent release from their pipeline. They notified SLC and DWQ of the relaese. SLC proceeded to investigate the storm drain system. They were able to locate a section of line in an old train yard located near 900 North and 500 West. They have proceeded to collect some product, but have reached a section of line that is full of railroad ballast and debris. They have not been able to connect with URPRR to gain access to the railroad right of way to clean out that section of line and are still investigating it. 

UPDATE: Notification from UPRR Critical Call Center indicating oil sheen from discharge line located near 700 North at south end of the UPRR North Yard.  As noted above, Salt Lake City Public Utilities has a contractor (Envirocare) on-scene deploying booms, etc.  Crews are investigating the source.
title_eventname: Salt Lake Co - Petroleum in SLC Storm Drain

The initial response contractor recovered 1500 gallons mixture of gasoline and oil.  Fire Dept responded and extinguished the fire.  Caller reports the tanker was carrying about 8,500 gallons.  Caller estimates potential volume of release is 7,000 gallons.  Fire suppression water, and fuel flowed into a storm water retention impoundment situated between I-15 southbound and the off-ramp to Highway 6 Spanish Fork.  Unless capacity of the retention area was exceeded, it should contain the release (still under investigation).  Contractor is currently on-scene excavating contaminated soils. name: Mt Pleasent Gravel Pit Burning
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting that there has been an ongoing issue with a gravel pit outside of Mount Pleasant in Sanpete County. The Gravel Pit allegedly has been receiving hauled waste including electronics and hazardous materials, collecting them and then burning it on-site. They will then move the waste around the site and bury it. They allow the ash to fly around the area and it impacts peoples homes. 
Caller is reporting that it has been going on for years. They have recently filed electronic reports from the DEQ website to various Divisions and followed up with Written reports to DEQ. They indicate they are including pictures.
Update from DEQ DE John Chartier 12/30/13 14:30 hrs

Phil Bondurant and I went out to the gravel pit today and looked around.  There wasn't anybody at the site, so we asked an employee at an adjacent business who owns the gravel pit.  The gravel pit owner is Branch Cox, a local contractor who we are familiar with.  While at the gravel pit, we did observe where the owner had been placing fill dirt in an area that I assume had been mined out for sand and gravel.  In addition to clean fill dirt, we also observed two places where it appeared the owner had disposed of some demolition waste.  The demolition waste had some boards, plastic, metal and other miscellaneous building material.  One of those two piles of demolition waste did appear to have been burned.  We did not see any hazardous waste or electronic waste at the site.  The majority of the fill being placed at the gravel pit appeared to be dirt, rocks and broken up concrete.

I called and spoke with the owner, Branch Cox, and let him know that dumping anything other than inert material on his private property isn't allowed.  I also let him know that if he wants to dispose of the construction and demolition waste on his property that it would have to be designed and permitted as a solid waste landfill and approved by the State of Utah Division of Solid and Hazardous Waste.  Mr. Cox said he wasn't aware of the rules regarding the disposal of demolition waste on private property.  He also indicated that due to the remote location of his gravel pit, he can't control other people from illegally dumping their waste at the site.  Mr. Cox agreed to not place anything other than inert material in the mined-out area of his gravel pit in the future.  He will also work on installing working gates at the entrance of his gravel pit in an effort to keep the general public out.  I should mention that the main gate entrance to the gravel pit does have a large sign that reads, "No Dumping Allowed".  

My opinion is that Mr. Cox will correct his actions and not continue to dispose of construction and demolition waste at his gravel pit site.  I am frequently in the Mt. Pleasant area, so I can periodically check the site for conformance in the future.

name: Vineyard Power Plant Acid Leak
incident_summary: Kerry Powell called reporting that they discovered a leak in the chemical feed system while working on another project. They were removing the concrete covers from the piping channel that crosses under the road between the cooling towers and the chemical storage building. Upon removal of the covers they discovered the channel was full of water with a low pH. They brought in a cleanup company who recovered the water/acid solution and noticed some of the channel liner was damaged. They initiated a soil investigation today along the channel. They dug 14 holes two feet deep along the channel. They tested the soil/road base by adding water to it and testing the pH level using pH paper and found one spot where the pH was low. They are going to remove the soil and determine what else needs to be done for remediation prior to covering the site again. They estimate between 4 and 40 gallons of the acid used in controlling the pH in the cooling towers. The water/acid solution collected from the channel will be used in the cooling towers to maintain the pH. A report will be emailed in by EOD April 4th.

incident_summary:
Caller reports strong odor of diesel on the Jordan River in the vicinity of the Cannon Health Building/Dept. of Agriculture Building location in Salt Lake City.  The caller then proceeded to the Jordan River locations co-located with the Fair Park and 2nd South.  The caller reported a sheen at the Fairpark.  Presence at 2nd South location appeared dimished relative to other locations.  DERR contacted the DWQ ER contact, whom reported similar observation of petroleum product the 7800 treatment plant.  Plant personnel had collected a sample for analysis.  One hour later when the results were completed, petroleum was still being observed.  There is appears to be insufficient information at this time to determine whether the observations in the North Temple area are related to the observation made at the 7800 treatment plant location.

Additional Observations - DERR made observations of the Jordan River at North Temple (south side 13:05) and at 500 North (13:12).  No odor, nor significant sheen was observed at either location.  Isolated patches of hydrocarbon sheen measuring several inches across were observed as spot eruptions to waters surface at the latter location.  Size of these eruptions relative to surface area of the river (with a width equivalent to a city street) was insignificant.  DERR has communcated these observations to DWQ.

name: Kennecott Arsenic Discharge
incident_summary:

The detection was made using a portable XRF instrument in the field.  Data from the laboratory analysis of the samples expected Monday (3/31) or Tuesday (4/1).

He reported that the elevated levels are in soil that is off Kennecott property along 7800 South west of Highway 111.

Mr. Vinton stated that their groundwater discharge permit requires them to report a discharge within 24 hours of discovery and that is why he was calling.  He stated that he left a message with Dan Hall at approximately 5:45 PM today (3/28).

name: Quik Transportation (Mark Nicholson) (Null RP Substituted)
address: Hwy 6 Eastbound at MM 192.7 Spanish Fork
address_location: Hwy 6 Eastbound at MM 192.7 Spanish Fork
incident_summary:
Caller is making notification of a crash involving a fuel tanker truck w/pup.  The vehicle took a turn and rolled onto the K-rails.  The impact ruptured the tanker.  The truck was carrying 8300 gallons of unleaded gasoline in a single compartment trailer.  Total amount of material released is currently unknown but the entire contents was either discharged to the ground or consumed in the subsequent fire.  Area impacted is estimated at 180 yards long x 2 yards width.  The driver was life-flighted w/ severe burns.  Spanish Fork River is approx. 75ft distant (no impact to river).

UPDATE 5/5/06 Progress report: Ten 2-inch wells were installed between the south track and Soldier Creek.  Wells are on 10-foot centers.  Well depths are between 16 - 18.5 feet.  Two wells had floating product.  Surfactant injection and recovery system remediation is being considered.  Injection wells will be installed and the source area delineated.  Use of surfactant requires approval from PRP and DEQ Div. Water Quality.  With the recovery system operating 24/7, the estimated time of removal is 2.5 weeks.  North side of Hwy 6 has been remediated.  Excavation along the south side of Hwy 6 is underway.  Detailed exacation is necessary to prevent damage to buried utility lines.  Will investigate potential migration along subsurface utility bedding material, and migration beneath the roadway.

name: Tesoro (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:

Should be starting up once UP&L gets out, however.  No immediate danger appears present.  Backup boilers -> steam turbines were activated last night, they lost those too for a while until they were able to get them re-lit.

UPDATE 4/17/02 - As of 23:00 hours 4/16/02 reporting flare event due to power failure.  Minimizing feed to unit that is flaring should be secure by 10:00.  Sulfur Dioxide at a release rate of 80 lbs./hour.  As of 09:20 4/17/02, the main process unit is on-line, however, still undergoing stabilization.  Rate of release has decreased to 40 lbs./hour.  Should be stable sometime this evening.

Crews started the clean-up activities but will need to return Monday with additional resources.  Sandblasting operations may need to be employed to remove diesel staining from rock faces on roadside.  Envirotech contact - Greg Crabtree cell (505) 947-9510; office (505) 632-0615.

Thatcher estimated 60 or 70,000 gallons of liquid were created.

Response: Salt Lake Fire Department was on the scene containing the fire and the running liquid.  Thatcher employees used a backhoe to build a dike preventing further flow of the material.  Two workers needed to be de-contaminated. Thatcher Chemical has so far not contacted the NRC on this because there are no RQs for the product.  Possible evacuation warnings were reported by viewers of the TV News.  At the request of Thatcher Management, DEQ employees visited and photographed the site Tuesday morning.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller stated that a report was received by UDOT of an alleged transformer observed in the roadway of SR-6 at milemarker 177.  Caller indicated that SR-6 has been shut-down between milemarkers 177 & 182, Route 89 westbound from Thistle is also closed.  Caller stated that there is no vehicle (PRP) on-scene to which the released material may be attributed.  Responders think the cargo fell from a truck and theorize that the driver was unaware of the loss.  10-15 gallons of material is on the road.  Provo Hazmat and UHP are on-scene.  A UP&L representative is also enroute.  The officer first on-scene has informed other responders of respiratory difficulties.

UPDATE 6/6/03 11:21 - UDOT provided the following add'l info.  UP&L responded and performed cleanup.  The transformer which is new (manufactured 2003) is a pole-mounted type unit with a 15 gallon capacity.  The plugs were still in place and the unit holds pure mineral oil.  Allegations of an individual succumbing to vapors were confirmed but not attributable to the transformer.  

UPDATE 6/6/03 16:18 - Utah Co. Health Dept. provided the following add'l info.  UCHD responded to the incident at 8:45.  First responders were still assessing the incident and determined that the transformer was newly manufactured (no PCBs) and owned by UP&L.  All mineral oil was released and remained on roadway asphalt; thus no waterways nor soils were impacted.  Majority of liquid absorbed into the asphalt and absorbant (kitty litter) was used to capture remaining free liquid.  Mineral oil is not suspected as cause of respiratory difficulties reported by 1st responder(s).

name: Freeway Chevron (Null RP Substituted)

Caller reported that 50-80 gallons of diesel was released to the asphalt at the Freeway Chevron.  The released diesel ran along the curb and gutter along the roadway.  Caller reported that the released diesel was close to a storm drain and that an unknown portion of the release had impacted soils in a vacant lot adjacent to the facility.  Upon discovering the release workers at the Chevron deployed absorbants in their spill kit to contain the release.  The Washington City Fire Dept. was notified and responded with additional absorbants.  

The DERR contacted the owner of the Freeway Chevron (Brad Anderson - 435-680-2120).  Mr. Anderson stated the release was caused when a trucker overfilled his saddle tank.  The wastes collected from the release have been containerized into two 5-gallon buckets.  Fuel Tech was contracted to dispose of the absorbant wastes.  Mr. Anderson stated that the storm drain consists of 3 catch basins none of which had diesel odors upon his inspection.  Washington City workers who happened to be visiting the Chevron this morning were asked to inspect the storm drain.  The Washington City workers reportedly did not note any diesel odors the storm drain.  Mr.  Anderson stated a small pile of sediments at the end of the gutter were contaminated but the release did not impact the adjacent vacant lot.  The contaminated sediments were containerized along with the other absorbant materials used in the response.

name: Resident (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported that the Provo Fire Dept. responded to a mercury release inside an apartment.  A resident inside the apartment was showing symptoms of mercury exposure and was taken to the ICU at Utah Valley Hospital.  The resident had been extracting mercury from computers parts.  How long this activity had been going on or the quantity of mercury handled in the process is not known.  A room-mate inside the apartment did not show signs of exposure.  The Fire Dept. locked down the apartment and will see that a response contractor is hired to investigate and remediate the release.

Fire Dept. Contact is Battalion Chief Tom Augustus.

UPDATE 1/6/09:  Dale Urban and Craig Barnitz (DERR) arrived on-site @ 10:30 on at Branbury Apts. and met with Boyd Stringham and David Johnson (UCHD) and Brandon Bourgeois (Branbury Apts) before analyzing APT. 210 with the Lumex mercury meter.  The situation by then had changed to the resident ingesting an unknown quantity of mercury before vomiting the material back up.  A clean-up was attempted inside the apartment by the resident's father before the Fire Dept. was notified on 1/3/09.  The Fire Dept. locked down the apartment and instructed the Branbury Apartments to hire a response contractor.  The total quantity of mercury left in the carpet as reported by Brandon was the size of a marble.  Response contractors contacted by Branbury Apartments either did not do mercury response or would not respond to such a smalll release.  Brandon removed and double-bagged the contaminated portion of carpet and requested that the UCHD and the DERR analyze the apartment to determine if it is safe for re-entry or in need of further clean-up.  Breathing zone concentrations inside the apartment varied between 519 - 1,400 ng/m3 with isolated hot spots in the carpet and padding, kitchen garbage can, and near cleaning supplies (mops and sponges under the sink) reaching 1,200 - 5,000 ng/m3.  EPA recommends 1,000 ng/m3 for human occupancy.

Mops, sponges, and garbage from the initial clean-up remained in the kitchen area and would need to be disposed.  Sinks in the bathrooms and kitchen should have their p-traps cleaned or replaced.  According to Brandon, the entire carpet inside the room and a small wooden board beneath the kitchen sink will be replaced.  The DERR recommended that several cycles of elevating the heat inside the apartment followed by ventilating the apartment be done before installing new carpet.  Contaminated carpet is stored in a locked storage space until proper disposal can be arranged.

UPDATE 2 1/7/09:  Contacted by Barbara Crouch (Utah Poison Control) and asked if the DERR could use the LUMEX meter to monitor the ICU unit at Utah Valley Regional Medical Center (UVRMC) where the patient is located.  Contact for UVMC was Jolyn Hulse (801) 357-7232.  Based on these readings a recommendation was made that the nurses in the ICU minimize their time around the patients head.   The hospital also asked if the level of risk the nurses might encounter by working near the patient for the duration of length of his stay (estimated weeks to months) could be quantified. The hospital also inquired if the hospital should consider requiring nurses to use respiratory protection around the patient.  DERR referred these inquiries to the DERR toxicologist Scott Everett and reported the situation to the EPA (Curtis Kimbel (OSC Mngr.), Gina Andrews (OSC), and Jason Nakatsu (Occup. Health & Safety).  Scott and the EPA discussed the situation and developed recommendations to make to UVRMC.  Scott discussed the issues with Robin Ebmeyer (801) 372-2500 at UVRMC.  Hospital has contacted their IHC corporate Industrial Hygienist Nick Rice(801) 442-3613 to assist.

UPDATE 3 1/14/09:  Tyrus Mitchell (KCI Enterprises) the company that rented the bed used for the patient in the ICU unit expressed concerns that the bed may still be contaminated and affecting employees in the storage area.  Tyrus Mitchell explained the bed was returned to KCI from UVRMC without certification of decontamination.  In a follow-up call to Nick Rice (IHC Occup. Health & Safety), the DERR found that the bed was removed and transported back to KCI before Nick could sweep the bed with his Jerome unit.  The issue appears to be with the rental agreement between IHC and KCI and should be worked out between the two parties.

name: Not reported (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:

Weber Morgan District Health Dept. is investigating further.

UPDATE 2/9/07 10:20am: DERR staff will respond to the school to monitor the classroom.  The spill is in a carpeted area.  No information is available about the spill amount.  Reportedly no spill clean up has been done.

UPDATE 2/9/07 13:10 - DERR staff confirmed release of mercury to a carpeted area of a classroom.  Room has been isolated to occupancy and is being ventilated.  Volume of mercury spilled estimated at less-than 1/4 teaspoon described as "a globule the size of an adult's little fingernail."  The school district has engaged a contractor for cleanup.  DERR personnel will proceed to the student's home to perform monitoring.

UPDATE 2/9/07 15:20 - DERR found significant contamination in the home of the family of the student who brought the mercury to school.  DERR notified EPA.  EPA has requisitioned a contractor to perform a removal action at the home.  EPA OSC will arrive later today.

UPDATE 2/12/07 9:00 - Received NRC for residence. NRC # 826092.

name: Dixon Brothers Trucking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A semi-truck carrying 3601 gallons of zinc sulfate solution wrecked at Honeyville exit yesterday (MP 375 southbound).  Initially Randy Wilde of the Bear River Health Dept. understood approx. 15 gallons of the chemical spilled onto soil into a contained barrow pit area of the freeway.  Late on 8/29, Wilde reported the spill estimate was increased to 500 gallons.  The contents of the wrecked truck was pumped by TW into a second truck which has been stored in the TW lot in North Salt Lake.  Wilde requested that TW do a "before and after weight" on the truck into which the remaining chemical was pumped so an accurate determination of the chemical spill could be made.  The chemical was shipped from Carus Chemical in Great Falls, Mt. (Ken Cragowski at 815/224-6860) who reported via phone to TW that the chemical was a 35% solution. Dixon Brothers Trucking (Mr. Huxfeldt at 307/746-2788), also from Great Falls, Mt., reported the chemical was a 12% solution.  The concentration of the solution is NOT provided on the shipping documents.  The spilled chemical has flowed into the road base of the freeway and remains there at the present time.  Mark Millett of the UHP (office # 801/596-9248) is involved with the spill and is attempting to determine if the RQ for the chemical has been exceeded.  The CERCLA RQ for zinc sulfate is 1000 pounds.  The other lead agency is UHP, Contact is Mark Millett at 801-596-9245.

name: Suspected former employee (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller owns a lawn care service in Provo.  Caller reported that an employee (described as disgruntled) quit on Friday (9/21/07) and threatened to report the company to the EPA on Monday with allegations of illegal disposal of pesticides at the facility.  Earlier this morning an unknown chemical spill was found in back of the facility.  Caller did not know what the chemical was (described as having a strong chemical odor) or how much was released but observed stained soils and 2 plate-sized puddles.  Caller did not know if any of her pesticides had been stolen from her facility.  Caller believes the spill is the former employee following through on their threats.  Caller was looking for advice on where she needs to go to follow-up on the incident.  Boyd Stringham (UCHD) agreed to follow-up.

UPDATE 1:  9/27/07 14:31:   Information received from Boyd Stringham (Utah County Health Dept.).  Visited property at 1:00 pm this date. Met with owner, Carol Rowberry. Business is an on-going lawn care service and stores both liquid and solid pesticides and herbicides. Was directed to north side of business and shown an approximate 12-inch diameter, moist area on soil surface. Owner stated that when first noted by one of her employees that morning it was a standing puddle and had a strong chemical smell. If standing liquid was allowed to accumulate total volume would probably not exceed one quart. At time of inspection, there were no chemical smells noted or undue staining in the soil area that might suggest impact by chemicals or that soil testing and/or cleanup would be required. Other suspicious soil staining or chemical smells were not noted on the property. Groundwater in the area is estimated to be at 5 to 7 feet below grade. Soil in the area of the spill appears to be a silty clay loam. Owner stated that she had already reported incident to Provo City Police Department. Informed owner that if LHD receives report from outside party that implicates business then this information can be provided to Provo City Police if she wished to pursue criminal charges. Also informed her that she may wish to take soil samples at that time if she wished to build her case and/or conduct a clean-up.

name: Myra Peeks (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
SLVHD reports that the resident was shaking down a thermometer when it struck an object and broke.  All mercury content was released to the carpet.  The couple knew not to vacuum and gathered as much as visible material mercury as possible.  SLVHD has advised the residents to seal the room and intiate a heat-and-vent cycle.

UPDATE 20Feb06 pm - At about 1145 this date DEQ duty officers were dispatched with the Lumex meter to an apartment at 2233 E. 2100 S. (#28) to evaluate the levels of Hg contamination after a medical thermometer was broken on the preceding Saturday in the nursery/home office.  DERR arrived at about 1200.  Outside background was 0 ng/m3.  Ambient levels at chest level in rooms (front, kitchen, hallway, and master bedroom ranged from 400 to 777.  Chest level concentration in the affected room was 480.  Floor (carpet) level readings were 209, 176, and 460 in the area of the main spill of Hg.  Readings were taken in the baby crib near the bedding (sheets and mattress cover) and they were 5546, 4520, and 1171.  A faux leather covered desk chair nearby was measured at 1909 on the seat.  The crib bedding was then stripped off the crib, put in a plastic bag, taken outside and then the Lumex hose was inserted into the bag and got a reading of 773.  The crib toys (mostly fabric covered animals like teddy bears) were put in a plastic bag, taken outside and then the Lumex hose was inserted into the bag and got a reading of 1130.  These fabric materials are deemed to have adsorbed Hg vapors while the room was heated by an electric heater.  The bag of cleaning materials used to cleanup the initial spill of Hg measured 27,670 ng/m3.  DERR departed the scene at 13:15.
 
Rolf Larsen of SLVHD witnessed the Lumex survey.  He left instructions with the family and the landlord about further actions to take.  The carpet in the nursery/home office is to be replaced, everything else is to be aerated and/or wiped down and the apartment is to be further heated and vented.

title_eventname: Small fuel spill in American Fork Creek

name: Salt Lake Co - Excess Emission CO
incident_summary: Caller is reporting one-hour excess emission of Carbon Monoxide.  Is followup on shut-down initiated yesterday.  Cause is under investigation.  Amount to be determined.  Crew is changing out a control card.  Venting through scrubber stack.  No impact to public.  Should have card replaced within several hours.
title_eventname: Salt Lake Co - Excess Emission CO

name: I-84 Diesel Spill
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a tractor/trailer accident occurred on I-84 East.  The truck rolled off the road and the fuel tanks were leaking diesel fuel into Lost Creek, a tributary of the Weber River.

Hazmat was on the scene and deployed booms.  Approximately 50 gallons was spilled before the tanks could be secured and the spill stopped.  The spill was approximately 100 yards from the Weber River but no fuel entered the river.

The scene has been secured, the truck is being removed from the creek and clean up is underway.

name: Ceramitek (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported the release of 400 lbs. of sodium hydroxide from an electrolytic module due to a fire.  The release was confined to the secondary containment area with some of the product going onto the floor.  Fire was extinguished and the release was cleaned up and put into waste containers.

All information for this report from National Response Center Incident Report #888476

name: Niels Fugal & Sons, digging contractors for Qwest (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Niels Fugal & Sons, digging contractors for Qwest
incident_summary: Caller stated that contractors for Qwest were working behind his house when a hydraulic line broke on their bobcat tractor.  Hydraulic fluid soaked into the soil and sprayed everywhere including on trees and in the backyard of his next-door neighbor who owns a daycare.  Caller lives on the Provo River and said the fluid may have impacted the river as well.  Caller talked to the workers and discovered that they are digging contractors for Qwest.  The workers put a bucket under the scoop of their tractor and left for the evening but did not clean up the spill.
title_eventname: Niels Fugal & Sons, digging contractors for Qwest (Null RP Substituted)

name: Quality Control Thermowell (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller alleges the PRP has been mis-handling wastes for years.  PRP is a machine shop manufacturing "Thermal Wells" for the refining industry.  Units are machined from stainless steel.  Other alloys of copper, brass etc., are worked also.  Facility has 4-5 scrap bins used for disposal.  Bins have dimensions est. length, width, height of 4ft x 8ft x 4ft.  Waste bins are in poor condition rusty etc., so integrity is questionable.  Production waste cuttings with lubricants, etc., are put into the bins.  Rresidual liquids settle and drip out to the ground.  Lubricants for milling and solvents for parts washing/cleaning specifically mentioned include cutting oil, "Bio-Cool", and xylene.  Is concerned about the potential threat to ground water and nearby wells.  Claims one well is 150ft distant and claims most in the area are on well water.

name: Tri-City Nursery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Liquid fertilizer was released to storm drain (cause to be determined).  Estimated volume 50 gallons.  Drain flows to series of retention ponds, through horse property and out to the Great Salt Lake.  Name of material is Nutri-Culture Fertilizer "Mag-Iron Special" 18-6-18.  Indicates material percentages are 18% nitrogen, 6% phosphate, 18 potash respectively.  Davis Co HD acquired info from manufacturer (MSDS).  Public Works Dept. responded and was able to shut the flow at the source and deploy boom to contain the drain; they determined not to close the flood gate(s) at the retention pond for risk of flooding nearby residentials.  UDEQ & SLVHD discussed… would advise PRP of requirements to make notification to UDEQ and perhaps US EPA.

name: TESORO Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that a CO boiler breakdown is causing a process stream (FCCU region gas) to be diverted to a by-pass stack, creating excess particulate releases.  Opacity exceedences may occur until repairs are made which is estimated to be about 4 days.  Caller has also reported incident to Rob Leishman of DAQ.  Written incident reports will be sent to DAQ.

name: SLC - Chevron Refinery SO2 Release
incident_summary: Caller reported a SO2 release to flare that is expected to exceed over 500 lbs due to a power outage at the refinery.  Rocky Mtn. Power lost power to the Wasatch Front and is uncertain when power will be restored.  Chevron will follow-up with a report to the DAQ with exact quantities of SO2 released when calculations are completed.

name: Amoco Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Mixer on distillate tank - seal on shaft leaked.  50 gallons on ground.  Repaired - Vacuum Truck will collect material.  Diked area from tank 212, Flash pt 138 degrees F.  Not off-site maintained in bermed area.            The water oil mixture was recycled through the refinery oil system back to a crude storage tank, where the oil will be reran thru the refining process

The caller notified UPRR and was informed that they would attempt to identify train and secure engines.

incident_summary: Caller reported neighbor at 842 E. 600 South is burning wood during Red-Air warning.

name: Washington County - Refrigerant Gases
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a release of refrigerant gas (R404) inside of the building from a broken line on a refrigeration unit. The building was evacuated during the release. The equipment was repaired.

name: Dan McDonald/L3 Communications (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A chemist in a laboratory dropped a 3 liter beaker containing a solution of potassium silver cyanide.  Salt Lake HazMat was called in a decontaminated 6 people.  Over 200 people were evacuated from the building.  TW Company was called in and cleaned up the liquid from a 4 square foot area on the floor.  TW is conducting air monitoring in the building.  Duty Officer recommended that L3 call NRC & Report Spill.  Reportable quantity of potassium silver cyanide is 1 lb.

name: Diesel Fuel Spill in Duchesne County
incident_summary: Caller reported an estimated 10-15 gallons of diesel fuel that was released to the road and soil.  This occurred when part of the road that a tractor trailer was driving on gave way causing the trailer to lean and spill its fuel.  No drains or waterways were impacted. title_eventname: Diesel Fuel Spill in Duchesne County

name: Acme Truck Line (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Update 6/5/2012 12:45:  Trina Henrick called to report the fish kill reported on 6/5/2012 are associated with a hatchery incident and are not associated with the chlorine release.

Update 6/4/12 16:35: Trina Hendrick (UDWR Regional office) reported that an Area Invasive Species biologist reported 
 dead fish in the Sheep Creek down stream of the chlorine release.  Anglers in the area also reported seeing dead fish for the past 3 weeks.

Caller from the UDWR field office (Utah Division of Wildlife Resources) reported an overturned truck leaking a chloride compound Sheep Creek along SR44.  USFS officer and UDWR officer are at the scene.  Spill impacting Sheep Creek.  No additional information was provided.  I contacted the NRC to report the spill (NRC #100813)

Update 4/12/12 16:30:  NRC report provides additional information under a new NRC#: 1008525 reported by Greg Johnson, Acme Truck Line.  Primary Phone:  (504)352-1756.  Alternate Phone: (504)347-5210.  A truck rolled over resulting in a release of class 8 corrosive material from totes being carried on the trailer (Chlorite solution [UN1908], oil and diesel).  An environmental contractor has been hired and is en route.

Update 4/12/12 15:39 from Scott Hacking>Darrin Brown with TriCounty Health Dept. just called, and reported that the contents of 12 330-gallon totes of Sodium Hypochlorite had gotten into Sheep Creek.  The Creek is running high, and no evidence of a fish kill has been found yet.  DWR staff are still walking the Creek and assessing.  The cleanup contractor (Envirocare) is already onsite. Darrin's phone number is (435) 790-5375 if needed.

Update 4/13/12 10:58 am from Darrin Brown> I wanted to give an update in the chemical spilled. The chemical is called "Vicon NF Breaker". Sold by Haliburton. It is a sodium chloride solution containing 14% chlorine. UN1908 chlorite solution. Ph of 11.5-12.5. Some cleanup is under way, however, the semi is wedged in a ravine and has not been removed yet.

Update 6/4/12 16:35: Trina Hendrick (UDWR Regional office) reported that an Area Invasive Species biologist reported dead fish in the Sheep Creek down stream of the chlorine release.  Anglers in the area also reported seeing dead fish for the past 3 weeks.

name: I-84 - Diesel Release from Semi-Truck
incident_summary: Caller reported that a semi-truck overturned releasing both its load of onions, and diesel fuel from its saddle tanks.  The quantity of diesel released is unknown as the cab of the truck caught fire soon after the accident.  Local Fire Department arrived on-scene and proceeded to extinguish the fire.  Storms drain entrances were bermed and absorbent materials were applied to the roadway by the Fire Department. Some of the fire suppression water/diesel fuel mixture left the roadway and ran down the hillside.  The Weber River was not impacted by the release.  Zack's Towing was contracted to remove the semi-truck from the roadway and subcontracted Lincoln Environmental to clean-up the spill.  Lincoln Environmental cleared the roadway and is waiting on the Zuba Link Trucking's insurance company before proceeding with excavation of the hillside.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported observing a grayish film/discoloration on the water surface in an irrigation ditch near his home.  The ditch runs east to west on the south side of the 800 block of 16th Street.  Source of the material is unknown.

name: Thatcher Chemical Co. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
An air line connected to the bottom of a tank of potassium hydroxide (KOH) had a faulty valve and resulted in a leak (past the chicago fittings) of over 4,000 gallons of KOH.  
Response: Workers are going to pump the spilled KOH into large containers where it will be used in the future for pH neutralization of Thatcher's waste water.  No KOH reached any surface water.  Dave will contact LEPC and Fire Department next.

UPDATE 7/14/08: Received a call from Kevin Okleberry w/SLVHD (801-580-6681) at 3:00 pm (Monday 7/14).  He stated the spill was over 4,000 gallons of concentrated KOH (45%).  An employee had left a line open over the weekend, and the tank leaked at approximately 1 gallon per minute until discovered early this morning.
 
The concentrate leaked onto the ground and spread down to the porous soil along the railroad tracks.  Workers pumped it out, dug trenches downhill of the spill, and prevented it getting into any surface waters.
 
Kevin concluded that the spill was contained, there was no threat to surface water, and it was a remediation effort at this point.  He suggested they put some kind of neutralizing solution into the affected soils to prevent future affects on infiltrating water through the ground.
 
The Thatcher employee in charge of the cleanup is Kurt Morgan (801-972-4587).
 
I contacted Jon Parry w/Utah DSHW (801-538-6780) at 3:15 to provide him this further information.  He recommended Thatcher report this spill directly to DSHW and contact them if they have any cleanup questions.  I passed this request on to Kurt Morgan w/Thatcher via his voice mail.

name: Duchesne Co - Sodium Hypochlorite 12.5% 1200 Gals
address: NE NE of Sec 14 T3S R2W
address_location: NE NE of Sec 14 T3S R2W
incident_summary: Tote with 12.5% sodium hypochlorite was ruptured when struck by the tine of a forklift.  About 1,200 lbs (Vol ~ 2.5 bbls) of solution was released.  All was contained on-site at location 4-14-3-2.  Will remediate by VAC truck (100 bbl volume), top off with water.  Tentatively plan to deliver to a lined disposal pond upon approval of appropriate authorities.  Land is private with regulatory oversight by DOGM.

name: WLA Inc. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a piece of road debris (a brake drum) struck the saddle tank of a semi-truck releasing an estimated 90 gallons of diesel fuel in the eastbound lane of I-80.  An estimated 80 gallons of the released diesel fuel entered a dry drainage ditch along side the eastbound lane.  From the ditch the diesel fuel entered a storm water culvert that crosses underneath I-80 and discharges into a wetlands area and small stream on the westbound side of I-80.  An estimated 5 gallons entered the wetlands area.  Local Fire, Sheriff, and Bob Swenson (SHD) responded to the scene.  Fire Dept. boomed the culvert to prevent more diesel from entering into wetlands.  USA Environmental was contracted to perform clean-up activities.  Semi-truck was repaired at the scene.   Bob Swenson (SHD) will return to the scene on the afternoon of 4/16 to inspect clean-up activities.

name: Utah Lake -- Harmful Algal Bloom
incident_summary:
A suspected Harmful Algal Bloom was discovered on 6 Jun 18.  DWQ employees collected 5 samples from the area; all 5 were positive for anatoxin and microcystin toxins (one sample was above 4ug/L threshold) and had high cell counts.

Six other samples collected in other areas of the lake on 31 May and 1 Jun 18 were all below the threshold levels.
