incident_summary: Caller reported to the NRC that the suspected responsible party has piles of trash and industrial waste on the property. Two retention ponds are being used as collection and are being directly pumped into storm drains. At one point, there were multiple 55-gallon drums with contents unknown floating within the pond as well.
title_eventname: Cache County - Release to storm drains

incident_summary: Salt Lake City public utilities is reporting a break in a 12" culinary water main near 700 South and Redwood road. /the release started around 18:00 hrs and has been flowing to a parking lot and out through a storm drain. They are maintaining positive pressure on the line until they can isolate it. The road has been paved recently and the water valves have been paved over.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City Water Main Break

incident_summary:

address_location: 3459 S. 700 W., South Salt Lake, Utah

title_eventname: South Salt Lake -- Oil contaminated water

name: Tesoro Refinery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a substancial release of aerosolized diesel fuel from Diesel Distillate Desulfurization unit (DDU); this unit is a DAQ-permitted process unit.  A hole developed in an elevated process line in the DDU that enabled the formation of ice.  Personnel observed this anomaly and began investigating.  The sytem holds about 1200 pounds of pressure.  Personnel estimate release of H2S was greater than 100 RQ.  Hydrogen and diesel fuel were materials released in largest volumes.  Response crew attained full isolation at about 12:00.  The situation was discovered at about 09:30.  By 11:30 the system had been depressurinzed from about 1200 pounds down to 5 pounds.  Response personnels' initial concern was for a possibility that the Lower Explosive Limit of the diesel vapor hugging the ground may have been exceeded.  When SLVHD contacted DEQ HAZMAT had already departed and vapors were no longer a concern.

name: Delta Airlines (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller stated that during routine storm water sampling, an oil and grease sample exceeded permit requirements.  The area was resampled and still above the allowable limit within their permit.  The release was tracked back to a hydraulic spill by Delta Airlines that was not reported. The spill is thought to have been approximately 25 gallons.

Granite is conducting cleanup and has contained the spill.  They are scrubbing the gutter to remove all staining.

name: Unidentified (Null RP Substituted)

While pulling the car out, the oil pan was punctured and oil from the pan went into the wetland near exit 99 going into Tooele County.  Pads and pigs were deployed onto the water.  Tooele County Health is mobilizing to the site.

name: Amoco Oil (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Spill of 200 gallons of Sodium Hypochlorite 12% by weight.  Exceeded reportable quantity by 20 pounds.  Chemical is used in water treatment.  Failure of gasket in flange caused the release.  Approximately 100 gallons was recovered on site by vac truck and 100 gallons was lost to the soil.  They intend to turn and aerate the soil.  Spill area is located about 250 yards northwest of the main gate.

Inventory control records indicate 600 - 1,000 gallons of gasoline was lost from a faulty product piping elbow. At the time of the call approximately 500 pounds had been released.  They estimated that when the event was done approximately 2000 pounds would be released.

name: Sewer Backup & Repair - South SLC
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a sewer line that has backed up and they found two line breaks.  The line is being repaired onsite for one of the breaks and the second is in the UDOT ROW and they are waiting for a permit.

There have not been any breaches of sewage into the building or surface.  The excavation areas are being pumped as needed by Beck Sanitation.

DEFA Construction is the contractor and Corby Tubbs feels like they are doing a good job of containing sewage during repairs and keeping the business open.

name: Iowa Tank Lines (hauler) Cathie Henrie (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Cause is not yet known.  A pup trailer released 4,000 gallons of crude oil.  Crude ignited.  An estimated 2,000 gallons burned off.  Liquid portion of crude flowed into a culvert.  Fire Dept diked down-gradient from where the crude can be seen emergent from the culvert.  Temperature is 20 degrees.  Crude has solidified.  Culvert was dry except for a portion of fire suppression water: estimated volume 600 gallons.  Culvert flows to Currant Creek which flows to the Strawberry River.  A contractor has been contacted for remedial assistance.

UPDATE 11/29/11 - Cause is from semi with empty diesel tank trailer running into the back of a pup trailer hualed by Iowa Tank Lines (ITL).  Diesel Tanker was operated by Sinclair or contractor as responsible for accident.  Crude hauled by ITL.  Nominal capacity of pup is 5000.  Hauler checking on actual volume being transported.  Visual inspection did not identify any impact to water.  Water at the scene was generated by snow melt and fire suppression.  Drainage is present on both sides of the road, neither is flowing any water at this time.  Cleanup contractor is A Plus Environmental: they project collecting at least seven confirmation samples.   LHD consulted with DWQ.  Add'l detail is available.
title_eventname: Iowa Tank Lines (hauler) Cathie Henrie (Null RP Substituted)

name: Davis County Transfomer Oil Spill
incident_summary:
The caller is reporting that a green electrical transformer in her front yard is leaking oil.  The oil is killing the grass around the transformer.  The transformer is also sinking into the ground.

They have called Rocky Mountain Power five times and have received no response.

They contacted Davis County Health Department and were given the number of the DWMRC.

name: Chevron Products Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports a release of sulfuric acid.  It was estimated that the leak occurred over a four or five hour period before it was detected.  A storage vessel piping on the #1 cooling tower had corroded releasing the approximately 200 gallons of sulfuric acid to the plants sewer system. The release was contained within the Chevron property.  The leak was repaired and the pH of the sewer system was being monitored. The contact provided for Chevron is Chris Battleson.

UPDATE 6August2004: Written communication received from the reporting party and dated 6 August 2004 provides that additional investigation, information and review of the process data indicates that the release of sulfuric acid did not exceed the RQ (1000 lbs.) to trigger notification pursuant to §40 CFR 355.40(b); the reporting party therefore retracts the original communication of 31 July 2004.

SLC Fire and Storm Water and SL County HD responded and are investigating.  Contractor has secured drums and cleaned up spill.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City -- leaking abandoned drums

name: Haliburton (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting discovery of visible soil and groundwater contamination after an in-ground oil/water separator was removed for plant shutdown.  Contamination consists of miscellaneous oil and grease, etc.  PRP will set pump & treat.  Soil and groundwater samples have been collected.
UPDATE 08/31/11 - This release originated from a regulated underground storage tank program (UST) site. The UST program will oversee cleanup activities.

Anonymous party reported the following via email:  
"Sir, I would like to anonymously report a matter that has been brought to my attention I feel needs to be addressed and or investigated.  The dumping of used motor oil  by one Edwardo Vasquez, the manager of an apartment building located at 260 North 100 east in order to control weed growth. Though I have not personally witnessed it but there are people who have brought it to my attention that has witnessed him doing this. The owner of the said apartments is John Salzman (J.L.S. Investments LC.).  From my understanding the ground is saturated from his illegal disposing of the motor oil. Thank you for your time. "

UPDATE 11/19/08 17:49: Update to Incident #7177 (used oil complaint):

I went to the apartment complex yesterday morning (11/18/08) to make a visual inspection of the property.  The entire property consists of the apartment building and the asphalt parking lot, therefore, the only area with dirt and weeds is around the perimeter of the property at the fence line.  I walked the entire fence line around the property and could not see any signs of oil dumping (no stained soils, oil soaked weeds, etc...).  I also talked to an adjacent property owner and asked if he had seen anybody dumping used oil or noticed anything like that going on, which he hadn't.  

I then called the complex owner, John Salzman, and informed him of the complaint.  He was not aware of any oil dumping occurring there and said that he would not allow that.  He did say that some of the tenants occasionally do auto maintenance there in the parking lot (and I did see some 'normal' oil stains on the asphalt).  He assured me that he would talk to the manager about it and make sure that no one is dumping used oil.

name: SLC - Unknown material inside trailer
incident_summary: Caller reported that the driver observed that an unknown material of unknown quantity had leaked inside his trailer.  Trailer contains the following suspected leaking materials: UN1280 Flammable liquid (propeylene oxide), UN1263 Paint related material, UN1263 Paint; however, the driver was unable to confirm which was the leaking material.  Release is contained to inside the trailer.  H20 Environmental was contacted to provide evaluate and remediate the release.  Estimated arrival time for H20 is 45 minutes.

name: Duchesne Diesel Release
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 40 gallons of diesel from a fuel tank at an oil/gas rig.  Fuel tank supplied fuel to a generator and the release occurred when a connection line leaked.  Diesel fuel released to standing storm-water at the site and was contained with the use of absorbant pads.  No water bodies were impacted.  Release location described as approximately 3 miles west of Duchesne, Utah.  Release occurred on tribal lands.

name: West Haven - Concrete slurry spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of 7000 gallons of concrete slurry with a high pH.  Spill was completely contained on their property.  No storm drains or waterways were impacted.  They plan to let the slurry dry out and then place it in one of their piles.

name: SLC Airport - Sheen on Stormwater
incident_summary: Caller reported during a walk around last night at their facility, personnel from Atlantic Aviation discovered a sheen on the storm water entering a storm drain. Sheen was possibly from older spills of jet fuel or from orphan oil spills along an adjacent vehicle service road, but no source of the sheen could be identified. Storm drain was covered with booms and socks to prevent further entry. SLC Airport and the Airport Fire Department were notified by the RP of the release.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Leak occurred from a flange on the bottom of rail car tank of 98 sulfuric acid.  Leak occurred during the unloading of railcar to the sulfuric acid storage tank.  Rail tank was on a private spur track owned by Thatcher Co.  Leak was discovered after rail car was pressurized to begin unloading operation.  Operator immediately began depressurizing the tank car and notified shift supervisor who contacted in-house hazmat team to assess.  A stainless steel spill containment box was placed under the leak.  Hazmat checked the flange bolts and found them to be loose.  After tightening the bolts the leak stopped.  3000 pounds.

name: Salt Lake County - Diesel

name: Chevron Pipeline Release - Willard Bay
incident_summary:
Pipeline break has resulted in a significant release of diesel fuel.  The amount is not known.  The spill has been blocked by booms from leaving the site. No surface water has been impacted.  Lat 41.3676  Lon -112.04305.  Google Earth Placemark is attached.

UPDATE 3/19/2013 10:06 (mz) DEQ received an NRC report (Incident Report #1041504) that was reported by US Bureau of Reclamation out of the BLM Provo office. Duty officer confirms that this appears to be this same incident.  LHD personnel identified a more specific location in or near a culvert that was impacted (UTM coordinates 4585227N, 412087E).  NRC report indicates that the fuel entered into Willard Bay Creek a tributary of Willard Bay Reservoir (impact to the creek has not yet been confirmed).  The release is now thought to be only 100-150 barrels.

UPDATE 3/22/2013 12:24  (dtu) DEQ received a call from the Chevron Pipeline call center (Susan Wyman) who reported that during ongoing cleanup operations at this Willard Bay pipeline release site, that a on-site frac tank overflowed spilling approximately 400 gallons of water and 20 gallons of diesel fuel onto the parking lot and adjacent soils.  Spill has been contained and is being recovered, and an unknown amount of impacted soils was overexcavated and stockpiled on-site pending off-site disposal.  Unified command personnel are already aware of this frac tank release of mixed water/diesel fuel.

UPDATE 3/28/13 09:47 & 10:04 (mz) Received from Chevron - The Chevron No. 1 oil pipeline will begin filling today, March 28.  The start-up plan is anticipated to take 2 days with increased patrolling requirements.  Chevron is planning to begin shipping product in this pipeline on Saturday, March 30 if the stand-up tests show no integrity issues.  A Chevron inspector will on-site observing the start-up process.  Line pressure will be limited to 80% of the failure pressure, even after this stage restart, until we receive and address the results of the metallurgical and root cause analysis that Chevron was ordered to do.

UPDATE 4/01/13 11:20 (mz) From DOT - The Chevron No 1 Oil Pipeline was given email permission by DOT Region Director to restart flow at 80% last Saturday (3/30/2013) morning around 7 am.  Chevron did the required notifications of the major stakeholders and responders prior to flowing, including Utah DEQ, Willard Bay State Park, and local fire departments.
 
The pipeline was briefly started around 9 am Saturday to check the SCADA program logic, shut down, and then restarted shortly after noon last Saturday (3/30/2013).  It has been operating ever since. There have been no problems and Chevron is complying with all of the terms of the Order.  DOT Region Director spent the last day checking pressure recordings since start up, validated pressures and relief device set points in the field, went to release site to check out the repair and clean-up activities, confirmed ongoing surveillance, and ensured proper outreach was being done.
 
Before the DOT Region Director left Chevron’s SLC pump station, he made contact with the Federal EPA FOSC, and gave the OSC a pipeline status update.  OSC said the cleanup is proceeding well.  DOT also spoke with a representative of Willard Bay State Park (801-244-5892) to let them know the pipeline had been operating with no problems for the last day.

ATSDR recommends that levels be no higher than about 500 ng/cum, especially with small children. The homeowners were advised to turn the furnace on and heat the home to at least 90 degrees Fahrenheit and to air out the home. Neil Taylor will return 06/06/18 to monitor the home again. Cleanup contractor (Envirocare) was notified to respond.  Caller was asked to advise PRP of need to notify DEQ and NRC.  PRP notified DEQ, and said sumps are at the bottom of a ramped loading dock.  They pump up to driveway that flows to curb and then into storm drain containing a series of 3 traps.  Melting point of oil is 76ºF. Via NRC - Caller is reporting spill of mercury, volume estimated up to 2 cups, from an old grandfather clock.  Employee was winding the clock when the chain holding the counter-weight containing mercury dropped, broke and spilled to the carpeted floor.  Business personnel attempted to recapture mercury using dustpan.  
09/02/09 - LHD reports Fire Dept responded on request from LHD.  Technician from Utah State University with Jerome mercury vapor monitor (model not ID'd) provided monitoring assistance.  Upon interview responders determined that the carpet had also been vacuumed by janitor.   LHD advised business operator to (1) cordon off impacted carpet/floor space;  (2) and ventilate; and (3) retain remedial contractor.  Ventilation is being done by keeping front & back doors open during business hours, and by operating  in-house process equipment during off-hours.  Process equipment is specifically designed to ventilate with the intent to mitigate potential for process exhaust to remain in the building.  LHD reports that results from the mercury vapor survey done the following morning show concentrations are below OSHA PEL.  LHD recommended blood testing for two individuals, employee and maintenance.  LHD oversight continues.

Caller has lived at the location for 11 years and has noted gasoline/fuel odors in the past but this is the first time she has observed a train releasing fuel.  Caller is concerned because an irrigation canal is located within 10 feet of the spill area and the property line between her property and the railroad has a lot of dry grass creating a potential fire hazard with the presence of the diesel fuel.  Boyd Stringham (UCHD) will visit the scene to investigate the spill.  Based on his observations, Boyd will contact Alan Jensen (UPRR) to address any needed clean-up of the released diesel fuel.
UPDATE:  Visited site 7/28/05. Met with Susan Park. Walked track section in question. According to Ms. Park an unknown quantity of diesel fuel sprayed approximately 4 feet from an open engine tank port onto the track rock surface and weeds adjacent to the track. All of the sprayed fuel appeared to have lightly coated the surface of the rocks and had since vaporized. Undue odors or impact to underlying soil were not noted during the inspection. Based on current conditions at the incident site, it does not appear that remedial action is necessary. Her main concerns at the time of the event were odors and the possibility of any future events impacting a nearby, currently dry irrigation ditch. A phone message explaining the above was left with Allen Jensen, UPRR Environmental Field Operations Manager, 801-212-2752.

Cleanup is underway and additional berms have been made to improve containment since additional rain is anticipated. name: Kroger Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
The spill occurred during preventative maintenance on a pump.  The pump was not locked out and 9,800 pounds of anhydrous ammonia was released to the air.  Reportedly, a stiff wind blew from the east and prevented the gas from settling in low areas.  The 35 employees at the facility were evacuated and the local police department notified the residents to the west.  The Layton city Fire Department responded to the incident.

UPDATE 15:00 the PRP called Davis County Health, who called DEQ for additional advice - NH3, it was discovered, got into a retention pond.  The pH was intially determined to be 12, but with the rain had dropped to pH=9.  The PRP inquired whether they can release the water from the retention pond.  DERR contacted DWQ, DWQ to provide response.

UPDATE 16:30 DERR received a callback from the Layton City Fire Dept. (LCFD).  LCFD indicated that the crew was performing a routine maintenance activity to clear oil from the NH3 system that is apparently introduced by the pump system.  This activity occurred inside the low pressure ammonia storage building.  The crew (as stated above) thought the valve had been locked-out; when they removed the flange nothing emerged.  The valve was left dis-assembled when the crew left for lunch.  In the interim, the anhydrous ammonia discharged from the flange directly into a sewer within the building.  The sewer is a sanitary sewer tied in to the North Davis Sewer District (they were also notified).  The Fire Chief indicated to DERR that the liquid-to-gas expansion ratio caused manhole covers to blow off, NH3 was also backing up through sanitary system (toilets, etc. within the facility).

name: Production water spill, Neola
incident_summary:
On Saturday May 14, 2016 at approximately 9:30 am, Lease Operator arrived on the Linn Energy 1-3A2 Central Battery in Neola, Utah. The Lease Operator found that the saltwater disposal had over filled and spilled a large amount of production water onto the location. It was found that AC power had failed; this prevented the pump from transferring the production water to the injection well. The backup DC power had also failed; this prevented the high fluid level alarm from being sent.  Based on flowrates an estimation of +/- 2100 Bbl of production water was released.  OtherDetail
The production water left the 1-3A2 location on the south east side where lease road connects to the location. The fluid then followed the lease road to the next location, the Linn Energy 4-11A2 SWD. The water built up on location then left the south side of location. The fluid then traveled 490 feet off of location before stopping. I was unable to see any evidence of pooling. Dennis Ingram with the Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining was notified by telephone and notified of the release.
Location on Map only proximate to Neola.

name: Unidentified (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Resident of condo reported to LHD observation of elemental mercury in residence.  Resident does not know origin of mercury.  Health Dept. made notification & request for assistance from DERR to perform a mercury vapor survey.  DERR duty officers responded.  
Resident provided information.  Mercury was observed in bedroom.  Resident had already performed some cleanup to collect mercury by scrapping together all visible material on the floor (flooring material is false "hardwood" resin-based laminate).  Resident subsequently washed bedding and other items proximal to location of spill  then vacuumed.  Survey results showed ambient mercury vapors in the residence at concentrations below the EPA minimum recommended action level.  Intermediate action levels were detected from monitoring done inside washing machine.  Authorities made recommendations (1) dispose of all bagged materials and vacuum; (2) near-term passive ventilation of entire residential space, and active ventilation of washing machine space (latter space has active ventilation system); (3) seek alternative clothes washing resources (until) (4) request followup monitoring to determine that any residual source and/or vapor has been properly exhausted and vented.

name: Salt Lake Co - Cement into Parleys Creek
incident_summary:
Kevin reported that there was a release of concrete from underground as a result of groundwater forcing it into the new pipe being installed up the canyon. Location is along I-80 between mm 129 and 131. The report is just preliminary, a request was made of Kevin that either he might update the report, or send the updates to Dan so he can update the information. Also, this project should be covered by a Construction Storm Water permit, and Kevin requested those detalis be forwarded to him.
UPDATE: WW Clyde notifed DEQ at 21:21.  They're contracted to abandon an historical nine-foot diameter pipeline that carried Parley's Creek.  Technique is to seal by pumping a flowable concrete aggregate fill into the line.  Line was being filled today.  A hiker observed discoloration in creek and reported to DOH.  The slurry moved/flowed around the bulkhead walls and flowed to an outfall into the creek.  WW Clyde shut down the operation and made an inspection walking several hundred yards downstream.  Bulk of slurry settled out at the outfall.  Lighter fractions were carried downstream and caused cloudiness.  Crew was able to access down to area of "suicide rock" (where creek passes beneath roadway) where the creek appeared relatively clear.  WW Clyde was notified of event at 15:36.  Upon notification to WW Clyde pumping was stopped within 10-15 minutes,  BMPs were intiated, filter fabric and check damns were deployed.  WW Clyde is now monitoring the creek for pH and other characteristics.  Volume of release is estmated at 2 to 5 cubic yards.  However, limited daylight prevented inspectors from making a complete evaluation of volume and extent of material in the stream channel.  SLVHD conducted similar monitoring of physical and chemical properties during their response.   Caller requested call-back from DWQ to coordinate near term response.  Location is along south side of I-80 at mouth of Parley's Canyon entering from south.
title_eventname: Salt Lake Co - Cement into Parleys Creek

UPDATE:  Based on a phone call with Randy Tumbarello (Logistics Express, Inc.) at 11:20 a.m., 7-17-02:  He received information from Don Sagendonf with U.H.P., who reported from the scene that there was no spill of diesel fuel nor of the liquid oxygen, only a minor spill of motor oil because the truck is upside-down.

name: Salt Lake County Accurate Recycling
incident_summary:
The caller turned the phone over to the Murray City Fire Marshal, Phil Roberts (801-792-5301), who reported that the Murray Mayors Office had been receiving complaints from people in the neighborhood of Accurate Recycling about headaches and nausea.  Upon arriving at the facility they found that Mr. Leo was running a process to extract silver from other materials.  The process involved Sodium Hydorsulfide and Nitric Acid.  The nitric acid at the facility was 50% concentration.  The process has a scrubber but Mr. Roberts was not sure if it was working properly.  Mr. Leo said that it should be because he had just paid a large amount of money to get it working.
Mr. Roberts had determined that the company does not have an air permit or an EPA ID Number.  He was concerned because there was a large amount of waste in totes that Mr. Leo is not able to send for disposal because he doesn't have a number.  Mr. Roberts stated that Mr. Leo told him that he was conducting R&D on the process and that if it worked out he was planning to get the necessary permits and numbers.

name: Petroleum Vapors
incident_summary:
This incident report is related to Incident #13758 and Incident #13762 that reported petroleum vapors in multiple homes near a Chevron gas station and a petroleum pipeline in Layton, Utah.  

The Division of Environmental Response and Remediation (DERR) has taken the lead in investigating the source of the vapors with a 417-Petroleum Storage Tank (PST) Trust Fund investigation as well as utilizing the Hazardous Substance Mitigation Act (HSMA) funding to mitigate vapors from the impacted homes.  

On 2/20/19 petroleum vapors were detected in the basements of three homes with a Photo Ionization Detector (PID) up to 31 ppm.  The vapors were measured at the highest concentrations near the location where the gas and water lines enter the basements.  

On 2/21/19, Andeavor Pipeline began excavating an area around their pipeline in the backyard of one of the impacted homes.  There was no visual evidence of impacts to the soil from the pipeline, but they were unable to excavate to depth without shoring.  The last update from the pipeline was they were waiting for trench boxes so they can dig deeper.  The DERR contractor was on-site to collect samples and observe the excavation as well as begin planning a vapor abatement system for the impacted homes.  

On 2/22/19 at 9:30 AM, Morgan Atkinson and Kevin Beery contacted the Layton City Public Works Engineering Director, Steve Jackson.  The receptionist who answered the call stated she just spoke to another homeowner at 1107 W. 450 S. indicating she could smell gasoline in her front yard coming from the storm drain.  This location is approximately ½ mile south of the homes with vapor impacts.  The DERR’s contractor, Jim Coletta and Kevin Beery were on-site with Layton City Public Works (Steve Jackson) and the Fire Department Battalion Chief (Brad Wiles) by 10:30 AM conducting a survey of the storm sewer, checking for petroleum vapors.  The storm sewer discharges into Kays Creek on Weaver Lane approximately 1-mile south of the impacted homes.  Kevin and Jim indicated they could smell gasoline vapors at the Kays Creek discharge point and in a manhole slightly up gradient of the creek.  There was no sheen or gasoline in the creek at this time.  

Layton City stated the storm sewer is a 33-inch concrete drain, buried 16-feet deep.  The storm sewer originates at Hill Air Force Base, discharging into Kays Creek.  The Air Force installed the storm sewer sometime in the 1950’s. 

In an effort to isolate the potential source of the vapors, they were heading north to check additional manholes along the storm sewer, up gradient form the impacted homes and the Chevron station.  Vapors were not detected north of the Chevron in manholes on Sugar Street.

The sanitary sewer was also checked near the same areas and no petroleum impacts were detected.

Kim Shelley with the Division of Water Quality has offered assistance with any needed sampling of the storm drain water or creek.  Kim also stated that the Layton City has a Class B2 Storm Drain and it is their responsibility to identify any impacts to their system.  We told her they have an active presence with the fire department and public works on-site.  

Morgan Atkinson also contacted the EPA Region 8 Spill Number and spoke to Ping to provide an update of the expanding vapor issue.  Ping offered EPA assistance for anything that may be needed.

Brent Everett has been updated and will contact Alan Matheson, Scott Baird and Donna Spangler.

As of 13:20 on 2/22/19, Andeavor Pipeline personnel are beginning a new excavation on the north side of Gentile Street to observe the pipeline and determine if they have any petroleum impacts in that area.  I asked Kevin Beery to request they excavate to groundwater to determine if there is any free product or impacts below the pipeline that have not yet been identified.

The DERR personnel, Layton City, and the DERR contractor have been requested to maintain detailed field logs with contacts and address of potential impacts and survey locations.

name: Uintah County Produced Water Spill
incident_summary:
The caller reported that approximately 30 barrels of produced water was released and flowed from the well site onto adjacent land.  Due to the cold temperatures the water has frozen.  They plan to allow the water to hard freeze overnight and then they will scoop it up in the morning.

No water bodies are threatened.

The well number is WV67.
The API number is 43-047-20043.
Latitude is 40.12170, Longitude is -109.54303.

Caller reports receiving a call from the Salt Lake City Fire Department Dispatcher reporting an odor and units sent to the site.  DERR contacted the FD Dispatcher, Phil Crocket, 801-799-4231.  The FD contaced the  LHD and the EPA, Dave Lemon.  The odor inside Beehive Clothing facility was suspected to be from a hazardous material source.  There were 17 people working in the affected area and 5 were sent to the hospital (via ambulances) with dizziness and nausea symptoms.  The workers were working in a relatively small, confined space.  The FD had two units at the scene and hazmat teams were analyzing the air. They found the oxygen levels were good.  At 13:47 DERR spoke to Kevin Okleberry, SLVHD, who was in route to the scene. At 13:52 FD Dispatcher reported their teams thought the odor was coming into the building via the ventilation system from the nearby Huish detergent facility at 3540 West 1980 South.  Also a newly received shipment of silk at the clothing facility may be a cause of the odor.   At 15:23 Kevin Okleberry reports crews at the scene have determined the source of the odor is likely the recent shipment of silk, as the odor is primarily in that area and other workers in the facility were not affected like those working nearest the silk.

name: Hill AFB SSO
incident_summary: Today @2:26p DWQ received a call from a Mark Roginske (801-775-3651), from the environmental office @ Hill, to report a sanitary sewer overflow from the sewer collection system on the base. The overflow was discovered in an abandoned area of the base by a jogger last Friday, but not reported to the authorities until yesterday about 5:00pm. The overflow went into a storm drain, then to a "Stormwater Pond 4" which eventually overflowed to a storm drain which leaves the base and follows Hwy 193 to the west. The overflow was due to an obstruction in the line and was stopped and the overflow from the pond this closed-off this morning about 9:00a. Preliminary estimates are that about 100,000 gallons were released to the storm water pond since being discovered on Friday. The base took samples from the middle of the pond and the outfall to determine if wastewater was discharged. They will have results tomorrow and will report them to us on Monday, in their 5-day written report. They also contacted the Davis County HD, who may also sample, and DNR Wildlife Resources to advise of possible contamination of wildlife areas around the lake. We'll consider what enforcement action may be appropriate after receiving the 5-day written report and consulting with Davis County.

name: Box Truck Release of a Flammable
incident_summary:
Incident was reported by UDOT worker at 10:00 to Moab FD.  UDOT employee reported observation of liquid spilling from a seam in the trailer at the front right corner.  Futher investigation revealed that the liquid is flammable and toxic (per MSDS: (a) material is identified as "MA-844W CnF® Additive";  recommended use "oilfield chemical"; (b) distribution of weight %).  Personnel attempted to catch as much liquid as possible, however several hundred gallons had already spilled to dirt on the shoulder.  Spill was covered with dirt to minimize vapors.  PRP contracted a cleanup company out of SLC that arrived at 18:00 (7/2/13).  Contractor is planning on removing all contaminated materials and soil for shipment back to company.  Expect to complete this work today. 

UPDATE per NRC report: 16 totes in a tractor trailer.  Driver was trying to avoid a collision causing totes to shift forward.  Some totes cracked causing spill of UN1993.
title_eventname: Box Truck Release of a Flammable

name: Laundry Sup. Co. (Craig Reaveley) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Two 10,000 gallon UST's were removed from responsible party's property on 4/4/96.  The tanks were used for Perchlorethylene (a.k.a. tetrachlorethylene) storage.  During removal no odors or signs of leaks were evident.  Soil and water samples were taken and results came back on 4/15/96 with .35 to 11 ppm PCE in 3 of the 4 soil samples and 22 and 180 ppm in the water samples. Water samples were from seepage into the excavation.  The excavation was backfilled after removal of tanks because there were no obvious signs of contamination.  The tank removal contractor (Westech) had apparently reported this to UST/LUST shortly after sample results were received. The contamination is expected to be restricted to the shallow aquifer.  There are some drinking water wells within a mile radius of the site, but are apparently deep wells (1100 feet). The UST facility ID # is 4-000508.  Tanks were pulled from underneath the parking lot for the site.
title_eventname: Laundry Sup. Co. (Craig Reaveley) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Roosevelt Manure Truck wahsout to creek
incident_summary:
Attached is the email report submitted by Scott Hacking
Darrin and I witnessed this incident firsthand late yesterday, at approximately 4:30pm.  Photos with captions are at:
https://picasaweb.google.com/105377044848809547245/WintertonTruckingSpill?authuser=0&authkey=Gv1sRgCIfr7LCw8tmdCw&feat=directlink
Attached is a Google Earth placemark showing the location.  This occurred on a small tributary to Dry Gulch Creek, just west of Roosevelt.  Darrin and I were driving by on US-40 approximately 4:30pm yesterday (June 5th) when we saw a cattle hauling truck to the north of the highway that had backed up to the small creek and was obviously being washed out.  We turned off the highway to investigate and found that a Winterton Trucking cattle hauling truck was in the process of being washed out into the small creek (see photos).  The water coming out of the truck was heavily laden with manure and it was inundating the small creek with manure and probably ammonia also (from the urine).  We observed dead and dying minnows in the small creek directly downstream of this, where the small creek was choked with manure.  We talked to a representative of the trucking company that was present and told them this activity was not allowed, and they agreed to stop the activity.  Apparently there had been several cattle trucks washed out at this location over the course of several days, in addition to the truck we observed being washed out.

No water samples were taken, as it did not seem necessary given the firsthand observations.  Any sample collected would have contained a heavy fraction of solids, due to the heavy manure load in the creek that this event caused.  The creek immediately downstream was more of a manure slurry than water.  I think we could sample this location for weeks to come and see the negative effects.  Please advise if you want us to do that.

Wintertons do own the land where this incident occurred.  It is open to public access, and there are no gates; there is direct access off of US-40.

As you know, Darrin sent an email earlier today recommending an NOV for this incident, and I agree completely.  Downstream this incident probably killed on the order of a hundred minnows, and it will negatively impact the creek for some time to come.  The amount of manure being washed out totally overwhelmed the small creek, and it will probably be many months before the Creek and its associated ecosystem can recover.  This was also a very blatant incident, occurring adjacent to the Roosevelt City Limits and only about 150-200 yards off of US-40.
title_eventname: Roosevelt Manure Truck wahsout to creek

name: Quality Inspection & Testing, Inc. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported a that a truck hauling radioactive material overturned along Highway 40.  Initial reports indicate that the material breached the containment.  An unknown liquid and powder material surrounds the crash site and EMS workers may have come into contact with these materials.  Jeremy Raymond (Uintah County Fire Dept.) is on-scene and awaiting meters (Geiger counters) to survey the area.  DERR contacted Bill Craig (Division Radiation Control - DRC).

UPDATE 1 10/24/10 08:54:  Bill Craig (DRC) reported that the truck rolled just west of Vernal on Highway 40.  The radiation source did NOT breach containment and there are NO exposures resulting from the incident.  The radiation source is owned by Quality Testing and they are on-scene working with local Emergency personnel.  The source is Iridium 192 and is intact.  I do not have the destination information for the source but the radiation source is a device used for strength-testing metals in production wells and welds in other metal components. Bill indicated these devices and their radiation sources are designed and secured during transport to withstand high impacts during accidents.  The driver of the truck was reportedly drunk at the time of the crash and he was removed from the scene by ambulance to treat injuries from the accident but was not exposed to any radiation. Bill Craig (801) 565-1129 (home phone) has been in contact technical support and providing with the On-Scene Coordinator - Duchesne Fire Chief Jeremy Raymond.  Gwen Galloway (DRC) home phone: (801) 964-2035 has taken over technical support duties and may visit the scene later today to provide regulatory oversight for handling of the source.  All indications are that the situation is now under control.

UPDATE 2 10/24/10 10:02:  Liquid material involved in the spill appears to be a dilute bleach solution used in the development of images taken by the device.  A contractor was hired to provide clean-up of the solution as well as any diesel released during the accident.
title_eventname: Quality Inspection & Testing, Inc. (Null RP Substituted)

name: Flash Flooding at Carbon Power Plant
incident_summary:
Brett Shakespear called to make notification that at approximately 14:00 hrs today a flash flood event caused a discharge to the Price River. Currently PacifiCorp is in the process of closing the Carbon Power Plant, as part of this work they are closing doing final closure work on the coal ash landfill. This entail installing cover materials and erosion controls. They have a storm water retention pond that was designed to collect run off from the landfill and was sized for a 100 year storm event. During construction activity they installed a culvert that was to divert water around the landfill. The flash flood over came the culvert, ran across the landfill cap, and overwhelmed the basin, discharging to the Price River. The water did erode cover material and coal ash and discharged it to the river. PacifiCorp is working on a sampling plan to identify how far the ash might have flowed. They will prepare and submit a report within five (5) days detailing information on amounts moved, and repairs made. 

The Price Drinking Water Plant has been notified, and they are upstream/impacted by the release. 

The ash has a tendency to settle quickly as water velocities drop.
title_eventname: Flash Flooding at Carbon Power Plant

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Small amounts of mercury were discovered on the parking lot and sidewalk at the Vernal Middle School.  Cause is unknown.  Local Health Dept. and Fire Dept. have responded.

Response: I have contacted the EPA who in turn will talk to the Tri County Health Dept. about the situation.  If necessary, the EPA will hire their contractor -E.R.- to perform the cleanup.

09:12 TRI-County contacted DEQ again after learning of the possibility and availability of a mercury vapor meter.  
DERR sent some preliminary documentation with mercury info to the health dept.

10:20 Tri-County informed DEQ that an EPA OSC will mobilize to the school to render assistance.  Tri-County is currently evacuating the school.  Free mercury was not observed at the entrances used by students.  Free mercury was believed observed near where the cooks enter the kitchen.

11:30 by JD Keetley: Craig Meyers (303-312-7166), OSC with EPA, informed me that he has sent the EPA responder, David Romero (303-884-1236) to Vernal along with the EPA contractor, URS.  They are driving to Vernal from Denver and should arrive there in a few hours.  Any questions on the response can be taken up with them.  I’ll update things as necessary. – JD

8/25/06 Update by JD Keetley: The EPA and contractor URS arrived in Vernal Thursday night and the cleanup is underway.

Friday morning (8/25/06) I received an inquiry from Richard Gee with State Public Safety and Darren Brown with Tri-County Health Department regarding State regulations or guidelines for the cleanup of mercury inside the Vernal school.  I told them we have guidelines that are based on the U.S. EPA’s guidelines taken off their website.

After conferring with other DERR personnel and with SLVHD personnel who have had experience with similar situations, I called back Darren Brown and advised that the usual cleanup level for mercury in ambient air is 3,000 nanograms/cubic meter for a commercial building and 1,000 nanograms/cubic meter for a residential building.  I added that a public school would be better off to make the cleanup level 1,000 nanograms (1 microgram).

Darren told me they had already made that decision and were going ahead with that cleanup level in mind.  He said the highest readings on their Lumex machine have been around 400 - 500 nanograms and that staying under 1,000 nanograms should not be that difficult.

There was still some uncertainty as to whether the cleanup would address the cafeteria workers who had possibly tracked the mercury onto their shoes and into their cars and homes.  If the EPA demobilizes after cleaning up the school only, then the Tri-County Health Department would be left to handle the monitoring and cleanup of the workers’ personal clothing and homes.  Since the County does not have a Lumex meter, they would ask DERR’s assistance in doing this since we do have a Lumex meter and trained personnel to use it.

As of 11:00 am Friday, no decision has yet been reached regarding the potential cafeteria workers’ mercury contamination.  -  JDK

Update & Summary 8/29/06: Thursday, August 24, 2006:  Mercury contamination was discovered in the parking and inside the building at the Vernal Middle School due to an anonymous phone call in the morning.  All students, faculty, and staff were dismissed from the school.

Initial notification of the incident to UDEQ/DERR was received Thursday morning around 8:30.  The situation was discussed with both Richard Gee at Utah DES and Darren Brown with Tri-County Health Department.  At 9:00 am, Craig Meyers with the U.S. EPA was contacted.  Craig later informed that he had mobilized their contractor, URS, and his field OSC, Dave Romero, to go to the site.  They arrived in Vernal late in the afternoon and began initial assessment and cleanup of the site.

It was estimated about 3 tablespoons of mercury had been spilled outside in the parking lot, and school employees later tracked the mercury into the building.  Mercury vapors were detected inside the school building.  The contractor ventilated the building, began clean up the mercury using special vacuums, and prepared to remove the contaminated flooring and carpets if necessary.

Friday August 25:  Cleanup levels for the mercury spill were discussed.  An “action level” of 1,000 nanograms/cubic meter (n-gm/m3 or 10-9 gm/m3) of mercury vapor in the air was set.  The contractor used a Lumex meter to measure mercury levels as cleanup of the school interior and the outside parking lots and sidewalks progressed.  Most levels inside the school were found to be less than 500 n-gm/m3, while outside levels of 1,000+ n-gm/m3were measured.

School was still not in session during the cleanup.  Meanwhile, the State DOH and the Utah Poison Control Center had been getting calls from concerned parents and doctors in Vernal about the spill.  The issue of the cafeteria workers’ possible mercury contamination on their clothes, homes, or cars was brought up.  In the afternoon, the EPA, the URS contractor, and the Tri-County Health Department offered employees of the school who feel they may have come into contact with mercury to have their clothes, shoes, cars, etc tested for mercury.  It was a voluntary offer, and EPA/URS would be in town all day Friday for it.  One employee came to be tested, and had her car tested for mercury levels.  The car’s levels were below action levels.  It was felt this car was the one most likely to have been exposed to mercury since it had been parked in the area of the spill in the parking lot.

By Friday evening, the cleanup was mostly over.  All contaminated materials were placed in bags and secured for the weekend.  The contractor continued to ventilate the school overnight and planned to come back in the morning to test the ambient air levels.  

Saturday August 26:  When the contractor returned to the school in the morning, the highest level of mercury measured was 250 n-gm/m3, found in the janitor’s closet due to an initial attempt to cleanup the spill himself.  Throughout the rest of the building, all rooms were tested and found to be at acceptable levels.  Outside, levels of 1,000 n-gm/m3 were still detected so the contractor applied MercEx (?) to the sidewalk: sprinkling finely powdered sulfur or zinc on the spill site to bind any remaining mercury so it can no longer vaporize.  All cracks and crevices in the sidewalks were then sealed with caulking.  When the sidewalks were tested again, results showed levels below 200 n-gm/m3.

The EPA and URS returned to Denver Saturday afternoon.  The contaminated materials from the cleanup were double-bagged and placed in a steel container which was later moved to a vacant, secure 5-acre lot owned by the Health Department.  The contractor took samples of the contaminated material to deliver to a laboratory in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, for analysis to determine if the material is hazardous.  When results come back, URS will return to Vernal to retrieve the container and dispose of it in an appropriate landfill: either Subtitle C or D depending if the material is deemed hazardous or not.  The material will be hauled off within a week.

Monday August 28:  Health Department personnel met with school officials and verified that everyone is satisfied with the cleanup.  School is back in session and there are no further issues of concern.

For any further information on this incident, please contact J. D. Keetley with UDEQ at 801-536-4130 or at jkeetley@utah.gov

name: Drill Rig Fire
incident_summary:
A drill rig fire resulted in the release of between 25-100 gallons of hydraulic oil to soil  The soil is next to a private enclosed pond but no sheen was observed on the pond.  Envirocare will be on site in the morning for site cleanup.

>>> On 9/7/2012 at 11:35 AM, Lewis Hastings <LHastings@co.wasatch.ut.us> wrote:
The responsible party is Dave’s Drilling, Dave Cullilard, 74 Kamas East, Marion, UT 84036; phone # 801-599-0361.

Release details:  The release resulted from a fire started when a hydraulic hose on a drill rig failed spraying hydraulic fluid onto the turbo.  The drill rig held approximately 500 gallons of hydraulic fluid and about 200 gallons of diesel.  By the time the fire fighters were able to arrive on scene the drill rig was fully engulfed and the emergency release valves on both tanks had ruptured to release excess pressure.  Based on the conditions of the fire, it was determined that the best course was to let the fire consume the rig and burn as much of the fuels as possible and monitor it so that it doesn’t spread to the surrounding environment.  The fire chief and responding firefighters estimated that most of the 700 gallons of fuel (hydraulic oil and diesel) was consumed by the fire; however, they estimate that less than 200 gallons of the fuel was not consumed and did enter into the environment.  Based on my observations, I think that estimate is high but that is what they reported to me.  The fire department contacted EnviroCare to come out to remediate the scene.  They are working on getting a work authorization signed by the RP and insurance information and then they will get to work.  I have discussed the cleanup standards with them and told them that they would need to meet the 500 mg/kg TPH level as required by water quality.

name: Injection Water Release
incident_summary:
The caller reported that 692 barrels of injection water was released over the course of the day.  In jection water is a mix of treated production water and fresh water.  The caller stated that their equipment allowed them to determine that the 692 barrels was made up of 512 barrels of fresh water and 180 barrels of treated production water.

Their current plan is to dam the stream and flush the spill from the source to the dam with fresh water.  The water will then be sucked from the dam area and disposed.  The dam will eventually be removed and the stream allowed to flow again.

name: Hills Brothers Chemical (Null RP Substituted)

The spill resulted in the highway being covered in salty looking thin residue for about one mile.  Puddles of the material could be seen at the side of the road.  Samples of the liquid were identified, by field testing, to be a liquid mixture of MgCl and CaCl.  The tanker spilling the material was then located.  No driver was found.  From information off the truck, the owner company was identified and the material identification confirmed.  Nathan Guinn with Water Quality was then contacted who indicated that, because of the thin nature of the residue, cleanup would not be required.

name: Heavy Truck Salvage (Russ Emery) (Null RP Substituted)

Caller has also observed PRP burning materials.  PRP has developed a salvage yard and activity has been increasing over the last five years.  Caller has observed PRP gather clean dirt to cover contaminated areas.  Calller stated that the area is not zoned for certain other salvage-related activities off- & on-loading flatbed trailers.  There are several culinary community and irrigation supply wells nearby.  Caller's well is within 250ft of the property.  

Additional Info: Area is zoned for agricultural/residential (not salvage activity).  Photos are available.  PRP smooths over dump areas in attempt to conceal.  Wells may be part of Autry Water System.  Evidence that salvage property is Quit-Claimed through various names on intervals as short as 48 hours.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller received call from SSLFD inquiring about how to handle the fire suppression water accumulated from an all night 6 alarm fire at the Smurfit-Stone facility.  Some estimates suggest about 2 million gallons of water is flooding the storage area of the plant and surrounding areas.  Steve Beach called the DEQ duty officer to informed DEQ of the situation.  DWQ was informed and asked to advise Steve Beach.  DWQ asked the DERR duty officer to relay to Steve Beach that fire suppression water is exempt from regulation, but suggested the water be strained or filtered to hold back the ash and larger particles from passing to the discharge point.  DERR has learned that the Region 8 EPA OSC was consulted also.  As of Monday 9am, July 19, 2004:  Sample results indicate the water is neutral ph-7.0, and does not contain any solvent or hydrocarbon compounds. The water has been cleared for discharge to a nearby canal.  The company (Smurfit-Stone) has asked for bids from some environmental contractors to handle the clean-up

name: Sewer line backup - 4 residences - Elk Ridge

Four residences are currently affected.  The Elk Ridge Public Works Dept has vacuumed the lines and completed some investigation with a camera, but it is still unknown what is stopping the flow and where.  It is believed that the sewer line may never have connected properly to the gravity-fed section of the sewer due to abandonment of a manhole.  The city's Public Works have contacted a contractor and are developing a strategy to remedy the problem.  The local drinking water supply is not believed to be affected, but lies about 440 lateral feet from the location.  No secondary water supplies are believed to be affected.
title_eventname: Sewer line backup - 4 residences - Elk Ridge

name: Holly Refining & Mrkg (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: The Sulfur Recovery Unit (SRU) interlocked three times over the past weekend.  Permit limitation for the release of sulfure dioxide is 500 lbs/day.  The facility changed to a different type of amine used (D.E.A. to M.D.E.A.) in the Amine Unit.  The amine unit has been foaming; theoretically this should not be happening.  They are attempting to identify the cause: hydrocarbons in the system(?), or differences in characteristics of M.D.E.A. vs. D.E.A. (?) and the impact these differences may be having on the system.  They are also going to try an anti-foaming agent from the vendor.  The upset in the amine unit causes a slug to pass to the SRU, which upsets equilibrium of the latter causing permit-limit excesses.

name: Fresenius POC Jim Earl (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported that employees at the Ogden Nature Center noticed a distinct petroleum odor last night as they were closing up.  Odor was reported outside the Education Campus at the Center.  Today a visible sheen and distinct red-colored petroleum product were observed in a canal that runs through the front portion of the Center.  The canal is reportedly a run-off canal for the City of Ogden and flows in to Mill Creek.  Caller stated he would attempt to determine if diesel has entered in to Mill Creek.  County engineering was notified of the spill and Bill Reyns (WMHD) will attempt to visit the site later today.

UPDATE 14:51- Followup correspondence, DWQ is making inquiries.  Weber-Morgan Health Dept. (WMHD) notified UDEQ of concern for consequence management.  Water body is identified as the Plain City storm water canal.  Canal flows adjacent to the Ogden Nature Center. WMHD and local Fire Dept. are on-scene investigating to determine the source to include the Business Depot Ogden (industrial center, formerly the Ogden Defense Depot).  In addition, WMHD reports evidence of sewage and suspects potential alternative unregulated point-of-discharge.  Ogden Nature Center employee reports that the sheen extends for 1/2 mile downstream.  Rreport of wildlife (deer) observed with legs stained red was noted.  Area is within Marriot-Slaterville municipal jurisdiction of the Ogden-Metro area.

UPDATE 12/14/07
08:59 WMHD through Weber Co. LEPC Emergency Manager - the spill originated from Fresenius. Estimated volume of release 200 gallons - #2 fuel oil.  09:45 Weber Co Emergency Management reports Fresenius will assume liability cleanup. USA Enviromental has been contracted.  11:10 UDEQ DWQ will participate in coordination and oversight.  The release resulted when a crew ruptured a 2-inch line on an AST.  A storm drain is in close proximity within several tens-of-feet away.  Ogden City Safety & Environmental Coordinator will have direct involvement.
title_eventname: Fresenius POC Jim Earl (Null RP Substituted)

name: Sinclair Service Station (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
The reporting party owns the Cove Health and Fitness Center on Wasatch Blvd.  He has been leasing the facility for 18 months.  A Sinclair service station is located adjacent and immediately west of his business.  He reported that for the last 18 months, every time a tanker truck fills the underground fuel tanks for the service station, gasoline vapors make him, his staff, and his customers in the fitness center dizzy and ill.  His customers frequently leave his business when they begin to smell the gasoline vapors while the underground tanks are being filled.  He said when the tanks are being filled, the gasoline vapors persist in his business for approximately two hours, then eventually dissipate.

The caller thinks the gasoline vapors are entering his place of business through the air conditioner system that is located on the roof of his building.  He has asked the service station owners to have gasoline delivered to the underground tanks when his business is not in operation; their response has been that they need to operate their service station as they see fit.

name: South Ogden Center For Family Medicine (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: South Ogden Center For Family Medicine
incident_summary:
Caller reports it was discovered this morning by a resident physician that a wall mounted mercury blood-pressure cuff device has broken.  The physician observed mercury on the carpet beneath the device in the examination room.  The physician attending to a patient at the time of the discovery is pregnant.  She decided to exit the facility based on concerns for her infant.  Personnel deployed the use of spill kit including collection syringe and powder absorbant/binding agent.  Personnel DO NOT know when the cuff actually broke.  Facility personnel removed the device from the wall and moved it to the facility bio-hazard room.  The device was placed on the biohazard trash can, double-bagged and sealed.  DEQ has dispatched a team (w/ Lumex) to investigate.

UPDATE 2/23/06: Al M. Jones and Neil Taylor responded to the release site at about 3 p.m. February 22.  Lumex monitoring of the medical center found mercury vapor air concentrations as follows:

Ambient air in the exam room where the mercury was spilled-36,520 ng/m3.
Hallway outside the exam room-8334 ng/m3.
Nursing station near spill location-11,170 ng/m3.
Exam rooms 1 and 2-approximately 8000 ng/m3.

Bill Reyns with the Weber County Health Department was present on site and was fully involved in decision-making. DEQ representatives recommended that the western (contaminated) portion of the clinic be professionally cleaned until mercury vapor concentrations were below the ATSDR recommended mercury standard for commercial locations, which is 3000 ng/m3. The only cleanup contractor found to be available at the time was Environmental Restoration.  The cleanup contractor was on-site by 8 p.m. 

Cleanup followed the standard protocol for mercury spills. Portions of the carpet were removed.  Contaminated areas of the clinic were heated to greater than 100 degrees and vented.  Al Jones was present throughout the night to monitor the cleanup progress.  This morning (February 23), Al Jones reports that concentrations in the clinic have been reduced to around 200-300 ng/m3.

Bill Reyns will be on site this morning.  Al will conduct a final sweep of the clinic with Bill present to document that satisfactory cleanup has been obtained.

FINAL UPDATE, 2/22/06: The Weber-Morgan HD rep, Bill Reyns, arrived at about 08:00.  The affected exam room had just finished another round of carpet cutting and removal (removing the source of fumes) plus heating and venting to the outside.  Bill and DERR surveyed the building taking Lumex readings at the same places the original survey had logged contaminated Hg air.  All readings were well below the 3000 ng/cm, the base line for the clean-up in a business setting.  The building/clinic is large, with 5 Dr's and 3 PA's and a lot of family practice patients.  The practice manager was given the okay by Bill that they could use all of their facilities as of 0830 this date.
title_eventname: South Ogden Center For Family Medicine (Null RP Substituted)

incident_summary: At the Chevron North Salt Lake Refinery, process waste water was discovered to be leaking from the underground junction box which connects the de-salter unit with the NPDES treatment system.  An unknown amount of waste water leaked before discovery, although it was observed there was at least 50 gallons in the hole by the junction box.  Water was measured to have 25-30 ppm benzene.  Leak is on-going, water is re-routed to the NPDES treatment system.

name: Rocky Mountain Power (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that a release of oil from a transformer on 08/22/11.  Response crews responded to the scene and cleaned up the release. The laboratory analysis for samples collected from the excavated soil detected PCBs at 464 ppm.  Confirmation samples were collected and submitted for analysis to insure that no PCBs reamin in the excavation.

name: AMOCO (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Approximately 5 gallons of K050 (heat exchanger sludge - a listed hazardous waste) spilled onto soil in the refinery at the heat exchanger cleaning pad.  The RQ on the material is reportedly 10 lbs.  The spill was cleaned up by 1500 hrs. on 7/24 and is being stored temporarily on the site pending shipment to an incinerator.

name: US Welding (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports a release of lime slurry to the storm drain by-passing the storage tanks. This is reportedly an on-going problem despite upgrades to the system last year.

UPDATE: 4/8/04 Gordon Lund of the SLVHD conducted a site visit.  Gordon found no slurry overflows in the storm drain(s).  He advised them on their record-keeping practices.  The matter has been referred to Tom Rushing of the UDWQ.  The company plant manager is Ted Omagoshe, 973-9082.  The company suspected the complaint was from a disgruntled employee, who has now been fired.

name: Pacific States Cast Iron (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that a fill-valave on a tank failed causing the tank to overflow.  Tank contains a mixture of water and 2% soluble oil.  Mixture overflowed tank and entered a nearby storm drain.  Material was captured in a series of catch basins within the storm water system on-site and was not discharged off-site.  Dan Griffin (DWQ) was contacted by the responsible party at 07:30.
title_eventname: Pacific States Cast Iron (Null RP Substituted)

name: Hallaburton
incident_summary: A 42 gallon drum was punctured by a fork lift. A chemical called emulsifier ran into a storm drain collection area. A drain pipe had been installed which allowed it to run onto a neighboring property to the North.

name: Coal Truck Rollover near Price
incident_summary:
Jason Llewely reported 
We just had a Semi Truck Rollover on SR 6 MP 238 at approximately 10:30am today,  just north of Castleview Hospital. 
It’s a Barney Truck Company Coal hauling tractor – trailer. Vehicle left the roadway and has spilled an unknown amount of oil/diesel fuel into the Price River. Best guess is 12-25 gallons total release. Semi is currently still in the River. Work crews, UHP and County Hazmat on scene along with Price Fire responders.
Company officials are on site and in the process of contacting a clean-up company to mitigate the spill.
Soctt Hacking Forwarded an update.
I am going to take a look at it now and will grab a water sample if that is justified. Dave is in Utah County at a meeting and coming back soon.  Not a lot of diesel released initially (10-25 gallons) so sampling may not be necessary, but the truck is apparently still in the river and there is still some danger of a larger release from the fuel tanks.  They are going to pump out the tanks before it is moved (according to Jason Llewelyn).

name: West Valley City - Diesel Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a 50-gallon diesel spill after a truck driver hit road debris and the passenger side saddle tank ruptured.  The spill impacted a storm drain.  A clean-up contractor is en route at this time and will be there at about 6 p.m.  Caller notified the NRC (incident #1134255).

name: Petroleum Impacts in Soil & Groundwater
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting petroleum impacted soils and groundwater (sheen) they discovered during replacing a pipeline in the area.

They are adjacent to railroad lines and surrounded by refineries and a bulk distributor.

The source is unknown.

Dominion contractors have collected soil and groundwater samples for analytical analysis.

name: 10 gal diesel spill in Ogden
incident_summary: Truck oil pan puncture released about 10 gallons of oil to the facility parking lot.  The insolated the spill with socks and absorbed the oil with kitty litter.  A sheen remains on the parking lot due to snowfall.

name: Uintah County -- Produced water release
incident_summary: 30 barrels of production water were released from an injection pump.  Material was captured in containment and did not leave the pad.  All liquids have been recovered.

name: Paint in Drain - SLC
incident_summary:
As reported to the NRC:

Caller reported a neighbor dumped paint into a drain near their residence.

name: Nestle USA - Foods Div. Inc. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: 80 gallons of hydraulic oil spilled at process plant, about 11:30pm last night.  Answering service received call from Nestle's at 2:12am - did not require an immediate call back. The hydraulic hose(s) on a freezer developed a leak; material entered the process sewer drain.  Expect an almost full recovery (approx. 99%) from process plant.  Spoke with Mr. Mattinson this morning - incident concluded and treatment plant cleaned up.
title_eventname: Nestle USA - Foods Div. Inc. (Null RP Substituted)

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that the subject property is identified as the lot adjacent to her business and it is showing an accumulation of unknown wastes.  The subject property is not secure and it has been subject in the past to dumping.  The subject property was the site of a recent fire.  Per description received today via telephone, the property owner was contacted in the past to remove wastes and was compliant in removing them.  Reporting party said new wastes have appeared.  Wastes include a gasoline can, four residential sized propane tanks, and one industrial propane tank described as being five feet tall.  The fire dept. investigated the gasoline container and determined that it it filled with water.  Caller described seeing tires on the property as well.

name: Western Zirconium (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Process upset - slop tank overflowed 100 gallons, Zirconyl Chloride was released, pH is less than 2. Neutralized and placed an elementary neutralization system with sodium bicarbonate.

name: BONNEVILLE PUMPING (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: ILLEGAL DISPOSAL OF GREASE DOWN SEWER AND BEING SHIPPED OFF SITE   REFERRED TO SALT LAKE COUNTY HEALTH         SUBSTANCES RELEASED: GREASE AND OIL

name: Warner Enterprises (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Tractor was involved in a 12 vehicle accident on I-15 southbound exit 318 Bountiful.  Tractor lost diesel fuel.  Fire Dept. has placed sand on spilled fuel.  Wrecker service has been dispatched to the scene.

14Feb05 UPDATE - PRP stated that Warner representative from Nebraska mobilized to the site but was unable to gather much information (by arrival most activity had been completed).  An estimated 30 gallons was spilled.  PRP stated that an agency/contractor did clean up the waste, but they are still investigating to identify.

name: Rocky Mountain Power (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that a car hit a transformer which caused 25 gallons of mineral oil to spill onto soil.  A sample has been sent to the lab.  The soil was excavated.  No waterways were impacted.

name: Utah County - Mercury
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of approximately 1/4 to 1/2 cup of mercury outside the home (503 South Nebo Drive) near the cobblestone stamped pathway near the driveway.  Beads were observed to cover an area about 6' by 6'.  They confirmed that they had not tracked through the area and if they had the items would be segregated and left outside.  Potential options for cleanup were discussed.  UDEQ was contacted based on a referral from Poison Control.

name: Sureline Transport (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Westbound I-80, jackknifed semi-truck.  50 gal diesel fuel spilled.  Lincoln Environmental doing cleanup.  Not near surface water.  Summit Co. is coordinating spill cleanup.

name: Salt Lake Co - Diesel spill
incident_summary: UPRR Intermodal Yard - yard crew discovered leaking diesel from a refrigeration trailer.  Spill has impacted 15-20 foot area around the unit.  Spill to snow and soils.  There are no drains nearby and none are impacted.  UPRR has a call out to Pacific West contractor to respond and remediate.  Caller will be making notification to UDOT and NRC.

incident_summary:
