name: Accurate Construction and Excavation (Wade) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Driver was delivering a load of exploration &production (RCRA exempt E&P) filter press waste to ECDC.  Material was being hauled in tandum truck with a pup.  Tow bar on the pup failed and the pup ran up against the hillside and tipped.  PRP estimates three to four yards of material was spilled.  Fire Dept, Sheriff's Office, UHP, and UDOT were on-scene when rep for PRP arrived.  Cleanup was completed last night.  Post excavation samples were collected.  Caller requests cleanup standards.  Waste is a dry waste from residual condensate and produced water generated from oil & gas operations.
title_eventname: Accurate Construction and Excavation (Wade) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Pool Chemical Spill - contained in trailer
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a small release of an algae control inside a tractor trailer at the YRC Freight yard.

The terminal personnel noticed a strong odor coming from the trailer and called Lincoln Environmental to investigate.  It was discovered a carton of algae control bottles were leaking but not getting outside of its box.

No release to the environment - all chemical contained inside a box inside the tractor trailer.
title_eventname: Pool Chemical Spill - contained in trailer

name: Salt Lake County Railroad Spill
incident_summary:
The caller is reporting a spill of 5 gallons of lead carbonate which is also called white lead.  The spill is confined to the railroad ballast and no water bodies or drains are impacted.

The cause of the spill is unknown at this time.

The spill is near the intersection of State Road 202 and State Road 201.

The Union Pacific hazmat manager is on his way to the scene and will be contacting a cleanup contractor.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Unknown white powder reported on I-15 milepost 25 North bound.  UHP requested DEQ assistance to identify the material.  Field Hazcat testing indicated the material was cement.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller believes there may be sewage emerging in the grass of the complex.  Dogs drink the fluid and have been throwing up and having diarrhea.  

UPDATE 14:57 from DWQ - Eagle Mountain City investigated sewage access points and found nothing unusual.  The city believes the excess water may be from the sprinkler system.

name: PIONEER PIPELINE (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: OVERFILLED SUMP UNLEADED GASOLINE 10 BARRL

name: Pioneer Refining Services (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: At approximately 6:45 a yellow plume of smoke was noticed going 400 - 500 feet into the air from Pioneer Refining.  After visiting the site at 7:10, the smoke immediately stopped.  The plant manager (Jerry Eldredge) indicated that they had processed a batch of silver with a lot of steel wool in it, and that is where the smoke was coming from.  It appeared to me (Jim Thiros) that one employee went into the scrubber area just before the smoke disappeared.

name: Salt Lake County - Mercury Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a broken mercury thermometer at their home.  The thermometer broke in the kitchen in the presence of several children.  The mercury was not vacuumed or swept while cleaning up.  A piece of paper was used to collect the beads into a Ziploc bag.  It was suggested that the homeowner identify other clothing items and place them in a garbage bag outside.

name: Coredor Trucking-Owner Jorge Corder (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A semi truck trailer broke a fuel crossover line while traveling north on I-15 near St. George.  The driver stopped at mile marker 3 or 4 and attempted to patch the line.  The truck continued to the K-Mart receiving dock at 745 S. Bluff Street.  The entire load of diesel fuel (approximately 150-180 gallons) was lost on the route.  The truck traveled over a sewer manhole and A St. George city employee was called to check the sewer for any fuel-none was found, but the UHP HazMat has requested that the sewer be checked again.  Also, a concrete-lined waterway is in the parking lot or in the path the truck traveled.  City employees placed sorbent booms over the drainage, and the trooper did not believe that any product made it to the waterway.  UHP Case #110001770.  The trucking company had called their contractor, H2O Environmental to remediate the spill and they were expected at scene @ 1:00 P.M.  UPDATE:  Wayne Thomas, district engineer, checked the drainage from the K-Mart parking lot to the Santa Clara River and did not find any evidence of product in the sewer.  He reported that some fuel entered the drainage ditch, but could not estimate the amount, and found no evidence of product after it entered the channel.  He estimated that a total of 60 gallons of fuel was released.  The absorbent booms.  The city workers had placed in the drainage had been removed by 12:45 P.M.
title_eventname: Coredor Trucking-Owner Jorge Corder (Null RP Substituted)

name: Algal Bloom - Bear River - Corinne
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a suspected algal bloom on the Bear River at the Corinne boat ramp.

name: Beaver - Trucking Accident
incident_summary: Caller reported a trucking accident resulted in the release of motor oil, antifreeze, and diesel.  No other details were known at the time of call.  Environmental Restoration (contact Jay Peterson 801-856-7184) was contracted to provide spill clean-up services.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported a noticeable electrical burning/general burning odor in one room of their house.  The odor usually occurs between 7-9 PM in the family room and has lasted for the last week and a half.  Caller reported concern because she has a 3 year old son.  Caller did mention that Public Utility work crews have been working on a sewer line near her home.  Yesterday the work crews told her not to use her water while they worked on the line.  DERR suggested the odor is likely sewer gas that have crept back into her home, but someone from the SLVHD could visit the home.  Caller said she will talk with one of the workers tomorrow but may contact the DERR to see if the SLVHD can come for a visit.

UPDATE 4/18/07 14:30:  Rolf Larsen (SLVHD) contacted the homeowner, Ana Ovieo.  She told Rolf the smell is an electrical burning odor.  Rolf's concern is that the odor is from an electrical short in her house's wiring.  Rolf set up for her to contact the Local Fire Dept. when/if she smells the odor tonight.  The Fire Dept. will inspect the situation.

name: Maverick Country Store, #260 (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Truck driver was filling underground tank with regular gasoline. Flapper valve closed and gasoline spilled onto the asphalt and conrete.  An estimated 30 to 50 gallons was spilled.  The store personnel boomed and diked the spilled gasoline to some extent. A "small quantity" of the gasoline got into a storm drain.  The Castledale Volunteer Fire Dept. responded and did some response and clean up activities on the site.  The fire dept. is billing Maverick for about $1,300 for their services.  Weissenborn advised that incident is  being reported late because he has been out of the office.

name: Chad Cornaby/Cornaby Railing (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller relates that upon returning to Utah, after several months away, the owner of the property at the back of Scott's 2.5 acre lot has started to operate a business (Cornaby Railings) wherein steel is sandblasted and painted.  The residue of the sandblasting (a black residue or dust) blows across Scott' pasture, piling up several inches in depth.  Scott has cattle etc on his property.  Other neighbors are complaining about black residue also.  Scott has asked the Cornaby owner (Chad Cornaby) to control the dusting, but he has not.  The business started last December.

UPDATE:  3/22/04, a sample of the residue migrating to Scott's property was brought to DERR's office, this date, by Steve Alder of UCHD.  DERR has an XRF unit and the sample was scanned.  The results reported are : Lead @ 624 ppm, Arsenic at 111ppm, and Mercury at 59ppm.  Other metals were below SCDM benchmarks (Superfund Chemical Data Matrix).

name: Petroleum spill in North Salt Lake
incident_summary: In the process of removing piping associated with the removal of an AST, gasoline was discovered in the piping trench. The piping has been removed and samples collected. A consultant has been called to asses the extent of contamination.
title_eventname: Petroleum spill in North Salt Lake

name: 9 Mile Canyon -- Dirt, garbage and debris in creek
incident_summary: Reporting party says gas companies have built two dirt platforms next to the creek at Harmon Canyon and Cottonwood Canyon for the purpose of loading water onto trucks.  The platforms are repeatedly scraped and graded which allows loose sediment to wash into the creek.  There is garbage and small oil spills on and around the platform areas.  In at the Harmon Canyon location the creek bed appears to have been altered.
title_eventname: 9 Mile Canyon -- Dirt, garbage and debris in creek

name: Provo - UPRR Diesel Release
incident_summary: Caller reported that a valve failure resulted in the release of an unknown quantity of diesel fuel at the Union Pacific Provo Rail Yard.  Diesel released through a drain an into a containment structure. Union Pcific HazMat coordinator (Jacob Hammer) is enroute with a clean-up contractor.  No storm drains or surface waters were impacted by the release.

name: UPDATE:West Valley City -- Cleaning compound spill
incident_summary:
A 55-gallon drum of non-hazardous "cleaning and scouring" compound fell out of a truck and broke open, releasing its contents into the gutter and storm drain.  A cleanup contractor has been contacted.  WVC Fire HazMat and Salt Lake County HD Emergency Response are on site.

UPDATE:  John Hoggan reports product is an organic acid solution with a pH of <1.  Material ran at least 400 feet in a drainage ditch.  Discharge was diluted by heavy rain storm which passed over the area shortly after the spill.
title_eventname: UPDATE:West Valley City -- Cleaning compound spill

name: Abandoned Oil Pipeline Leak - Escalante
incident_summary:
Caller forwarded an email with photos (attached), stating an old abandoned oil pipeline is leaking oil onto Dixie National Forest land that is migrating to his property  He stated the area is located in the Upper Valley Creek Watershed that is part of the Upper Escalante River Watershed.  

The caller has notified DOGM, DWO, Dixie National Forest, and others. They are working on identifying the pipeline owner and determining the quantity of oil released.  It is believed to be only a few gallons at this time. 

From callers email -
The old pipeline which was "drained" in 1988 is leaking residual oil from cracks in the pipe. It is leaking into an intermittent drainage on Dixie National Forest land just downstream adjacent to the east border of my property, which lies between MM 46 and 47 on the south side of Byway 12 west of Escalante, UT.

The spill seems to have started this March 2019. I included pictures from before and after I patched it with duct tape. 

You can view the pipeline on pre 80's topo maps.

Thanks,
Russell Carpenter
Adjacent Property Owner
360-477-8699

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Reporting party received anonymous call.  Caller reports suspicion that a large amount of oil may have been dumped to the ground or a hole and burined as recently as this morning.  Caller reports material was gone overnight.  PRP is alleged a separate company occupies and leases the east part the Great Basin Engineerring facility at the address given.  Caller did not provide business name.  Facilty is next to Mosquito abatement.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Abandoned materials found to the side of I-15 milemarker 186 near Scipio.  Ammo box with red phosphorus, black powder, aluminum powder, lamp black and other containers of unknown materials.  Books on bomb making and obtaining false identification found a distance down the road.  The sherrif did not want to leave the materials near the road, due to safety considerations and has taken the materials to an outdoor, fenced storage area in Filmore.  District engineer is unavailable to assist.  Neil Taylor will be in the area and will assist in the identification of those materials which can be easily and safely sampled.  Right now, the best option for disposing of the sealed containers seems to be detonation.  That and other options are being considered.

name: Juab Co - Tractor Rollover
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a tractor trailer rollover I-15 southbound at milemarker 217.  Trailer is placarded under Hazard Class III -- Flammable Liquids.  It is unknown at this time if an actual release has occurred.  HazMat is enroute w/ ETA 2 hours.  Fire Dept is on-scene.  Vehicle is blocking one lane and remainer is in ditch.  Reporting party is attempting to contact driver for get shipping information.

name: Salt Lake Co - Nitric Acid
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of an estimated one gallon of nitric acid.  Trailer contains cargo including two 55-gallon drums of nitric acid.  Personnel discovered each drum with approximately 0.5 gallons on top of the drum.   Cause appears to be a faulty cap on each.  All acid was contained by the top of the drum and remains inside the trailer.  No impact to environment (trailer, soils outside the trailer, etc.).  Lincoln Environmental is on-scene and will overpack the drums.  Materila spilled did not migrate from off the tops of the drums.

name: Rocky Mountain Power (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that Rocky Mountain Power excavated a leaking underground transformer from his property.  Caller stated that oily contaminated dirt was placed back into the excavation.  Caller has registered a complaint and received a work order with Rocky Mountain Power but has been unsuccessful in getting a response.  RMP Work Order is 56E1713.

name: Not Reported (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Estimating-3-5 tons Sulfur Dioxide released to air.  Release of aluminum silica-based catalyst from Fluid Catalytic Cracking Unit (Cat-Cracker) that makes gasoline.  Electrostatic precipitator went down causing temporary Cat-Cracker shut down.

name: Cardinal Freight Carrier (Null RP Substituted)
address: Exit 99 of I-80, and State Highway 136
address_location: Exit 99 of I-80, and State Highway 136
incident_summary:
A Cardinal Freight Carrier tractor-trailer semi truck developed a fuel leak, resulting in a spill of about 100 gallons of diesel at the TA Truck Stop, exit 99 of I-80, the Tooele-Grantsville exit.  The spill occurred in the parking lot of the truck stop.  The Tooele County sheriff's office was notified, and a deputy came out to the site.  

Response:  Cardinal Freight notified Cura Emergency Services who then contacted the TW Company.  They used absorbent pads to clean up the spill, and a "vac-jet" was brought to finish the cleanup.  Cura will send us a cleanup report.

name: Logan
incident_summary: Caller reported he needed to make emergency repairs to a mobile PET scanner at Logan Regional Hospital.  License is 1331107-01.  Calling due to radiation source in the scanner.

name: Chevron (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Flaring release of SO2 that was not previously reported to the SERC.  Will also be incorporated into a followup letter to be issued.

name: Davis County - Sulfur Dioxide
incident_summary: The caller reported that hydrocarbons overwhelmed the sulfur recovery unit resulting in the release of sulfur dioxide greater than 500 pounds. The total quantity released is undetermined but initial measurements indicate an exceedance. The Davis County LEPC has also been notified.

name: Trinity Industry Corporation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports a fire at the facility resulted in a release of 12,500 gallons of a 10-11% sulfuric acid solution to a secondary containment.  No injuries were reported.  The local FD responded.  The fire started in one of two polypropylene tanks and partially damaged both tanks.   Consultants with a vacuum truck have been contacted to remove the spilled material.  A report will be sent to DEQ.  The facility is Plant #33 and the manager is Stuart Craig.  The facility manufactures guardrails and the sulfuric acid is used in the pre-treatment process prior to galvanizing the materials.

name: Wermer Trucking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 50-75 gallons of diesel to the soils on the side of the road.  Lincoln Environmental was contracted and secured the release.  Utility locates will be done on Monday (2/8) and the contaminated soils excavated on Tuesday (2/9).

name: Knight Transportation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Road debris punctured a fuel tank on a semi truck.  About 25 gallons was spilled on I-15.  Lincoln Environmental is cleaning up the spill.  The local health department is on site.

name: neighbor (Null RP Substituted)
address: north side neighbor of 562 Grace Ave.
address_location: north side neighbor of 562 Grace Ave.
incident_summary: Caller reports that their neighbor on the north side was working on a car engine in the yard.  Used oils, anti-freeze were drained and allowed to run down into a nearby storm-drain.  Caller believes storm drain may discharge to a retention pond behind her development, which is inhabited by waterfowl.  Caller contacted local police who instructed neighbor to put down sand over puddled oils.  After police left the scene, the neighbor used a garden hose to again wash residues down the storm drain.

name: Norman Fife (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
The reporting party advised that the responsible party (Norman Fife) has hauled a great deal of materials of various kinds onto his property at 915 West 1500 North (Swede Town) in Salt Lake City.  Materials on the property include several mobile homes (in disrepair), batteries, used paint containers, large blocks of Styrofoam (from former UDOT projects), and inoperable "electric trucks".  Mr. Fife reportedly purchases a "lot of stuff" from surplus sales at Hill Air Force Base.  Fifty 5-gallon black buckets ("with skull and cross bones on them") were hauled onto the property in the past few months and loads of broken roof trusses were hauled onto the property last week.  The caller believes the mobile homes on the property are being used as storage facilities for some of the materials brought onto the property.  The caller is concerned that the materials on the subject property represent a tremendous fire risk to his property and neighboring properties.  The caller also reported that Mr. Fife has unlicensed trucks and trailers parked on the public street near his property.

The reporting party also advised that a second property in Swede Town, at 878 Everett Avenue, is entirely filled with wooden pallets to the extent that the pallets obscure the dwelling on the lot and completely cover a truck parked on the property.  The caller thinks the pallets on this property also represent a severe fire hazard.

name: UPRR (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a small leak in a rail call caused the release of a small amount of soda ash.  Quantity released was unknown at the time of call.  No waterways impacted.

name: Tesoro Station (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A call was received by Paul Zahn at UDERR/LUST from Debbie Anderson concerning vapors in her home located at 868 E. 1300 S.  She lives in the bottom of a four-plex at 868 E. 1300 S. in SLC.  She reports that vapors have been in her basement and home for past 5 days.  She has lived next door to a Tesoro station (UST Facility ID - 4000765) for five years and this is the first problem.  The vapors seem to be coming from an area in the basement below ground surface and seem to be getting worse.  She was at work, but could leave work to meet people there.  The site is on the PST fund and the site was referred  to Mike Pecorelli of the UDERR/PST section to followup and contact her.  He will be performing site visit today at 2:00.

name: Transformer - Car accident
incident_summary:
Caller stated that a car hit a power pole and knocked the transformer off causing a release of 30-40 gallons of the transformer mineral oil - NO PCBs.  The mineral oil migrated into the gutter and storm drain and into Barton Creek. 

Bountiful City Power immediately contacted Envirocare to respond and begin abatement measures.  Envirocare is currently in the process of cleaning up the release.  

Caller stated he also notified Davis County Health Department.  

I asked that the caller notify the NRC and provide a report number when available.

name: Parley's Canyon Crude Oil Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a crude oil spill of approximately 105 barrels onto the freeway after two semitrailers crashed near the Lamb's Canyon exit in Parley's Canyon.  The spill occurred in the early morning hours when temperatures were freezing so the oil was conglomerated and stayed mostly in one place.  As the day warmed up, the crude started flowing into a ditch and storm drain but by then, booms had been placed and an earthen dam was built to prevent the crude from entering Parley's Creek.  Because of the rapid clean-up response while the crude was conglomerated, the impact to Parley's Creek was minimal.  Surface water samples have been collected by DWQ and are being analyzed.  The RP has been instructed to report the spill to the NRC.  The spill site on attached map is approximate.

name: Salt Lake City - Sheen in Ditch
incident_summary:
Caller stated that Tesoro Operators were doing an inspection around the refinery when they observed a light sheen in a ditch along Warm Springs Road.  Once the operators confirmed the source of the sheen was not from the Tesoro property they notified SLC Public Utiliies dispatch to report it.  Greg Archuleta (SLC Public Utilities) responded and placed a boom inside the ditch to contain the sheen.  SLC Public UItilies inspected the area but could not identify a source.  WIll return in the morning (10/24) to follow-up. 

UPDATE - Received a call from Will Snarr, Tesoro Env H&S manager, 801-528-2009.  Tesoro does not believe they are the source of the sheen but they are assisting SLC with finding the source and sampling.  The source appears to be coming from the bottom of the canal and a sample was collected.  SLC public works should provide further updates and details.  (Morgan Atkinson)
title_eventname: Salt Lake City - Sheen in Ditch

name: Payson -- Sewage line overflow
responsible_party: Payson City Waste Water Treatment Plant
incident_summary: A main sewer line is blocked and sewage is overflowing.  Sewage treatment plant employees have been unsuccessful in clearing the blockage so they are planning to do a bypass until the problem is fixed.

name: Yard Maintenance Co. for The Vintage Condominiums (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Yard Maintenance Co. for The Vintage Condominiums
incident_summary: Caller reported yard maintenance company spraying the rocks for suspected weed control (golden color liquid - herbicide).  Excess spray coming off of truck was draining into the gutter and into the storm drain which leads to the Virgin river.  Caller was concerned about potential impact to the Virgin River and general area.
title_eventname: Yard Maintenance Co. for The Vintage Condominiums (Null RP Substituted)

name: Chevron Refinery (Null RP Substituted)

UPDATE 25 Oct 2005 14:00 - DEQ received information from Chevron of pending subsequent notifications.  In a Consent Decree signed between EPA and Chevron, the latter has agreed to review historical records and file notifications with appropriate agencies for past incidents pursuant to the terms of the Consent Decree.  At this time DEQ has received a total of 22 NRC reports.  Each report is a notification for the release of the chemical Nitric Oxide.  The amount of Nitric Oxide released ranges between 12 to 569 pounds.  Sixteen reports show a range between 12 to 97 pounds, with most being in the 20 to 40 pound range.  Five reports show release amounts of 160, 258, 300, 407.4, and 569 pounds.  Fifteen reports indicate that emissions from the refinery flare due to refinery upset.  One report reflects that emissions from the refinery are due to process unit shutdown.  All NRC report numbers are comprised of six digits; the first 3 digits for all reports begin with 777 as shown in the first number provided below. name: EP Energy, Brine Release,
incident_summary:
Late Wednesday evening a call came in from a land owner that he had found a salt water leak on his property, the night lease operator and production supervisor met with the land owner and went to the location and found the salt water line south of the Brotherson 2-15B4 had developed a leak 2000 feet south of the location.
The leak was in the crossing of a dry wash, the water ran 150 yards down the wash and was contained in a catch basin.
The pipe line is a 2 7/8 steel line wrapped with black tape and fiberglass lined.
The line was exposed and found to have external corrosion.
The line will be repaired and hydro tested.
Calculator 5 and 6 was used.
90 bbls was spilled

Line break spill point GPS:  557199E; 4461018N
Wash berm or end point:     557297E; 4461049N
(berm or dam constructed by surface owner to catch rainwater)


Photos of spill indicate backwash fluid level was several feet above the bottom of the wash some thirty feet west of the line break or spill, which leaves me to believe the volume of water is much higher than reported.  The landowner told the operator there was water already in the bermed area below from the rains and so EP Energy reduced their original report of 300 barrels to 90.  I believe the operator did recover three loads of spill or spill/rainwater from the bermed area below which was between 240 to 300 barrels of fluid.  There was no trace of oil in the spill area.  When Scott Hacking and I returned on a second visit the bermed area still had six inches of fluid or more, which either was left or was water that had drained from the saturated soils of the wash.  The landowner was contacted and EP Energy promised to send DOGM a contact number.  The operator explained that the landowner claimed a spring was present in that wash, but I could not find a (for sure) stream flow at any point and would have to make another trip after the wash drys out.

The odor made many people nauseated.  At least 10 persons were transported to local hospitals.  It is thought the cause of the odor was an upset at the Chevron Refinery.

The epoxy material remained contained to the buckets with some material bubbling over on to the flooring.  No storm drains or waterways were impacted. 

Onyx Environmental was contacted to conduct cleanup.  Under normal conditions, the hardened epoxy is disposed as solid waste.  Onyx is reporting that the burned epoxy material will be containerized and disposed as hazardous waste as a precaution (Onyx operates their own haz-waste landfill in Henderson, CO).  Keith Larsen (BRHD) requested a copy of waste manifests prepared by Onyx to ensure proper disposal.

name: Reynolds Brothers Construction (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports that he lives along a single lane road in a rural portion of Ogden.  A nearby alfalfa field (25-30 acres) is currently being converted into a non-paved bus parking lot in preparation for the Olympics.  The above noted construction company began work at 07:00 hours this morning (Saturday) with numerous pieces of heavy equipment (belly dumpers, excavating equipment, paving roller, etc.) travelling past his home.  The caller stated that he has respiratory ailments and must sleep wearing a C.P.A.T. unit in combination with oxygen.  When the project was first initiated, the caller spoke directly with the contractor with a request to mitigate dust, etc.  Caller acknowledged that the construction crew has a water truck, but it is not necessarily begin deployed to locations off-site.  

Activity begun today has produced a significant volume of dust which has blanketed the interior of the household and outside items - their vehicle was named as one example.  Activity is also contributing as significant amount of diesel exhaust that has been introduced into the home via the swanp-cooler.  Both are a source of discomfort and frustration to both the caller and his spouse.  For these reasons the caller has elected to temporarily close all windows and forego use of the swamp-cooler until a solution can be found.  Caller stated that during conversation with the construction company, it was related to him that the parking lot is to be completed with road-base material, however, it will remain unpaved.  Furthermore, once the Olympics are finished, the uncapped roadbase will be left in place.  Hence, this material has the potential to become a source of residual windblown dust that may prove to have a negative impact on his condition.  DEQ advised that the local Weber-Morgan Health Dept. (WMHD) would be contacted.  There was add'l discussion about use of the water truck along off-site routes, and to determine efforts to mitigate the exhaust, if alternative routes to the job-site exist.  These ideas could be shared with a responder.  

10:18 DEQ contacted the caller to inform him of applicable Air Quality regulations as summarized by DAQ.  The DAQ dust rule as it applies in the Ogden area states that within Ogden City limits, track-out dust at a property boundary cannot exceed 10% in attainment areas (in common terms, if there is visible dust, likely this exceeds 10%).  If so, this constitutes a violation.  While speaking to the caller he reported that minutes prior the vibrations created from a passing roller machine knocked a hanging picture and a clock off the wall.  DERR inquired and determined that the caller is within Ogden City limits.  DAQ also indicated that a representative could be dispatched on Monday to determine if activities require additional attention.

DEQ left a message with Reynolds Bros. with a request of consideration to DAQ rules as stated above.  At about 10:30 WMHD contacted the DEQ duty officer to inform DEQ that a WMHD representative would respond to the call.

name: Unknown
incident_summary:
Caller stated that the neighbor performs vehicle repairs in a shop located in his back yard.  The caller's yard and the neighbor's share a common boundary with the he caller being on the down gradient side.  The caller alleges that neighbor has various buckets of oil and other debris that he believe is contributing to the demise of grass and trees along the common boundary.  The caller has taken photos of the area.  The caller alleges that the situation has been on-going for about 2 years but has gotten worse.  The Pleasant Grove police have been notified.  The caller stated that ground water is shallow about 2 feet below grade.  The caller believes there are several municipal wells and artesion sources in the area as well - the caller named nearby Anders Park as one location with an artesian source just east of the rodeo grounds.

UPDATE 9/23/02: Per request, DERR contacted the complainant - caller provided add'l followup info. Caller stated that PRP is also engaged in commercial vehicle paint work in an old building with large openings - it is not an approved paint booth.  Caller stated that paint vapors are affected their (caller's) yard plants and observed white paint residue covering garden plants.  Caller alleges that structured used were constructed without proper building permits.

name: Salt Lake County Anonymous Complaint
incident_summary:
The caller stated that in one of the two buildings at the facility there are six "chrome tanks" containing chromic acid. The facility has temporarily removed the tanks and is currently in the process of shoring up the concrete underneath the tanks.  According to caller, the concrete under the tanks has been degraded (eroded or corroded away) down to the re-bar, and there is water coming up from underneath.  The caller is concerned that the acid from the tanks has corroded the concrete beneath the tanks, and that therefore chromic acid has leaked into the groundwater.  The caller stated that the facility will be pouring new concrete soon to place the chromic acid tanks onto.

In the building near the chromic acid tanks, there are seven grinders where parts, some of which are chromium plated, are ground.  The machines use a mineral oil-based coolant, and sludge from the grinding process is collected in a tank associated with the grinders.  The sludge is then shoveled into containers (cans or barrels).  The containers of sludge are then simply placed into the dumpster and are picked up by the trash hauling company.

Additionally,  in the second building at the facility, there is a honing machine that is operated similarly to the grinding machine.  Honing oil and metal shavings make up the sludge, and this material is handled in the same manner as the grinding sludge.

Drippings from parts removed from the chromic acid tanks go back into the chromic acid tanks, and sometimes a brief rinse of the parts is performed over the tanks.  However, to prevent too much water from getting into the tanks, parts are also put onto a cart and brought to the wash bay located on the east side of  the building where the tanks are located.  The parts are then washed there, and the rinsate goes into the drain in the concrete pad.  The caller made no mention of a sump or where this drain leads.

The company does employ an environmental company to remove old chromic acid from the chromic acid tanks.  The tanks are then recharged with fresh chromic acid.  However, the practices listed above still occur.

The caller made no mention of POTW discharges or neutralization of any discharges.  The caller had no information on whether that occurred at the facility.

The caller provided two names: Bruce Ward - President and Mike Bush - Chrome Shop Manager.

Caller suspects that the integrity of an 8 inch gasoline line may be compromised.  The line passes between Tesoro and Chevron. Next action is to excavate the line for inspection.  Hydrocarbon product has been observed in a nearby sump.

UPDATE 6/4/02 13:30 from Tesoro - Quantity of piping and inherent risk has made excavation activity very slow.  Using VAC trucks (capacity 4500 gallons/truck) crew has collected 5 volumes.  Mixture collected is 5 - 50% gasoline (depending upon who you ask).  Volume is being deposited to Tesoro wastewater treatment where the hydrocarbon is recovered and placed back into crude tank.  Six roll-off units are on-site to collect contaminated soils.  Crew has not yet located leak.  They've checked the site perimeter and it does not appear any product has yet left the site.  Will call as add'l info becomes available.

UPDATE 6/6/02 - Tesoro reported that the line causing the leak has been determined although not yet entirely unearthed.  The line in question is under Chevron refinery authority.  It is an effluent line that operates between a catalytic cracker and process product tank and carries "light cracked gasoline."  Aproduct very similar to the line that passes from the Tesoro to Chevron facilities.  An earlier report from Chevron confirms these findings.

The Utah County Health Department requested DEQ assistance in ensuring the contamination had not spread inside the home. Neil Taylor and Melissa Ottley with DERR met Ron Tobler with Utah County Health on-site and monitored inside the house and the couch. Background levels were found inside the home. Levels of about 30,000 ng/cubic meter were found on one of the couch cushions. Levels of about 1,700 to 2,000 ng/cubic meter were detected inside the couch. The homeowners were asked to bag the heavily contaminated cushion in a plastic bag and dispose of the cushion during the newly started household hazardous waste collection day at the landfill. The remainder of the couch will be disposed of in the regular landfill waste.

incident_summary:
The caller stated that a condenser on a machine leaked an unknown amount of Anhydrous Ammonia in an industrial park.  Response:  HazMat crews, Fire, and Police were notified.  300 West was temporarily shut down, and employees in this surrounding businesses were evacuated.

UPDATE:  At 09:45, 05-30-03, UDOT (965-4317 or 633-6218) called DERR and said the ammonia spill had gotten into the ponds below the I-15, I-80, and 2100 South interchange.   UHP has been notified of this, as has UDOT Region 2 Risk Management.  At 09:55 DERR contacted DWQ and left a voice message with this information.

UPDATE 5-30-03 15:49 DERR received notification from Farr-Russell about this incident.  The caller stated that the release began between 22:00 - 23:30 hours 5-29.  Time frame of the release was determined from the cleaning crew's schedule since no odor was noted prior to their departure at 22:00.  A pasteurizer arrived at 23:30 hours and noted a very strong odor that prevented the individual from departing his vehicle.  Response crews shut-down the freezer feed line at about midnight.  The release was caused when a fan blade failed and punctured the evaporator of a freezer.  Liquid ammonia released to a defrosting tray to a line out to the storm sewer.  The storm sewer drains to the ponds located beneath the I-15 & 2100 South system of overpasses.  As noted above the caller confirmed that SLCFD, PD, and hazmat all responded and evacuated nearby businesses.  Facility had not yet determine the volume released.  FD flushed storm system to remove hazardous material.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller in Ferron complained of odors coming from an oil/gas well right in the town about 1/4-mile from her house.  She said the well had recently been activated since about one month ago.  Odors were irritating the lungs, causing her to cough and feel sick.  She said the odor was similar to the smell of the refineries in North Salt Lake; not , apparently, the rotten egg smell of hydrogen sulfide (H2S). 

Response: I called Dave Ariotti (District Engineer w/Southeast District H.D.) and Gil Hunt (w/DOGM) who said they would investigate it.

UPDATE 9/12/07 from Gil Hunt: Bart Kettle of the Utah Division of Oil Gas & Mining - Price office - visited the well site near Ferron yesterday.  It is a recently activated oil well that does emit some petroleum odors which he could no longer smell once off location a short distance.  He also went to the Ferron City offices.  They told him they have had some other odor complaints and it would be on their City Council meeting agenda for September 27, 7:00pm.  His H2S detector did not register any detectable level of H2S.  Apparently there are other houses closer to the well than the person's home that originally called in.  Neighbors said the smell is worse in the evening.  Mr. Kettle plans on re-visiting the site in the evening to check it out.

It is believed at this point that it is probably no health problem, but rather a nuisance issue.  The well operator has apparently been in communication with city officials.  DOGM has no regulations concerning nuisance complaints.  It would probably be best if the operator can work with city officials to agree and mitigate the problem if necessary and economically possible.

UPDATE 9/14/07: Bart Kettle w/DOGM sent the following report today:

He stopped in at Ferron last night, mainly around the Ferron Creek No. 2 well and also briefly at the Pan Am No. 3 and J Lemon No. 1 well.  He could smell what he believed was the odor from the oil off location along the county road to the east 500'.  He drove along 400 West and caught a real faint whiff of the oil odor right along the dip where Ferron Creek intersects 400 West.  No H2S readings were detected anywhere.

Bart thought it possible people in Ferron living along 400 West are able to smell a strong odor from the well under the right conditions.  In his opinion it is probably the oil they are smelling, and he was not sure much can be done to change the situation.
 
All for now.  If anyone needs something more to be done please contact the agency.

UPDATE 9/24/07: Further reported from Bart.  Talked with Steve Alt of NorthStar (well operator) about the issues in Ferron.  I think they are being as proactive as we can ask a company to be on the issue in Ferron.  They have been in discussion with citizens of the area, and listened to their concerns.  Right now they are periodically monitoring the area for gas concentrations (apparently as is the Ferron Fire department) and are in the process of developing a charcoal based unit to further address odor concerns.  They have already got a flare stack in place and are keeping fluids hauled off site to the best of their ability.  

Concerning noise issues which have recently been added to the complaints I'm fielding, Steve informed me they anticipate changing the lift system out from the current 10' stroke Weatherford V8 driven system to a 30' stroke pumping unit which will be a hydraulic ramp driven by an electric motor.

name: Cuiqiong Xie (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller made notification of a broken mercury thermometer in an apartment of a student housing apartment complex located on/near the University of Utah campus.  SLVHD requested field assistance in assessing the release.  DERR will respond to render assistance in coordination with SLVHD (DEQ has the capability to provide mercury vapor monitoring using a LUMEX mercury vapor analyzer).  

UPDATE - DERR performed preliminary monitoring of the appartment.  Mercury vapor concentrations were collected which exceeded action levels indicative of moving the residents to an alternative living space as a prudent action.  Latent levels in the bedroom (after intial entry into the room was made and the door had been opened) ranged between 11.29 ng/m3 to 33.72 ng/m3.  Readings collected from outside the room prior to entry and opening of the door were slightly higher (the condition wherein the door is closed for a period of time serves to allow the accumulation and concentration of mercury vapor).  Results prompted DERR to notify the EPA OSC on-duty to discuss options, etc.  

In coordination discussions with EPA recommendations were made to the property owner to remove the tile carpet in the room in which the mercury was released and bag and monitor personal items to determine disposition.  The U. of U. administrative personnel were able to provide a temporary alternative apartment.  EPA motioned to delay a federal response pending additional information on local (PRP) resources that may be available to perform cleanup.  Additional recommentations were made to the resident to dispose of several personal items, a vacuum, the bathroom plastic garbage can (w/ contents), and a comforter and several wash-clothes which were bagged during the intial response.  With appropriate concent of responding agencies, SLVHD performed removal of the carpet tiles.  Post action mercury concentrations resulted in levels hovering at the action level.  DERR returned to the site on 9Feb06 to initiate additional mitigation with cycles of heating & venting.  After several cycles, ambient concentrations collected in the appartment and bedroom were found to be below the recommended residential action level.

name: Thatcher Chemical (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: SO2 emissions out of stack exceeded conditions under approval order (50 ppm SO2 over 2 hour period).  Main scrubber is fed sodium bisulfite in order to capture SO2.  If the pH is greater than 6.5, then emissions will be at 20ppm SO2.  If pH drops below 6.5 SO2 concentration emissions will increase.  Upon startup of scrubber, pump that regulates Sodium Bisulfite feed to scrubber - and hence the pH - was not operating properly and therefore pH was not maintained above 6.5.  This occurred for a period greater than 2 hours prompting a reportable breakdown.  Normally, under such conditions the process is shutdown, however, it is yet to be determined why the operator did not do so.

name: Book Cliffs Pipeline Release
incident_summary:
Hector Monteroso noticed the spill when driving along the county road to his lease on another parcel of trust land.  The easement for the pipeline is held by Slate River Resources, LLC, 418 E Main, Vernal, 84078.  The easement was approved in February of 2006.  It is described as an 8-inch natural gas gathering pipeline that transports gas from wells in the Agency Draw area to market.  It crosses trust land in Section 2, T13S, R20E, and terminates in Section 35, T12S, R20E, where it connects to another pipeline.

David Hackford of DOGM visited the site Tuesday morning at approximately 9am, and he reported that the 8-inch diameter pipeline was leaking a small amount of natural gas under relatively low pressure, and that some condensate liquids had leaked out of the pipeline and covered a small area of ground near the pipeline.  Dave called Slate River's contractor (the "pumper", not sure who that was) and told them to fix the leak ASAP.  

SITLA staff (Sonja Wallace, Jim Davis and Scott Bartlett) and I also visited the site at approximately 11:30am on Tuesday, and found things as Dave had described.  The contractor had not responded yet to fix the leak, but it was raining at the time and weather was a factor in getting equipment to the scene.  The leak was small and not too serious, due to the low pressure in the line at the time.  The condensate spill was very localized, as Dave had described.  We did not collect any samples due to the very localized nature of the condensate spill, which had only run about 5 or 6 feet from the pipeline.  The spill is small and should be very easy to clean up.

Surface water was not affected, the nearest would be Willow Creek, which is over 3 miles away from this location.  It was raining at the time, so there was some stormwater runoff.

name: Hildale Floods
incident_summary:
DEM reported floods in Hildale Utah had claimed the live of multiple persons with others missing. State EOC was activated. DEQ was not asked to report to the EOC; however, Ken Bousfield spoke with Victor Jessop, the operator of Hildale yesterday afternoon. He reported that the two spring pipelines were breached before they flow up a hill before flowing downhill to the Town.  DDW discussed sampling and a precautionary boil order. 

Ken sent language for the boil order to Victor in an e-mail. A copy of the e-mail was sent to Robert Beers of the SW District LHD.  Dale Pierson of Rural Water also asked Victor to let him or Greg Johnson with Rural Water know of any equipment or materials needed to restore the system.  Townspeople report the town water is dark brown to black. Samples are being collected and received by SW Dist, HD.

Scott Alvord, the DEM county liason, is coordinating a daily conference call with state agencies involved with restoration activities. Doug Wong and Greg Johnson are also obtaining information about the town's wastewater collection and treatment system.

name: West Valley Report
incident_summary:
Person sent a letter in reporting several posible violations. Letter is logged as DWQ-2014-015919. Text Below.

"I reported on 11/9/2014 to OSHA a violation at the Discover Financial Headquarters located at 2500 S. Lake Park Blvd. West Valley, Utah. 84120. The facilities office contact is David Anderson with Discover Financial 801 902 7000.1 reported the following to OSHA within 30 days of termination and they advised I contact your office personally.

I am reporting that I believe tower waste water continues to be dumped into the roof storm drains which in turn goes into the lake. This was improperly piped to roof drains and corrected when I mentioned the problem, in 2012, but reluctantly corrected after months of being notified. They believe them may continue to dump the tower water into the roof drains from time to time as directed by Dick Morton, the supervisor.

I want to report that for many many years - as long as the PEP filter were installed they had been previously dumping tower water with chemicals that MSDS sheets say are hazardous to aquatic life. You can investigate them if you wish and find out when the PEP filters were installed and how long this occurred and if any penalties are appropriate. 

The practice of dumping tower water into the roof drains was also a regular occurrence at their UPC facility in West Valley. You may want to inspect that also. It has been fixed, but for some time drains were left to dump on the roof."

address_location: 740 W. 1700 S., Salt Lake City, Utah
incident_summary: Complainant reports approximately 30 gallons of a "white, oily substance" has been discharged and has pooled in the parking lot of an industrial complex.  No responsible party has been identified.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City -- Unknown Liquid Discharge

name: Logan - Cement Truck in Waterway
incident_summary:
Caller reported that a cement mixer truck working on a job site for a waste-water treatment plant tipped oer into a canal.  The truck landed right-side up in the canal so no cement is currently discharging into the canal. The area was bermed off to prevent migration of potential contaminants. Caller did not know the name of the canal but it runs on the north side of 200 North (State Road 30).  The canal flows into the Bear River approximately 2.5 miles downstream at the south end of Cutler Reservoir. The work crew on-site did not report a sheen on in the water. Logan City (John Christensen) was reportedly on-scene. Envirocare will be contacted to provide spill clean-up as needed. 

On-scene contact for Geneva Rock is Rodney Fors (520) 247-2024.

name: Transformer Spill - Ogden
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a transformer spill from deterioration.

Approximately 60-gallons of non-PCB oil released to soils surrounding the transformer. 

No Waterways impacted and no other exposures.

Pacific West is onsite excavating impacted soils.

name: Diesel spill at Ogden Rail Yard
incident_summary: Rail yard employee discovered an about 100 gallon spill of diesel fuel and lube oil in a puddle in the rail yard.  Source is unknown. The spill is contained and will be cleaned up.
title_eventname: Diesel spill at Ogden Rail Yard

name: Production Water Release, Myton
incident_summary:
Underground injection line leaked 18 barrels of water.  Some water ran off the right of way and down a dry drainage about 400 feet.
Clean up crew has been dispatched.  Line will be repaired asap and soil will be sampled after clean up.
Mr. Thayne has reportedly notified BLM, DOGM, and the District Engineer.

name: Davis County Diesel Spill
incident_summary:
The caller reported that a truck driving southbound on I-15 hit some debris on the road that flipped up and punctured a saddle tank.  Approximately 30 gallons of diesel fuel was released to the roadway and some of the soil on the side of the road.  This occurred near the Center Street exit in North Salt Lake.

Envirocare was dispatched to clean up the spill.

No water bodies or storm drains were impacted.

name: Draper - Diesel fuel spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a diesel fuel spill to concrete, approximately 100-150 gallons, when a driver ran over a curb at a loading dock and ruptured the saddle tank.  The spill was completely contained at the loading dock.  No waterways were impacted.  Salt Lake Valley Health Dept. and the Fire Dept. are on scene.  Envirocare has been called for clean-up.

name: Summit County Hazardous Waste Dumping
incident_summary:
This complaint was received by EPA on November 7, 2018.

The complainant stated that he personally observed Robert Wether direct an employee of Terra engineering to bury drums of toxic waste including ,diesel fuel, benzene,industrial solvents at locations which the complainant can identify.

name: SLC - Univ. of Utah - Mercury Spill
incident_summary: During demolition/remodeling work, construction crew observed open containers of mercury in a research lab room, along with unlabeled chemical containers, a container with radioactive labels, and containers marked as "pentaborane" (a highly reactive rocket fuel).  A plumber spilled mercury contained in a pea trap he was removing resulting in a mercury spill to the work area.  Currently unsure as to what containment or cleanup measures have been taken.
title_eventname: SLC - Univ. of Utah - Mercury Spill

name: Wasatch County -- Manure near creek
incident_summary: Property owner has placed several large tractor loads of manure next to Center Creek.  Wasatch County HD responded and verified presence of manure next to creek.

name: Cache County Sewer Overflow
incident_summary:
The caller stated that a sanitary sewer overflow occurred at a lift station due to problems with a force main.  The sewage flowed into some grasses on the lift station property and covered an area approximately 10 or 12 feet by 40 or 50 feet.

No water bodies were impacted or threatened by the release.

Caller did not provide the location of the lift station and subsequent calls to get the location have not been returned.

Richard Worley from the Bear River Health Department had responded to the site before the call was placed to DEQ.  Mr. Worley told the caller that no cleanup was required and that he would be contacting DEQ as well.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports that diesel fuel was observed pooling in the guter of the intersection just north of the building in which his business resides.  The caller stated that wife of the building's previous owner, last night, observed a truck in the lot of a defunct auto service business located nearby.   Someone is currently attempting to contact the previous owner for more to see if any additional info (name on the truck) can be identified.  DERR asked caller about potential impact to nearby storm drains.  The caller stated that the closest storm drain is located across the street on the south side of the street; the diesel currently remains along the north side of the road.  

09:45 - SLVHD will dispatch to the location to investigate.  SLVHD left a message with the caller.
10:25 - SLVHD dispatched some absorbant material, determined that the road falls under the jurisdiction of UDOT, and notified UDOT.  SLVHD estimated release at 2-3 gallons.

name: Box Elder County - Illegal Septic Sludge Disposal
incident_summary: Owner of the property is pumping out septic tanks and disposing of the waste in the gravel pit.  Although the owner claims to have received approval to use the property for septic disposal from DEQ in the past, it was determined by DEQ that the current operation does not have a valid permit and the facility is not in compliance with regulations.
title_eventname: Box Elder County - Illegal Septic Sludge Disposal

name: North Salt Lake - Continuous Release from Big West
incident_summary: Caller reported a continuous release of hydrogen cyanide from the refinery. Caller reported the facility conducted a one-time stack test from the FCC Unit and observed hydrogen cyanide emissions in excess of the 10 lbs/day limit. Stack tests indicate a daily emission rate of 163 pounds per day.
title_eventname: North Salt Lake - Continuous Release from Big West

name: Duchesne County  -- Produced Water Discharge
incident_summary: Company representative reported a produced water spill of 8 barrels that flowed into a Right-of-Way.  Due to confusion over jurisdiction it was not reported to DEQ at the time of the discharge.  No waterways were impacted.  API #43-013-30082.

name: Salt Lake City -- Industrial storm water pumping
incident_summary: A citizen observed the company pumping a large amount of dirty water from the back of their parking lot into the Jordan River.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City -- Industrial storm water pumping

name: Keller-Strass Oil Co. (Null RP Substituted)
address: I-15 between Bntfl 5th No & Cntrvlle, Parrish Lane
address_location: I-15 between Bntfl 5th No & Cntrvlle, Parrish Lane
incident_summary:
Tanker truck carrying about 7,000 gal. gasoline overturned and burned in the northbound lanes of I-15, south of the Parrish Lane exit (Centerville).  Most of the product burned, some an unknown amount reached a storm drain and issued into a canal.  TW was called and they boomed the canal and are remediating the road side soil and canal area.  Burning asphalt may also have released oil to the soils.  Per followup call from Keller Strass, Davis County Health was on-scene.  Another lead agency is D&HW, Marty Gray, 538-6170.

From NRC Flashfax - Fire Dept., UHP, and Hazmat were also on-scene.  Tanker cargo capacity is 8000 gallons.

name: Com Tech International (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Ultratech = Ammonium hydroxide @ 40%; RQ 1,000 lbs., Ammonium Chloride @ 25%; RQ 5,000 lbs., reacted with hydrogen peroxide that was inadvertently pumped into ultratech tanks. Elgin-Dyer is head of POTW.  He was alerted the incident had created waste water that could affect the POTW.  He sent a sampling team to investigate. 2 tank capacity of 1,600 gal each.  100 gal of ultratech remained in each tank.  Unknown how much discharged from Hydrogen peroxide tanker truck.  Immediate reaction and cloud emerged that set off sprinkler system's eleven sprinkler heads & knocked down cloud.  Driver shut off pumps.  Water amt. was approx. 1,000 gallons from sprinklers.  Squeegied floor and pumped into a tank, pH - 8.3.  Waiting on samples to determine if can discharge to POTW.  In-house spill response team responded, with local fire department oversight.

name: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Line
incident_summary: Caller reported a treated injection water line leak resulting in a preliminary estimate of 35 barrels of treated water (about 50% river water and 50% treated injection water) that leaked off of the pad traveling northeast into a dry drainage. Then traveled approximately 3,000 feet down the drainage. Spill occurred near injection water well #3-36-8-16. Clean-up is underway. Then it will be flushed with fresh water and samples will be collected. The spill occurred on SITLA land and they have been notified. Caller also contacted Amy Doebele (DOGM).
title_eventname: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Line

name: Conway Freight (Null RP Substituted)
address: Hwy 40 Westbound at Jordanelle Overlook/Rest Stop
address_location: Hwy 40 Westbound at Jordanelle Overlook/Rest Stop
incident_summary: Caller reported that 30 gallons of a potasium hydroxide/potassium carbonate solution released from a tote on the back of a semi-truck and entered into a nearby storm drain.  The commercial name for the material is Technisolve 2000 and is used as a scale disolver.  Caller estimated that 10 gallons had entered into the storm drain but was absorbed by sediments in the bottom of the catch-basin.  Envirocare responded by transferring material remaining in the tote to drums and using floor-dri to collect any pooled material.  Envirocare will return to the scene on Friday to remove the contaminated sediments inside the catch-basin.  The release was likely caused by an improperly secured load.

name: Weber County - Asphalt Cement
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of about 75 gallons of asphalt cement mix at the facility near 1555 South 1900 West.  The material is used for asphalt paving for roads.  A trucking company was offloading product and transferred to an unempty tank.  The product will be allowed to solidify and scraped up later today or tomorrow.  No waterways were impacted.

name: Ken Mckey (spelling uncertain) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: The reporting party lives in an unincorporated area of Salt Lake County at 3133 Lambourne Circle (about 2445 East).  The responsible party has a metal garage on his property where he reportedly restores antique cars as a hobby.  The responsible party periodically sprays and/or dumps gasoline (believed to be a waste product from the antique car repair activities) on his property, and was last observed doing this on May 3, 2004.  The reporting party is concerned about the strong gasoline odors that can be smelled on her property and claims that the gasoline has affected her vegetable garden.  The "Board of Health" (presumably the Salt Lake Valley health Department) reportedly visited this site as a result of an earlier similar complaint and gave the responsible party a "warning" about spraying or dumping gasoline on his property. Caller was driving along I-80 eastbound (near mile marker 85) when he observed a Harper Construction fuel truck possibly leaking diesel from the tanker.  Caller reported diesel was spraying from the top of the tanker whenever truck traveled over bumps or potholes, and thought that the inlet cover for the tanker was not properly secured.  Caller reported a strong smell of diesel prior to passing the truck.  No report of quantity released. 
DERR advised caller to contact Highway Patrol to see if they could try to identify and flag down the truck.  DERR contacted Harper Construction dispatcher to advise them of the situation and attempt to identify the truck and driver to notify them of the situation.

incident_summary: 9,660 gallons of peraxylene, constituents include: p-xylene, m-xylene, o-xylene and benzene.  Primarily 90% trimethylbenzene. Discovered it today at noon.  Suspect it has been leaking for several hours.  Storage tank leak, all has been captured by secondary containment.  Secondary leakage should also be recovered via waste-water treatment capture. name: 300 Barrels Produced Water Near Duchesne

The caller said a DEQ representative is on site although the caller could not identify that person. A cleanup plan is being formulated. The APR well unit number is 43-013-33972.

name: Salt Lake Co. Parks & Recreation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Facility operators responded to system sensor alarms at the Salt Lake City Sports Complex.  Facility was evacuated on a precautionary measure.  Fire Dept., Hazmat, and Salt Lake Valley Env. Health  responded on-scene.  The system services two recreational ice sheets.  At the time of notification the release had not been contained.  The facility mobilized ammonia system consultant experts who determined that ammonia began was leaking via a slow (pinhole type) leak into the system exchange brine fluid solution through a rupture in a heat exchanger beneath the ice.  Operators have not yet been able to determine the amount of the release, nor rate of release based on findings of the investigation.  System holds between 3600-4000 lbs.

The PRP is prepared to excavate soils and transport them to facility that is willing to receive them.  DERR contacted the UDOT Hazardous Materials Coordinator.  UDOT indicated that the accident likely occurred within the jurisdiction of the UDOT highway right-of-way.  UDOT will dispatch a regional representative to the site to verfiy jurisdiction and provide oversite and assistance.  DERR coordinated with UDOT to contact the excavation company.  They will strongly suggest that cleanup work commence as early as possible tomorrow (7/2/02) morning to avoid conflicts with anticipated holiday traffic loads and associated UDOT activity.

UPDATE 7/1/02 PM - In an effort to restore - ASAP - normal flow and operation of the highway, UDOT personnel will provide oversite on the cleanup effort to be performed by the PRP.  Work will begin at 7:30 on 7/2/02.  After satisfactory completion, UDOT will proceed with final repairs on the guard rails.

Additional information from Dennis Keith (Davis County Health Dept. – (801) 807-9031

name: Chevron Products Co. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Chevron Refinery had a release Wednesday evening (1/12/05) of hydrogen sulfide (H2S).  A leak developed in a sour gas line at 16:15, allowing the gas to escape.  Bill Oakton with Chevron (801-539-7220) notified UDEQ at 17:45 because the leak was going to take longer than 2 hours to repair.  I was told the gas was dissipating, the line will be repaired, their engineers will come up with some emission numbers for the report to be sent within 7 days, and that there was nothing further they could do at the time.  I notified state Division of Air Quality and the Salt Lake Valley Health Department.

At 20:30 I received a call from Debbie Perrin with the National Infrastructure Coordinating Council (NICC) (202-282-9201), a part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).  They had received notification of the release from the National Response Center (NRC).  Deb asked me about the status of the release and I gave her what information I had.  I gave her the contact number I had for the Chevron refinery if she wanted any more information.  I asked why the DHS would have an interest in this release, and she explained that since the release of chlorine in the train accident in South Carolina last week that caused 8 to 10 deaths, the NICC was taking very seriously any releases of toxic substances that have a potential to impact communities.

About 10 minutes after we hung up, she called me called right back saying she was unable to reach anyone at the refinery, and that all numbers she tried just led to voice message machines.  After several attempts I was able to get through to a live person who was then able to put me in touch with the shift supervisor, Ken Pruett (801-539-7201).  Ken informed me that they had cut production back by about 60% in order to cut back on emission of H2S.  They had roped the area off and were using steam hoses to knock down any gas that was present.  He said that Chevron workers had entered the area, wearing self-contained breathing apparatuses, and had installed a temporary clamp on the broken line to lessen the release.  They had contacted a company in Houston called the Ferminite Company to custom build a box-like clamp to place over the line.  The clamp will be assembled overnight and shipped out first thing in the morning via air freight.  Workers will install the clamp over the line and then inject a gel into the box-like clamp which will set up and seal the leak, similar to an epoxy.  Ken assured me that no gas was escaping from the premises and that there was no exposure to any workers.

I then called back the NICC to tell Deb what I had found out.  She informed me that she had received a call at 23:20 her time (21:20 here) from Paul Hewitt, Salt Lake City Fire Department (SLCFD) (801-799-4231) battalion chief.  Paul had been told by someone at Chevron that the release was of sulfur gas only, which is not toxic and non-hazardous, and the repair was 80% complete.  I then called Paul about this information but was only able to leave a message with Dispatch.  About 15 minutes later I received a call from Mike Barfuss with the South Davis Metro Fire Department (801-677-2400).  He told me he had been in touch with both Paul Hewitt with SLCFD and Deb Perrin with NICC, and had received the same conflicting information about whether the release was only sulfur gas or the toxic H2S.  I told him I was sure it was H2S, having gotten the information from the shift supervisor at Chevron, and I didn’t know how the misinformation about sulfur gas had been reported.  Mike said he would turn all this information over to their refinery specialist, Brent Argyle (801-677-2404), in the morning.  South Davis Metro F.D. actually had jurisdiction over the release.

In follow-up phone calls Thursday morning, Kris Battleson (801-539-7222; cell 801-598-3919), environmental engineer with Chevron, told me the leak was still on-going, the refinery had shut its feed rate down to minimal levels to cut down on the emission, they were expecting the clamp to arrive from Houston any time, and she expected to have the repair completed once it arrives.  She also confirmed for me that the leak was definitely H2S, that no workers were exposed, and that there were no off-site impacts to the public from the release.  Kris said Chevron will file a report within 7 days to the state Division of Air Quality, the LEPC of Davis County, and the SERC.

Kirsten Jensen (703-563-3544) with NICC called me after I had sent her agency an email with a brief update about the release.  I told her what Kris Battleson had just told me about the release and the expected repair, and that the gas was definitely H2S.  I told her there had been no exposure to workers and no off-site impacts.  Kirsten said she would probably notify the Department of Health and Human Services about the release, and consult some chemical specialists about it.  I told her I would send her an email describing the entire incident when I write one up, and to call either Kris Battleson or me if she has any further questions.  The NICC can be reached via email at:  nicc@dhs.gov

I also notified Dan King with Utah OSHA (801-530-6901) about the incident.

name: Chevron Products Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: 5 - 20 gallons of low-sulfur diesel was released during a truck loading operation at the Chevron fuel truck loading rack.  While loading two compartments, the driver mis-aligned the loading arms.  Volume is determined by driver whom enters the volume to be dispensed via a preset system.  Of the two volumes one was greater than the other, and since the loading arms had been mis-aligned the larger volume was dispensed into a compartment of lesser capacity causing an overflow. Driver and personnel used spill pads and speedy-dry absorbant material to contain product.  No diesel left the property and absorbants were containerized.

name: Elpaso Energy (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
From John Isanhart USFS 11/8/11:   Looks like it is mostly cleaned up. The pit has oil in it with a lot of cellulose. It really only went between the well head and pit.. No signs of spillage outside of the pad area. This is a fee well so our jurisdiction is just mig birds and other listed fish or animals. The only listed species in the near vicinity would be Ute's ladies tresses. There are some wetland areas along the road into the well but not next to the pad itself.

The well is in the NENW Sec 3 T 2 S R 3 W. It is labelled the Conover 3-3B-3. 

Update From Scott Hacking:  11/5/2011 - I was at the site today at noon.  El Paso was right in the middle of critical operations to contain the well, so I was not able to get too close to the well head (still a threat of explosion, H2S gas present).  The well was still uncontained but oil was not really shooting up in the air, the oil had been diverted to flow to excavated ponds on site.  As far as I could tell oil was not leaving the site.  El Paso did have a stream of trucks coming and going to truck the oil out of the emergency pits that had been constructed at the site.  The nearest downstream surface water is a farmer's pond about 1/4 mile away.  The first "live" water is about two miles SE downstream (Dry Gulch Creek, which does have water at this location).  There is also a pond that is closer to the NW but that pond is uphill from the site.  The irrigation season is over so the farmer's ditches and the canals do have water in them currently.  It is unknown how deep the groundwater is at the site, but apparently they did not hit groundwater while excavating the emergency ponds.  Dwayne Davies with El Paso is the contact for this incident, he was at the site but was extremely busy with operations to cap the well.  His mobile phone is 435-823-1470, and his e-mail is dwayne.davies@elpaso.com.  EPA was not at the site yet when I was there.  The local incident command system has not been activated, El Paso is in control of the site and has the resources to address the situation.  They have established access control at the site and appear to be dealing with the situation appropriately and with urgency.  A well control company (Wild Well Control) has been brought in to help them deal with the situation.  
 
El Paso has multiple H2S meters at the site and on their personnel.  The nearest neighbor is about 1/8 mile to the west (see photo 16 in background), which is generally upwind but not always (today the wind was blowing stiffly to the east so that neighbor was upwind).  The next nearest potentially downwind neighbor is about 1/4 mile to the NE (see photo 15, the residence is on the right).  There are two other residences to the NW and SW slightly further away.  There did not appear to be anybody home at the two closest residences, they may have been advised to leave by Mike Lefler (local Fire Marshall), but I am not sure about that.  
 
So there appears to be no release to surface water at this time.  There is still some potential for H2S gas release, but measurements so far at the site (according to El Paso) have been low.  The wind is helping disperse H2S from the immediate area.  We should revisit the site Monday or Tuesday (hopefully the well is fully contained by then) for more detailed followup and to determine for sure if the excavated ponds encountered any groundwater. UPDATE 12:25 - Volume released is estmated at three tablespoons on the sidewalk.  Deputy Director Env. Health is on-site.  13:00 LHD rep on-site reports that the mercury was found on a set of wooden stairs on a private building adjacent to a public building.  Most of the mercury is trapped in the wood of the stairs and decking at the top with some observed on the concrete beneath the structure.
UPDATE January 30, 2007  9:10 a.m.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
Darrin Brown reports that the owner of the property Mr."Dennis Judd" will make a decision today as to who will cleanup the mercury spill.  EPA is unwilling to cleanup the spill using EPA funds because the spill is on business property.  Mr. Judd has received several bids for the cleanup, but feels that all bids are too expensive.
