name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
SMELL CALL

At 6:15 pm on Tuesday January 7th, I received a call from Martha Wolf (303-312-6839) at the EPA who had taken a call from Jeannie Parker, an employee at the Continental Reservations office near the Salt Lake International Airport, regarding an odor that had pervaded the building she worked in causing people to feel sick.  I called Jeannie Parker (cell: 801-949-4274; work: 238-4940) and she told me there had been an unpleasant odor at her office building on and off for the last 3 days.  She described it as a “petroleum-like smell,” possibly jet fuel, and the smell was still present when she left work at 5:30 pm.  The Continental Airlines Reservations office is located at 2445 West Jet Way Avenue, south of the Thrifty Car Rental office on 2200 West and south of North Temple.

At 6:30 I called Steve Beach (580-6681 or 231-6905) with SLVHD who said he would contact Salt Lake Dispatch (799-4231), and then drive out to the area.  He thought the smell might be from the three new power generators Utah Power east of their storage area near Redwood Road and North Temple.  The generators run off natural gas and they may be venting gas into the air.

I called Mike Zucker.  We had earlier discussed a call to which he was asked to respond that was received by Steve Thiriot from the Executive Director at the Tax Commission, Rod Marrelli (297-3845), concerning an odor people in that building had experienced between 9:00 and 10:00 that morning.  By the time information of that event reached us, however, it was mid-afternoon and the smell had dissipated so there was nothing we could do.  Mike had also been very active in a series of calls regarding obnoxious odors last month and he had made contact with Bruce Allen (887-0772) at the State Air Monitoring Center (AMC) about a future response to such smell calls and getting summa canisters to the scene to grab a sample of the air if possible for analysis.  See Spill Report number 4743, dated December 23, 2002.

At 7:15 pm Mike met Bruce at the AMC office (2861 West Parkway Blvd/2670 So.) to pick up two summa canisters.  We decided to meet at 7:30 at the Thrifty Rental Car facility, but while waiting there the S. L Fire Department fire truck drove by on its way to the Continental building and I decided to accompany them and assist with the inspection of the premises.  There was no way to contact Mike about this change since the duty officers have not been issued individual cell phones, but hoped they would just figure out that I’d gone ahead to the Continental building.

The fire crewmembers were from Station #11 (596-5251): Randy Montgomery, Kevin Stowe, and another man.  Mike and Bruce showed up with two summa canisters at 8:00.  We walked through large rooms where over 200 telephone receptionists help customers with reservations.  None of us smelled anything terribly bad that would suggest discomfort to a person, only a weak smell of something too faint to identify.  The fire crew left.  Mike, Bruce, and I talked with the Continental managers Regina Peery and Mark Houberg (238-4900), who agreed the smell was like that of “rotten eggs,” sulfur-like, possibly natural gas, and always came in the afternoon/evenings when the wind was from the northwest.  

Bruce carefully explained to Regina and Mark the procedure for collecting an air sample: take off the bronze cap covering the inlet, open (unscrew) the valve to let the vacuum in the canister suck in ambient air, allow this to go on for about 3 minutes, then close the valve and replace the cap.  He also explained that it is imperative they collect samples using both canisters, since they are used to analyze for two different classes of compounds: one is for sulfur compounds and the other is for carbon compounds.  There were a set of instructions attached to the canisters, and a yellow card they are to fill out when they collect the sample giving details on the time, place, wind direction, air conditions, etc.  Bruce suggested that samples be collected when the odor is most acute.  Regina and Mark would call us after collecting the sample and we will pickup the canisters and deliver them to a laboratory.  We left around 9:00 pm.

The next morning (Wednesday January 8th) I had a voice mail message from one of the firemen saying that on their way back to the station last night they could smell a strong odor in the area of 2200 West and 700 North, and he suggested we go there to collect an air sample.  Unfortunately, the message was left at my office phone the night before so by that time it was too late.

Steve Beach called at 8:30 to say that last night he drove around the Redwood and North Temple area near the Utah Power generators and could smell a strong odor at the overpass where Redwood Road passes over I-80, but was not sure where it was coming from or what it was.  He had also observed significant plumes at the Thatcher Chemical plant near 1300 South and I-215.

Mike obtained two more summa canisters for the S. L. HazMat team to use the next time they go out on a smell call.  We invited Steve and Teresa Gray to come with us.  We arrived at the S. L. Fire Department station #6 at 900 West and 800 South and talked with Dan Gish, explaining the purpose of the two canisters and how to collect a sample.  Several firemen suggested we contact Dispatch and ask for a list of calls over the last few weeks to get the data on the time and place such calls were made and see if we could detect a pattern to the movement (and possible source location) of the stench plume.  They said last time the calls began to the northwest near an apartment complex around Redwood Road and 600 South and over time progressed to the southeast around the area at 1300 South and I-15. 

At 11:20 I received a phone call from Regina Peery at Continental saying she had collected an air sample in one of the canisters from 11:10 to 11:15 am.  Regina informed DERR that she contacted the National Weather Service facility, located nearby just north of the Continental building, to ascertain the wind direction and wind speed:  3-4 knots, from the northwest.  Mike and I went there and picked up the canister.  While discussing the issue in Tracey Bartlett’s office (238-4950), the odor was again observed, but not strong enough to justify our taking a sample with the other, unused canister.  We realized the odor was introduced through the HVAC system.

Mike and I then met Bruce Allen at the AMC.  We decided not to run the analysis of the one canister, since it requires both canisters to do a thorough analysis and the one sample canister that was used was for carbon-based compounds whereas it was felt the smell is more likely due to a sulfur-based compound(s).  Plus each test costs about $160.  Bruce gave us a replacement canister for the carbon tests to deliver to Continental.

At Continental, I gave the replacement canister to Tracey Bartlett at 1:15 pm, and gave her a brief review of the sampling procedure.  In a conversation with her, Mike Schwinghammer the facilities coordinator, Cindy Fisher, and Regional Director John O’Brien (538-4900), they all said the same thing: the smell only comes when there is a wind from the northwest, only in winter, and actually was first noticeable last winter.  The first time they noticed it this winter was on Friday, December 13, 2002.  They called the Fire Department who responded and came out but found nothing.  Tracey told me the firemen had told her then that they had received several calls that same day about the same odor.  Unfortunately, DERR had not been notified of all these incidents.  I gave her our evening/weekend 24-hour number (536-4123) for future reference.

The employees said it means a lot to actually see someone on the premises responding to their concerns, and that by doing so we are providing an invaluable service to the public.  I assured her that once we collect and analyze a viable sample of the odor, we could then work on locating the source of the odor and addressing the problem.

At 3:00 pm I called Jeff Tucker (220-2989) with Utah Power and asked him if he was aware of any releases at their new generators east of the intersection of Redwood and North Temple.  He said the generators are what they call “peakers,” meaning they are only used during peak electrical demand hours which are in the morning hours around 7:00 am and in the evening at 6:00 pm especially in the summer during high air-conditioning use and during the Christmas holidays.  Since the generators are frequently turned off and on, they may vent a little natural gas (which powers them) into the atmosphere for a few seconds immediately after being turned off, but it is too small of an amount to cause a problem, especially to buildings as distant as Continental.

At close of business day on Wednesday, January 8th, the following possible explanations of the smell had been offered:
-Seeding the airport runway;
-De-icing the planes using ethylene glycol (anti-freeze), especially if they capture it in retaining ponds or tanks after use and prior to disposal or re-use; one theory also includes the possible addition of mercaptan (the natural gas smell) or some other additive;
-Sewer gas coming up through the lines, drains, or via “p-joints” that are dry and allowing the gas to escape into the atmosphere near the Airport or into buildings in the area;
-Swamp gas arising from the area;
-The “lake smell;”
-The Surplus Canal
-Oil refineries
-Jets passing overhead and emitting either unused jet fuel or exhaust;
-Utah Power’s 3 new generators
-Questar facility on 100 South and 1200 West – a possible leak in their gas line;
-The small Questar substation building on North Temple just west of the I-215 overpass;
-Thatcher Chemical
-General overall Wasatch Front air pollution, along with an inversion.

name: Parowan - Contaminated mine tailings
incident_summary:
Justin Wayment, the Parowan city attorney, received a packet of information from a John Anderson, regarding hazardous mine tailings that Mr. Anderson entered into a contract with Mr. Eric Flippo, to transport from Arizona to Parowan.

Mr. Anderson believes that no permits have been acquired to receive or treat the tailings, and that they are being stored improperly.  He has previously hired at least one individual, Roger Bowers, a geologist, to manage sampling and analysis of the waste through a lab.  Mr. Anderson has also recently hired Hill West Environmental out of Park City, to conduct further investigation.  Initial analysis of the waste indicates that the following are present, among other constituents:  arsenic, beryllium, mercury

To date, Mr. Anderson says he has transported 47 tons of the material.  Mr. Anderson was originally solicited to transport 1 million tons of the material.  He is concerned about potential affects to the environment and people in the community.  Mr. Wayment, attorney for Parowan City, states that the city municipal well is located approximately 1/4 mile from the location of the waste pile.

Several pages of information were provided by email and have been forwarded to Hans Millican.

address_location: Winderland and Trapper Circle, Springdale, Utah
incident_summary: A rainstorm washed a large amount of sediment and debris from the construction sites, which flowed into storm drains and then into a catch basin which drains into the Virgin River.

name: Whey Spill - Logan
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a valve broke on their whey tank spilling 75,000 pounds of whey.

The spill was contained on-site within their retention ponds and drains that flow into on-site waste water treatment.

No water ways impacted.

name: Yuba Lake -- Harmful Algal Bloom
incident_summary: Water samples contained microcystin toxin concentrations which exceeded Warning Advisory Levels.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
06/05/2012  12:49:  Ron Lund reports the following:  They were two five gallon containers.  One was labeled as hydraulic oil and the other as asphalt sealant.  Absorbent pads recovered remaining liquid in the storm drain.  The University of Utah cleaned the road of the majority of the spill.  It is unknown the amount of product in either container.  I estimate less than 1 gallon entered the manhole.  The asphalt sealant is not readily water soluble.  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
University workers discovered two spilling 25 gallon containers of hydraulic oil and asphalt sealant abandoned in the street on South Campus Drive.  Some of the spillage had flowed down the road and into a manhole cover.  A cleanup contractor and Ron Lund with Salt Lake Valley Health have been notified.  Ron will provide oversight of the cleanup.

name: Central Refrigerated (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller stated that the refrigeration tank on trailer was damaged and leaked 30 gallons of diesel onto an asphalt lot.  Approximately 1,500 ft2 was impacted.  Crew used sorbent booms and pads to collect fuel.

name: La Verkin - Release of Refrigerant Gas
incident_summary:
Caller reported that the company is releasing refrigerant gas to the atmosphere and is not using the recovery equipment. 

All information for this report from the National Response Center Incident Report #1255947.
title_eventname: La Verkin - Release of Refrigerant Gas

name: Gerold Schroeder (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
A private party, with residency in Salt Lake County, consisting of a mother and her young children had gone to their private physician to be tested for potential mercury exposure (testing was completed via fingernail samples).  The physician contacted Poison Control, who in turn contacted the Salt Lake Valley Health Dept.  The SLVHD reported the information to DEQ.  The mother is an immediate relative, and temporary resident of the homeowner.  The homeowner, who is a resident of Spring City Sanpete County Utah, repairs electric components has accumulated elemental mercury recovered from the components in an effort to return the mercury to beneficial use by reselling it to commercial interests.  The caller indicates that the homeowner's son (age 19) found the mercury and apparently has played with it in his room.  

25.Nov.05 DERR discussed this report with the EPA Region 8 OSC on duty.  Based on information provided by DEQ at this time, EPA does not deem it necessary at this time to dispatch personnel.  The recommendation by EPA is to advise the homeowner to notify a contractor to perform a cleanup.  DERR will notify the NRC to establish this report as matter of record.

name: RIchfield -- Oil Spill at UDOT Facility
incident_summary: A mechanic working on a vehicle accidentally released an estimated 50-100 gallons of oil into the sanitary sewer drain.  Most of the material was caught in oil-water separators; an unknown amount was discharged into the Richfield sewer system.
title_eventname: RIchfield -- Oil Spill at UDOT Facility

name: Sewage in SLC Airport Storm Drain
incident_summary: A sewage haul truck for Delta Airlines dumped about 220 gallons of sewage on the asphalt. about 180 gallons entered a storm drain. The above-ground spill was cleaned. The storm drain was not cleaned.
title_eventname: Sewage in SLC Airport Storm Drain

name: Diesel fuel spill near Clearfield
incident_summary:
About 100 gallons of diesel fuel was spilled from a tanker. The spill was contained to soil and the spill is being remediated. The location is estimated based on the reporter knowledge. The incident number is:
2019-10-23-076-NWE.

name: Vernal - Diesel Spill
incident_summary: On the morning of Monday 2/10/2020, control was lost when an electric generator was being unloaded from the back of a flatbed truck.  The generator contained approximately 200 gallons of diesel fuel, which spilled onto the dirt roadway.  No waterways or drains were directly impacted. Environmental Management Inc was contracted to clean up the spill and will commence cleaning on 2/11/2020.

name: Plymouth - Hydraulic fluid release
incident_summary: Caller reported an estimated 150 gallon hydraulic fluid release onto soil after a hydraulic hose broke on a grapple crane.  No waterways were impacted.  Absorbents were placed on the entire area.  The contaminated soil will be excavated and disposed of properly in a landfill.

name: Salt Lake County Gasoline Odor
incident_summary:
The caller stated that while walking his dog in Wasatch Hollow Park he noticed the smell of gasoline coming from Emigration Creek as he crossed it on the bridge.  He said that he could still smell gasoline farther along the creek but it was strongest at the bridge.

He did not see anyone dumping and did not notice anything in the water.  The NRC was not notified at this time because there is no confirmation of contamination in the water.

name: Salt Brine - Delta
incident_summary: A pressure valve malfunction cause a break in a line which released an estimated 70-80 barrels of brine water.  The caller stated that no other chemicals are part of the brine and that no known animals or vegetation are affected.  The site is reported to be at least 5 miles from any drinking water wells, and no surface waters are affected.

name: Myton -- Injection Water Spill
incident_summary: An buried injection water pipeline leaked and released an estimated 77 gallons onto the right of way and into a dry drainage.  BLM will assess potential impacts to any endangered cacti in area.

name: FBAC (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a release of 1000 pounds of anhydrous ammonia from a refrigeration system due to an equipment failure of a seal.  The release has been secured and the area is being vented.  The local fire dept. is on-scene.  This incident was reported to DERR via fax from the National Response Center (INR# 1003525).

name: I-15 Antifreeze Spill  SLC
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting an accident where a tractor trailer jack knifed and punctured the radiator.  12 gallons of antifreeze was released to the roadway.  Melting snow and runoff caused the antifreeze to run into the storm drain.

Pads and absorbents were placed on the spill and the storm drain was inspected for product.  There was no visible antifreeze in the storm drain.

name: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Spill
incident_summary:
Caller reported a release of 52 barrels of treated injection water. Release flowed along ROW into a dry drainage.  The line has been isolated and they will flush the area with fresh water and then take soil samples for lab analysis. 
  
Caller said that he contacted Randy Bywater with BLM and Amy G? with DOGM.    Any indicated she would inspect the site and take photos sometime tomorrow.
title_eventname: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Spill

name: Salt Lake Co - PCB Oil
incident_summary: Driver picked up PCB oil from electrical components at a Rocky Mountain Power facility.  PCB oil was reported at a concentration of greater-than 50 ppm.  Driver did not properly clear the hose.  Residual oil spilled from the hose to asphalt/concrete surface.  No other media were impacted.  Estimated volume of oil released is one-half gallon.  Material was cleaned up with absorbent (kitty litter).  Absorbent was ground into the surface to maximize uptake.  Wastes were properly disposed under UN2315 Hazard Class 9 Packing Group 3.  Driver recently reported the event.

name: Kennecott - Arsenic release
incident_summary: This incident was reported to the NRC (report #1248946).  Caller reported that gravity flow pipes at a closed gold mine overflowed three boxes sometime within the last two months and spilled water with elevated arsenic concentrations.  The spill has likely exceeded the one pound reportable quantity limit.  The amount will be less than 10 pounds but greater than one pound.  The overflow is likely due to rainwater.  The release has been secured.

name: SLC - Possible chlorine release to river
incident_summary: Caller reported that there was an abandoned metal storage shed in the southeast area of the Seven Peaks Waterpark property that contained chlorine tablets.  For reasons unknown, the storage shed caught fire and the SLC Fire Dept. doused the shed with water to put the fire out.  Afterwards, there was some concern that the chlorine water may have entered the Jordan River, however, this has not been confirmed.
title_eventname: SLC - Possible chlorine release to river

name: Hydraulic oil spill in St. George
incident_summary: The Dixie Medical Center trash compactor has been leaking hydraulic oil for about a year. From five to 20 gallons has been leaked to the soil. According to Landon Lee (435) 215-5710 who called Washington County Emergency Management, Envirocare has been contacted to clean up the spill.
title_eventname: Hydraulic oil spill in St. George

name: Ogden -- Hydraulic fluid spill in UPRR yard
address: Track 23 east side of Ogden Rail Yard
address_location: Track 23 east side of Ogden Rail Yard
incident_summary:
Company reports an accidental release of an estimated 500 gallons of hydraulic fluid onto the ground.  No waterways impacted, contractor is en route.  Location on map is approximate.

UPRR on-site contact is HazMat Manager Dana Pompetti 801-386-4208.
title_eventname: Ogden -- Hydraulic fluid spill in UPRR yard

name: Cottonwood Heights -- Release of concrete dust
address: 6901 S. Wasatch Blvd., Cottonwood Heights, Utah
address_location: 6901 S. Wasatch Blvd., Cottonwood Heights, Utah
incident_summary: A hole burst in a concrete mixing container during loading, releasing an unknown amount of concrete dust onto the ground in the facility.  The dust was cleaned with 7,000 gallons of water which was captured in a lined pond.  The company is neutralizing the mixture to about pH 9 and will recycle the water and dispose of the sediment.
title_eventname: Cottonwood Heights -- Release of concrete dust

name: Utah Lake -- Harmful Algal Bloom
incident_summary: Results of analysis of samples reveal water from several locations on Utah Lake contains concentrations of cyanobacteria which exceed warning levels.  Satellite imagery shows algal bloom covers most of the lake.

name: Rich County Possible Algae
incident_summary: A dog was brought to Bear Lake Animal Hospital by owner.  Vet is reporting a possible exposure to an algal bloom based on observed symptoms.  Location is a stagnant body of backwater near near the Bear Lake Rest Stop along Route 30 adjacent to Cheney Creek.  Vet is requesting water testing to determine the concentration.

name: UPDATE: Salt Lake City - Oil like substance
incident_summary:
Caller reported that when a container was pulled off a train it was noticed that the container was slowly leaking an oil like substance. About one-quarter of a cup was spilled onto concrete. No soils, storm drains, or water ways impacted. The Union Pacific Hazmat manager is en route to determine how to proceed. If needed there will be absorbent pads put down.

Update: Substance was discovered to be rhodonite (a non-hazardous material). 100 gallons were released, remediation has been complete.
title_eventname: UPDATE: Salt Lake City - Oil like substance

name: Orem -- Chemical odor of unknown origin
incident_summary: Complainant reported a strong industrial-chemical smell in the neighborhood.  Complainant stated it did not smell like a natural gas leak or a gasoline spill.
title_eventname: Orem -- Chemical odor of unknown origin

name: Wrecking Yard BMPs
incident_summary: Caller is making report of used oil spillage and poor waste management practices on a lot that is west of his property (PRP's junkyard is west of the address given).  Caller stated that the PRP is operating a vehicle wrecking yard in an area zoned as agricultural.  Lots are blocked off in 100 x 100 dimensions.   Vehicles are stacked so tightly that one cannot pass between them.  Caller stated that PRP is also expanding his junk yard, and said he services semis and releases materials to the ground.  There are multiple waterways nearby, irrigation ditches, and canals and the Sevier River is not far.  Caller said there is a canal that runs adjacent to his property.

name: Sewage Spill near Milford
incident_summary: About 2,300 gallons of sewage spilled to the soil after a control valve was turned in error. The sewage has frozen and will be removed with shovels where possible.

name: Farmington - Release of sodium hypochlorite
incident_summary: Caller reported that a leak was detected in the chlorination system at the drinking water facility at Lagoon Amusement Park at approximately 8:00 AM. The leak was stopped and the facility believed the release was contained to the sanitary sewer system. Further evaluation of the release found residual chlorine in Farmington Creek. Facility will divert water from the Rattlesnake Rapids amusement ride to the creek to dilute the residuals. Davis County Health Department is responding on-scene.

name: Pintura -- Diesel Fuel Spill
incident_summary: A semi-truck left the freeway and rolled onto its side, releasing an estimated 80 gallons of diesel fuel.

name: Process Water Release - Huntington
incident_summary: Process water line break released about 1,000 gallons of process water into Huntington Creek. Process water quality is good, so little impact is anticipated.

name: Midvale -- Sediment discharge in Jordan River
incident_summary: Caller reported a large discharge of sediment and accompanying fish kill into the Jordan River between 7200 S. and 9000 S.  Discharge is believed to be related to irrigation canal maintenance.
title_eventname: Midvale -- Sediment discharge in Jordan River

name: Diesel Oil - Washington County
incident_summary:
CALLER REPORTING THE RELEASE OF 50 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL FROM A
  SADDLE TANK DUE TO UNKNOWN REASONS.

name: Hydraulic Fluid - Vernal
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a spill of approximately 35 gallons of hydraulic fluid from a broken line on a D-11 bulldozer.  The spill was discovered and a catch pool was placed under the truck to contain the release.  About 10-gallons have been captured.

Impacts are to soils where they are tearing out old roads and hard surfaces at the mine site for reclamation.  No waterways impacted.

name: Chevron Refinery - SO2 Release
incident_summary: Caller reported facility start-up procedures resulted in the release of 698 pounds (lbs) of sulfur dioxide (SO2) to flare. SO2 released from Flares 1 & 2 directly to the atmosphere. Caller did not know how long facility had been flaring. Caller notified the National Response Center report #1262343.

name: Jordan River Jordan Narrows -- Harmful Algal Bloom
incident_summary: Analysis of water samples showed anatoxin levels exceeded Warning Advisory Thresholds.
title_eventname: Jordan River Jordan Narrows -- Harmful Algal Bloom

name: Utah Co - Diesel Spill
incident_summary: Driver pulled into final location after being flagged by another driver about a puncture and fuel leak emitting from the reserve tank serving refrig unit (capacity 50 gallons, actual amount lost has not yet been determined).  Driver notified and the fire department was dispatched. Driver initially deployed absorbent blanket and fire department deployed absorbents upon arrival.  The release trail follows the driver's path.  American Fork FD described the impact to a nearby surface water canal: a 1-2 inch wide flow of fuel from the pool on the ground entered the canal.  FD observed a sheen at the point of entry into the canal.  FD followed the canal to make observations and find a pooling/collection point to deploy booms, etc.  Sheen dissipated and was not observed further downstream.  It is believed the canal empties into Utah Lake with farmland in between.

name: Quick Lube of Spanish Fork (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller is an employee or former employee of Quick Lube in Spanish Fork.  The caller states that the facility manager, possible same as the owner, pours all used oil and radiator fluids down a drain in the pit (basement) of the facility.  The caller did not know if this was a storm drain or sewer.  The situation has been going on for more than a year.
title_eventname: Quick Lube of Spanish Fork (Null RP Substituted)

name: Hydraulic oil spill at SLC Airport
incident_summary: About 20 gallons of hydraulic oil spilled from a truck to asphalt. A small amount entered the airport closed-loop storm drain. All the material has been cleaned up.
title_eventname: Hydraulic oil spill at SLC Airport

name: Farmington Pond - Duck with fish hook in bill
incident_summary:
Caller reported there was a duck in Farmington Pond with a fish hook stuck in it's bill.

The UDEQ Duty Officer contacted Scott Walker (DNR/WR). Scott indicated that County Dispatch will have after hours contact information for Wildlife Officers.
title_eventname: Farmington Pond - Duck with fish hook in bill

name: PSC Industrial (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that  25 gallons of diesel fuel was released while cleaning out the pipeline within the remote tank farm at the Chevron Refinery.  Fuel needs to be transported from one tank to another so that the pipeline can be cleaned and allow for any necessary maintenance.  During transport from one tank to another the truck was overfilled releasing the 25 gallons of diesel to the surrounding soils.  Release was confined to the Chevron property.  Contaminated soils were excavated and placed in drums.  Waste materials will be staged on-site and disposed of on Monday.

name: Box Lake -- Harmful Algal Bloom
incident_summary: Water samples collected from the lake contained cyanobacteria in excess of Waring Advisory Thresholds.

name: Sandy - Transformer Oil Release
incident_summary: Caller reported that during the month of November 2018, the facility was switching out the transformers in their sub-station. The two replaced transformers were set aside and placed on the ground within the sub-station. During an April 25, 2019 inspection of the area, one of the replaced transformers was found to be leaking. The oil in the transformers was drained and the empty transformers were shipped off-site. The soils were tested for PCBs and excavated. Soils were determined to be non-detect for PCBs and shipped to the Salt Lake County Landfill for disposal. Quantity of transformer oil released was unknown, however, the capacity of the transformers was 1,600 gallons. No surface waters or storm drains were impacted.

name: Transformer Oil Spill in Wellsville
incident_summary: About 400 gallons of non-PCB transformer oil spilled from a transformer no longer in use to the soil. The date of the spill is unknown. The spill was discovered July 11. The spill went to soil below the transformer. The soil will be excavated next week.

name: Duchesne County Production Water Spill
incident_summary:
The point of contact for this incident is Matt Guest.  His contact information is above.

The caller reported a spill of 60 to 80 barrels of production water due to a truck accident.

The water spilled onto a dirt road covered in ice and snow.  The water ran down the road back to the well site where it seeped into the location pad.  The well site is LC Tribal 1956.  The GPS coordinates are:

N 40.06705
W -110.55727

No water bodies or drains are threatened.

Work on the clean up has been shutdown for the night due to cold and icy conditions.  A full assessment of the spill will be made a first light.

name: Farmers Distribution (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported the company (Farmers Distribution) operates a refueling pump on their property.  Stated that the shut-off valve on the fuel dispenser does not operate.  When a driver is finished refueling, the remaining #2 Diesel left in the dispenser & hose leaks to the ground.  Property owner has attempted to remedy the situation by placing buckets to capture the spilled diesel.  Caller reported the problem has gone on for a long time and that buckets routinely over flow releasing diesel to surrounding soil.  Wayne Thomas (SW District Engineer) will investigate.

name: Bluebell -- Pipeline leak
incident_summary: During excavation for maintenance a leak was discovered in an underground pipeline which released an estimated 127 barrels of produced water into the trench.  Approximately 125 barrels was recovered by the company.

name: Sevier -- Road paint spilled into dry wash
incident_summary: A truck crash released an estimated 750 gallons of yellow highway paint that flowed into a storm drain in the median and then into a dry wash.
title_eventname: Sevier -- Road paint spilled into dry wash

name: Redman Movies and Stories (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Film company equipment (articulated) truck was traveling west down Little Cottonwood Canyon.  Saddle tank struck a rock outcrop which ripped the tank open.  The impact caused the vehicle to jack-knife across to the south side of the road.  The further sliding was arrested by the snowbank which left the vehicle "hanging off" the bank - the rear of the tractor and front portion of the trailer are "hanging."  Response crews on-scene, in coordination with the PRP, estimate 20-30 gallons of diesel was released.  SLVHD reports that it appears most has been captured by the road-base, snow and soils.  At the current moment SLVHD sees no evidence of a direct impact to Little Cottonwood Creek, but acknowledg the possibility that some could reach the creek resulting from the proximity of contaminated snow and soils to the creek.  The PRP has contracted a local hazmat remedial company who is enroute to begin remedial actions.
title_eventname: Redman Movies and Stories (Null RP Substituted)

name: Kane Co - Gasoline Spill
incident_summary: Caller reports a private 23 foot pleasure vessel struck some rocks and damaged the fuel line.  Vessel made it back to Bullfrog Marina where it was trailered out of the water.  Operator reported a drip leak from point of impact back to the marina.  Rangers are in the process of determining where the accident occurred.

name: UPDATE:  Sewage in Lake Powell
incident_summary: A broken pipe resulted in the release of about 100 gallons of sewage into Lake Powell. The pipe was repaired and bleach was applied to the affected soil.

name: Little Cottonwood Canyon - Coal-tar pipeline wrap
incident_summary: Caller reported that during the landslide that occurred in Little Cottonwood Canyon on August 8, 2019, a 6-7 foot section of coal tar pipeline wrap was torn from a natural gas pipeline in the canyon. The torn section of pipeline wrap was not recovered. The material is described as non-hazardous. Incident occurred near mile- marker 8 along SR 210.
title_eventname: Little Cottonwood Canyon - Coal-tar pipeline wrap

name: UPALCO -- Produced water line leak
incident_summary: A leak from a valve in a produced water disposal line resulted in the discharge of an estimated 23 barrels of produced water.  The water covered the road and flowed into a nearby dry ditch.

name: Otter Creek Reservoir - Harmful Algal Bloom (HAB)
incident_summary: On 8/14/19, DWQ collected water samples at Otter Creek Reservoir at the Midway Shore during a routine monitoring run.  Toxin results delivered on 8/21/19 determined that microcystin levels in the water column are greater than 5 ug/L, which exceeds the Utah recreational health guidance for a Warning Advisory.  The Central Public Health Dept. put the lake on advisory.  DWQ is currently awaiting additional lab data results.
title_eventname: Otter Creek Reservoir - Harmful Algal Bloom (HAB)

name: Big West Oil (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that a tank leak resulted in the release of 1,000-2,000 gallons of reduced crude oil.  The release was contained within the secondary containment (earthern berm) around the tank.  Crews will attempt to recover the crude oil to the extent possible and excavate contaminated soils.  Release was believed to have occurred when a steam coil ruptured inside the tank.

name: Salt Lake City - Union Pacific unknown liquid
incident_summary: If contacting Union Pacific, refer to Report # 2019-05-20-196KSJ .  A transport container is leaking a liquid at a slow drip at the Salt Lake City Inter-modal Terminal.   The container is considered a mixed hazardous load, containing non-waste packages en-route for FedEx delivery.  The only placard associated with the shipment is UN-3480 -- Li-Ion batteries.  Union Pacific's hazardous materials team has been dispatched for designation and cleanup.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City - Union Pacific unknown liquid

name: Native Soils in Ditch - Goshen
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a spill of 10 cubic yards of native soils dumped in the Warm Springs Ditch in Goshen.

Dominion is constructing a mitigation wetlands area and removing native soils.  A truck lost the load in the pup when crossing the bridge.  The native soils and sediment are being removed from the ditch area.  

No hazardous materials were spilled and there are no other impacts to the ditch.

Dominion will contact the Corps of Engineers to report.

Their storm water permit is UTR 397789.

name: Kennecott Production Water Release
incident_summary: A process water spill may have caused an RQ exceedance of arsenic.  Release occurred at a power generating facility for mining operations.  Spill was caused by incorrect valving.

name: Uintah County -- Crude oil discharge
incident_summary: Operator at the GH 5-21 site discovered a failure in a flow line which resulted in the loss of 14 barrels of crude oil and produced water.  Discharge was contained on site and did not leave the pad.

name: Chevron (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported a malfuntion of their Sulfur unit.  Unit was shut down and H2S was routed to the flare.  Followup letter states chemical as sulfur dioxide.

name: Davis County - Unavoidable Breakdown
incident_summary: Caller reported that the carbon feed screw motor was replaced for the B furnace. The carbon feed rate was not maintained from 800 to 1600 and is considered an unavoidable breakdown according to the permit.

name: Lehi -- Battery acid spill
incident_summary: A fork lift being towed on a trailer struck the freeway overpass and fell over, releasing an estimated 5 gallons of battery acid onto the road and soils.  No waterways were affected.

name: Nancy Clark Trucking, LLC (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A citizen was out photographing bald eagles and observed a semi with a trailer dumping its load.  The substance dumped was a dark sludgy liquid with a creamy tan foam.  The tuck was pulled 50 ft off the highway.  Martin (the citizen)  collected a quart of the substance and photographs of the incident.  Martin was not sure if this is a legal place to dump.  The cab’s description was a medium blue solid in color Kenworth, number 507 from Nancy Clark Trucking, LLC.  The trailer’s description was front to back, mostly white and then diagonal lines of light gray, dark gray and red with a Utah license plate 05449P.  Martin also observed animal guts (sheep) dumped in the same area.  The area is approximately ½ mile from a residence.  John Chartier (Dist. Engineer) is inspecting the area.
title_eventname: Nancy Clark Trucking, LLC (Null RP Substituted)

name: Bland Brothers Construction (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Fuel spill occurred before 10-3-95 on closed section of Bruin Blvd. Diesel fuel, 100 gallons, spilled.  Occurred on road bed they're working on at college.  Have cleaned up by transporting to gravel pit owned by Bland Brothers.  There it's laid out on plastic sheeting to air dry.  SL County Fire Department responded - Haz Mat team.  Richard Van Allen wants to know if Bland Brothers needs a TSD Permit (could get names).

name: Houseboat Sewage Release - Lake Powell
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a sewage spill from a houseboat in Padre Bay at Lake Powell.  The US Coast Guard had a patrol in the area and they were notified by a boat staying in the area near the leaking houseboat.

Kids were swimming in the water and noticed sewage odors and bubbles coming to the water surface near the houseboat.

The dispatcher has notified the Coast Guard NRC, Kane County Health Dispatch and the Headquarters Staff, Park Service.

The rental company is sending a crew out to investigate.

name: SAPP Brothers (Holly Cunningham, GM) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
LHD was active and onscene.  PRP was making fuel delivery to Dairy Farmers of America facility.  Human error caused overflow into above ground storage tank.  Volumr recovered is 2,200 gallons.  AST has concrete secondary containment.  Visual evidence near a pipe with a ball valve that passes through the concrete was left open.  Envirocare was contracted to responded &  remediate.  Valve was closed when they arrived.  An undetermined volume flowed out, across soils and into a nearby irrigation ditch.  Area of impacted soils estimated 15ft x 20ft and reach along the ditch is estimated at 100 feet.  Spill is believed secure and contained and not expected to escape beyond the irriagation ditch.  

UPDATE 1/28/11 15:18: Information from John Hart (Envirocare) (801) 299-1900:  Envirocare was contracted to provide clean-up services.  Envirocare pumped out excess fuel from the containment, and steam cleaned the concrete, and have excavated the impacted soils.  Envirocare will begin excavating the contaminated soils within the irrigation ditch.  NRC and Bear River Health Dept were additionally notified of this release.  The impacted Irrigation Company was also notified of the release and on-scene along with BRHD to discuss clean-up alternatives.

UPDATE 2/2/11 16:14 - From DWQ Envirocare removed fuel from containment on 1/28.  Based on fuel recovered 20-40 gallons escaped containment.  CGRS is contracted to do surface contamination excavation.  Anticipate beginning week of Feb 7.
title_eventname: SAPP Brothers (Holly Cunningham, GM) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Transformer oil spill in Central UT
incident_summary: Overpressure of a transformer during a power surge resulted in the overpressure of a transformer and the release of 50 gallons of transformer oil to soil and rock. H2O Environmental has been called in to clean up the spill.
title_eventname: Transformer oil spill in Central UT

name: Lake Point -- Spill of mixed hazardous wastes
address: 8960 Clinton Landing Road, Lake Point, Utah
address_location: 8960 Clinton Landing Road, Lake Point, Utah
incident_summary:
A container full of mixed liquid hazardous wastes (UN 2924) leaked and spilled an estimated 40 gallons of waste into the back of the truck and onto the parking lot.  Approximately 10 gallons of waste flowed onto soil.

Mixture contained benzene at 0-10 ppm and D007 chromium at 0-100 ppm.  Cleanup was completed immediately after spill.
title_eventname: Lake Point -- Spill of mixed hazardous wastes

name: TruTech Laser Corp & Attostat Nano Technology (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: TruTech Laser Corp & Attostat Nano Technology
incident_summary: Reporting party (RP) made notification via letter.  Reporting party makes several assertions: the company uses nano silver, nano copper, nano iridium, platimum, gold, tungsten, cobalt and other heavy metals suspended in liquid using lasers; the disposal plan consists of of dumping used wastes in to a storm drain at a late evening hour; experiments at the facility have generated chlorine gas and other toxic materials which are continually "cooked" outside (south side of the building) to hide activity from view; fumes from these processes have caused other tenents to move due to symptoms of headache and accumulation of toxic gases in the building.  RP believe the facility: holds no permits, has not made notification to local authorities to inform of the materials at the facility, nor provided safety training on proper handling and disposal.
title_eventname: TruTech Laser Corp & Attostat Nano Technology (Null RP Substituted)

name: Orem - Petroleum Spill
incident_summary: Caller stated a Republic Services trash truck experienced a mechanic failure resulting in the release of approximately 20 gallons of Hydraulic Oil, most of which went into a storm drain. They are currently working to get a contractor out to clean up the spill.

name: Spring Lake -- Dead fish and suspected algal bloom
address: 12400 S. Spring Lake Road, Spring Lake, Utah
address_location: 12400 S. Spring Lake Road, Spring Lake, Utah
incident_summary: Caller reporting large amounts of algae in the water and an estimated dozen dead catfish and carp on the shoreline.
title_eventname: Spring Lake -- Dead fish and suspected algal bloom

name: North Salt Lake - SO2 Release
incident_summary:
The sulfur recovery unit at the Chevron Refinery experienced a trip releasing approximately 2,000 pounds SO2 out of the stack into the air. The release was stopped within about 24 hours.

NRC was also notified. NRC #1257109

name: North Salt Lake - Asphalt Seal Coat Slurry Spill

name: Semi Accident - Diesel I-80 Wanship

County fire has provided spill kits containment until a contractor arrives.

name: West Valley - Aluminum Sulfate Spill
incident_summary: A 275-gallon tote fell off a flatbed trailer spilling approximately 150-200 gallons of aluminum sulfate onto the freeway and dirt.  No waterways or storm drains were impacted.  This occurred on the southbound I-215 on-ramp at 3500 South in West Valley City.  The contents of the spill is currently on the shoulder of the road.  The pH was tested and found to be 3 so soda ash was used to neutralize the aluminum sulfate.  The West Valley Fire Dept. and Highway Patrol is on scene and SLVHD is en route.  A clean-up contractor will be called for clean-up.

name: Unknown Resident(?) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller stated that individual was observed performing repairs on a VW last week 5/10.  The vehicle has been removed from the location however, the residual wastes - a container of used oil - from the repair remains on/near the grass.  Caller related that when the wastes where first left behind, they smelled of gasoline.  Vehicles moving through the area have tracked the residual wastes along the ashpalt.  There exists only the single passage through the parking lot so going around it is not really an option.  This is a small condominium complex.  Condo owner has been contacted as well.  Pursuant to the question asked by DERR there are no storm drains nearby.

name: Questar Gas Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Received via National Response Center notification.  Natural gas is releasing from a service line due to a car hitting the gas meter and breaking it off the riser. name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:

The stormwater system will be scoped and cleaned.

The majority of the oil was contained in the basin; however, the liner had a leak and some oil leaked from the basin to the soil.  The exact quantity is unknown but they believe that more than 25 gallons leaked from the basin.

No water bodies are affected.

They have pumped the remaining oil from the basin and the transformer and are currently removing contaminated soil and disposing of it at the Kane County Landfill.

incident_summary: A process water overflow caused the release of about 75 gallons of process water to the storm drain. A sample was collected and will be analyzed.

name: Logan City Public Works - Tom dickinson (Null RP Substituted)

The spill consisted of either UN1133 adhesive or a water-based glue.  It had seeped through the floor boards of the truck onto the parking lot of a Best Western hotel.  No waterways or soils were impacted.  Lincoln Environmental was called for clean-up.

name: Provo - Chevron Petroleum Release
incident_summary: One of the steel tanks at the Chevron was in alarm mode for "an extended period of time", so Csesco was in the process of pumping all remaining fuel out of the UST.  Csesco estimated the leak rate was between 1.5 - 3.0 gallons per minute, at a potential for a loss of ~3,000 gallons fuel/day.  Kevin Beery contacted the station owner (Ryan Gordon) and advised him on abatement and investigation requirements and advised him to hire an environmental consultant to assist with mitigating the release.  Petroleum vapors in basements or buildings could be a potential major issue.  Chris Davis w/ Utah County Health Dept. is aware of the problem as of late Monday the 12th.  Owner told Kevin Beery that he plans on removing and replacing the affected UST as soon as possible.  Assuming both soils and groundwater have already been impacted, with the potential to impact indoor air as well.

name: Point of Mtn. - Dust Plume
incident_summary: Great plum of dust is blowing across the I-15 freeway from the sand and gravel operation at the point-of-the-mountain.  Doesn't look like they are using any dust supression.

name: Safety Kleen (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that the VAC trucks require period maintenance to remove what is termed "the elbow."  Crews had 2 VAC trucks on location for maitenance, and had cleaned residual solids material out of the back of a one of them.  The elbow had built up to a degree that it prevented drainage of an estimated 25 gallons of liquid material.  As a result, while opening the back of the VAC truck the 25 gallons was released.  Normal operation during the process includes construction of a solids containment/decon. pad constructed with heavy sheet plastic surrounded by a berm.  The larger volume overflowed this containment onto the asphalt parking lot.  The release was quickly diked and contained using absorbant materials.  Free liquid was captured by the second VAC truck.  No storm drains or surface waters were impacted.  VAC trucks are used to clean oil/water separators.  Mixture released cosisted of oil and water.

name: SLC - Suspicion of illegal dumping

Hoyt Place (address approximated from SLCo Recorder maps) late at night.  The property is owned by an elderly neighbor.  Caller believed that Mr. Costa has misrepresented himself to the neighbor to gain access to the property.  A previous call to the police ended with the removal of a container of chlordane.  Caller stated that Mr. Costa is the same Andrew Costa convicted in 2010 for illegal waste dumping in SLC.  The situation at the property has been on-going since early July 2013.

name: SL General Aviation Fuel Spill
incident_summary:
Caller reported that at 0240 this morning an operator was fueling an over wing aircraft and notice fuel leaking from the truck. Upon investigating he shut off the fuel and started emergency procedures. They discovered fuel had spread to cover a 20 by 20 area and deployed absorbents and other materials. TAC air then notified the Salt Lake Airport and Ken Pratt responded to investigate. The proceeded to a storm box 400 ft away and checked it. There was no evidence of any fuel in the box so the boomed it and contacted a cleanup company. Envirocare responded about 0500 and proceeded to recover fuel and material from all the drains they could find. The also installed booms and pads in each box. The plan to return on Monday or Tuesday and flush and clean the drains and boxes. The estimate of fuel released id high due to the nighttime operation. For the sake of safety they keep the operator from climbing on top of the truck at night when they are filling it. They do not have an accurate starting volume for the truck, they only have what it was left and how much was fueled into the aircraft. The estimate is an over estimate.

Update 1/6/14 1422 hrs, recalculating the fuel released was done and a closer estimate of 96 gallons is estimated to have been released.

The catch basin is unlined.  Vegetation at the catch basin was covered in a black residue and there was a hydrocarbon odor.

112 Degrees 0 Minutes 35.62 Seconds West

The Director of Environmental for the corporate office of Pilot Travel Centers is Joey Cupps.

name: Production Water Spill
incident_summary: While transporting produced water to a SWD facility, a Howell Trucking water truck lost control of the vehicle and rolled over.  As a result, ~158 bbls. of produced water were released onto the ground running into the roadside ditch.  The spill travelled ~350' south in the roadside ditch before running down the eastern slope approximately 25' before stopping.  The release occurred approximately 1.7 miles south of the intersection of Strawberry River Rd. and US 40.  BBC notified Duchesne County of the release after it occurred. The accident/release was verbally reported to Dennis Ingram on 8/23/13 at ~8:30 A.M.  Diversion structures were constructed to hold the pooled produced water until it was recovered with another water truck.  All standing water was removed by a backup water truck.  No visible hydrocarbon impact was observed on the surface within the spill path.  Soil samples were collected along the entire spill path to evaluate for potential impacts.  The laboratory results of these samples are pending and BBC will share these results with UDOGM upon receipt.

name: Lewis Bros. Stages (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported regarding several health and environmental issues occurring at the Lewis Bros. Stage facility.  Caller indicated that aircraft stripping compound is used at the facility to prep buses prior to painting.  The aircraft stripping compound is rinsed/drained from the buses and is allowed to flow into a storm drain.  Caller indicated 15 – 20 buses have been handled at the facility in this manner and 1 bus is currently in the paint shop.  Caller also reported issues within the paint shop indicating that poorly ventilated paint fumes have lead to breathing difficulty and fugitive emissions are allowed to escape to outside air.  Caller reported that the paint shop had previously been shut down for violations but was unsure which government agency shut down the operation (caller guessed that it had been the Fire Marshall’s Office).   Steve Larson is the Shop Foreman at Lewis Bros. Stage.                                                                                                                                                                                Tom Rushing (DWQ) was on conference call at the time of notification to DERR.  The DERR has notified Rolf Larsen (SLVHD) regarding the report.

UPDATE 10/24/06 16:58:  Rolf Larsen (SLVHD) visited the Lewis Bros. facility with Gordon Lund (SLVHD), the Fire Marshal, and Randy Peterson (SLC Public Utilities).  Rolf reported that the buses are being washed out back without containment for rinsate water.  The cleaning solution used in the washing operation contains a green tracer dye and Rolf reported visible green puddles on the asphalt and in a nearby storm drain box.  After washing, the buses are moved inside for engine servicing/oil change.  Rolf did not note any visible problems at this part of the facility.  Personnel claimed to have all proper paperwork for used oil.  Lewis Bros. was also operating an unpermited paint booth at the facility.  Fans inside the paint booth blow paint/paint fumes to outside air.  Additional information from Glen Detton (Reporting Party) indicated employees wear respirators inside the booth but may not be receiving proper fitting, and training from Lewis Bros.  Other worker safety issues may be present at the facility.  Rolf also reported the facility has a "drop box" for the collection of sewage from the buses.  Rolf reported that the drivers may not be using necessary precautions and are not discharging sewage entirely to drop box.  Evidence of raw sewage was visible on the asphalt and running out into the gutter.

TW Company was called in to mitigate and cleanup spilled chemicals.  Four AST tanks (2-12,000 gal, and 2-6,000 gal capacity) had their tops blown off.  Cause of incident is unknown but is being investigated.  Products released or burned in the incident were: Glycol Ether – “DM”, Glycol Ether -“PM”, Glycol Ether -“DPM”; (these tanks were empty down to the drain valve), DowFrost (includes glycol) tank had 4700 gallons before incident.  None of these chemicals have a reportable quantity.  A nearby tank containing Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) was discovered (during fire suppression activities)  to be leaking product from a broken sight tube.  The sight tube valve was closed stopping the leaking product which was burning.  This tank did not explode.  The fire was reported to be out before 9 am.   TW Company and VOPAK employees worked to mitigate and control fire suppression water runoff to storm drains and thence  to the Jordan River, although some water reached the river.  Later in the afternoon a containment basin was tested and had low Ph.water.  It was then discovered that a tank of Nitric Acid was leaking product to a secondary containment.  Amount lost is 3000 gallons.  Storm drains were closed to contain material, but to prevent the material from running onto 800 South Street the drains were opened. Sulfur Recovery Unit (SRU) has interlocked.  Crew is working to restore the SRU.  Caller will have environmental personnel call w/add'l info and status update.

12:45 - Phillips will have to shut down the unit completely.  Ruptured steam tube on the 4th pass of the sulfur condensation unit - part of the SRU. name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
DERR Tanks personnel received notification of a heating oil tank release.  A petroleum odor was encountered by a construction company in the process of installing gas lines.  Installation of lines is being done using directional drilling.  They broke through an abandoned 10-12 inch steel pipe running the length of an ally.  May be an old water line but city crew had no info and claim to it.  An old brick pump house appears along the same route of the line.  An active sewer line runs north-to-south in the alley.  Crew trenched in order to determine cause and noted groundwater at 5-6 feet below grade.  When the pipe was uncovered groundwater flowed into the pipe and displaced the vapor and emitted an odor of petroleum.  DERR made inspection and reported no odor of petroleum, and only a faint natural gas smell was noted.  Groundwater appeared to be 3-4 feet below grade.  No evidence of a heating oil tank was found.  Construction crew seeks advice to cap the pipe and or backfilling the hole.  

5/21/2012 DEQ contacted construction representative.  Construction crew information offers an alternative circumstance: crew stated there they do not believe water in the excavation is groundwater; they suspect it is the water that emerged from the pipe itself when it was expsosed to the excavation.

name: Salt Lake County Residential Waste Burial
incident_summary:
Mr. Gibson stated that the house that his parents lived in was recently bought from the bank 1-2 months ago by a new owner.  The house is apparently being remodeled in order to "flip" the house.  Dan is concerned that any prospective person who will reside in the house in the future will have health risks due to the following:

Mr. Gibson stated that his parents owned and lived in the house from 1963 until several years ago (father passed away before his mother).  Mr. Gibson stated that his father buried various items in the backyard over the years, including a car and refrigerator.  The car is apparently buried on the east/northeast side of the property, and the freezer is buried on the southwest part of the property,toward the back near a barn-type structure, and due south of the house.

Furthermore, Mr. Gibson's daughter (Mary Anne Huffman) bought the house approximately 5-6 years ago and lived in the house until early 2016.  Apparently, Ms. Huffman's children were getting sick often and this was attributed to conditions in the house.  Mr. Gibson stated that there were several sewer backup events inside the house, which has caused significant mold issues in the house.  Ms. Huffman abandoned the house in early 2016 and walked away - the bank then took ownership of the property.

Because Ms. Huffman abandoned the house and the bank took ownership of the property, no environmental hazards were disclosed when the new owner bought the house 1-2 months ago from the bank.

Mr. Gibson believes that the new owner may not 1) be aware of the hazards or 2) may over look the hazards in order to flip the house, and therefore, any prospective occupant of the property may be at risk due to environmental hazards.
title_eventname: Salt Lake County Residential Waste Burial

name: Varian Medical Systems (Null RP Substituted)

The system was checked at 5:30 AM and there were no problems.  Calculations were done to estimate the amount of discharge between 5:30 AM and 7:30 AM and an estimated 2800 gallons was released maximum, however, the amount may have been less depending on when the system failure took place.  Samples were sent to the lab for VOC testing.  In the meantime, the system has been shut down to determine the cause of the system failure.  Caller was advised to contact the NRC to report this incident.  UPDATE (2/10/11 @10:55 AM):  J.C. Smith called to report lab results.  TCE was 179 mcg/L and cis-1,2-DCE was 8 mcg/L.

incident_summary:

4/12/11 Bear River Health plans to investigate the site this morning.
4/13/11 Bear River Health made an inspection of the site yesterday and observed two small isolated areas of incdental oil in the veneer of sand on a boat ramp.  BRHD removed some of the oily sand (by shovel) to a depth of 2-3 inches and uncovered a joint in the cement (boat ramp).  After removing the oily sand the seepage from the  joint became clear and largely free of any oil contamination.  The oil appeared to be discarded or leaked and of unknown origin.  Quantity of contaminated soils is estamated to be five gallons most of which was above water.

name: Los Angeles Chemical Company (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:

There is an open grassy area near the facility and apparently neighboring businesses have not been affected.  The gas is noticeable, but not strong.  No odors were detected inside the building and no personnel have reacted negatively to the gas being released from the tanker.  It is not known at this time if the release constitutes a reportable quantity.  The responsible party is consulting the manufacture of possible remedies and will file a complete report of the incident to that State.  No emergency personnel have been called to the site.

UPDATE  VIA NRC:   Reported on 10/07/03 at 17:30, Shelley Thompson, Los Angeles Chemical Company.  Release happened on September 4, 2003.  Release to atmosphere was 33 pounds of chlorine gas.  A reaction occurred inside of a parked tanker truck between sodium chlorate and residual sulfuric acid resulting in a release of chlorine gas into the atmosphere.

name: Covenant Transport (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports that a truck was traveling eastbound on I-70 when it rolled off the embankment.  The saddle tank hit the guard rail and was ripped from the tractor.  The entire truck continued beyond the guard rail rolling an additional 80 yards down a 60-degree embankment.  The truck came to rest on the frontage road below.  The capacity of the saddle tank is 140 gallons (diesel).  At this time the PRP is still investigating to see if they can determine what the actual capacity of fuel was at the time of the incident.  Weather conditions at the time - snowing.  UHP responded.  Johnson's Towing out of Salina was dispatched to assist in removing the vehicle.  Responders deployed a plow to gain access to the truck (which also became stuck).  TW Company (TW) was dispatched from Salt Lake City and arrived on-scene at 20:00 hours last night.  TW coordinated with ACT.  TW reported that with exception to a single puddle of fuel observed, there were no other obvious spots of fuel observed.  TW attempted to determine the viability of cleaning spotty areas using a shovel and much of the material is well frozen.  TW reported that Salina Creek is an estimated 75 yards distant from the accident zone and has not been impacted.

UPDATE 1Feb06 11:15 - The Central District Health Dept. did a site visit.  CDHD reports that there is quite a bit of fuel still present and soils are heavily saturated with diesel.  It is currently snowing at the site and so much may be obscured from view.  CDHD described the general topography of the site - resides on the highway along canyon turn.  The guard rail is set back from the hardtop of the roadway several yards and there is a 1-2 foot high berm of soil immediately behind the railing.  Moving back away from the road, the berm then drops down along a steep slope to the frontage road immediately below.  The drop is estimated at 20-30 feet down from the guardrail.  The approximate zone of contamination extends 35-40 feet in length and 10 feet in width.  Most appears to be near the guardrail on top.  Soils in the berm next to the highway appear saturated with fuel.  With the volume of snow and snowmelt some of the fuel was observed being readily mobilized and is currently flowing along the pavement creating a potentially dangerous situation for motorists.  For the purpose of remedial efforts, CDHD believes the zone of contaminated soils appears to be easily accessible with a backhoe or trackhoe.

UPDATE 1Feb06 PM - ACT notified DEQ; ACT will contact UDOT to coordinate immediate delivery of sand or other absorbant material to be dispenced on the road with the intent to eliminate the risk posed by fuel flowing across the roadway.  TW Company will dispatch to the incident location on 2Feb06 to begin cleanup work.

name: VersaCold - Ross Smith (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports a pump shaft seal failure allowed ammonia to escape the refrigeration system.  The ammonia escaped to air in a warehouse.  The building was evacuated (10-15 employees) while the SLCFD and hazmat crews cleared the air in the building and washed down the floors.  Estimated amount of ammonia released is 50 lbs.  Release has been secured and repairs underway.  The 5700 block of Harold Gatty Dr. was blocked off by the FD while mitigating the release.

UPDATE (written notice dated 28Aug06 rcv'd 5Sept06) - Event is attributed to human error and not equipment failure.  After action review - tech initially thought he had opened a valve on a line leading back in to the vessel; tech inadvertently had opened a line directly to the atmosphere on the discharge side of a pump.  Valve did not have steel plug (contractor alleges it is standard practice to have plug).  Believe a super-chilled plug of oil resident in the pipe and valve is the reason there was not an immediate observation of odor (contractor alleges it is not unusual to have such ablockage in the line when opening a valve on a low temperature line).  Temp and pressure will usually move this oil out of the valve area within minutes.  Post event analysis indicates the total volume calculated of ammonia released was estimated at 2018 lbs.; the contractor re-charged 2,000 lbs back into the system restoring it to operational levels recorded earlier in the week pre-release.  Two injuries recorded self-dispatched themselves for medical evaluation, were treated and released the same evening and back to work the following day.

name: Ferron - Gasoline Sheen on Canal
incident_summary:
From the NRC Report - 

THE CALLER OBSERVED WHAT APPEARS TO BE GASOLINE AND OIL IN A STORM  DRAIN, THIS  RESULTED IN A SHEEN ON A NEARBY CANAL. THE SOURCE OF THE DISCHARGE IS UNKNOWN. THE CALLER STATED THAT THE ODOR WAS INITIALLY DISCOVERED SOMETIME LAST WEEK HOWEVER IT HAS WORSENED.

DWQ Currently has a gasoline release from a former above ground storage tank facility at 15 W Main that had impacts to the sewer near the reported address.  Ed Hickey is managing that facility.

UPDATE March 16, 2015 - Caller reports an increase in sheen appearing in a storm drain that discharges to Ferron Creek.  Sheriff's hazardous materials response has been deploying booms to the storm drain in as an on-going activity.  DEQ District Engineer and DWQ have been active and the latter recently conducted a site visit.  Due to warmer temperatures, product is volatilizing at a higher rate and the migration of product is more apparent.  Authorities are receiving more complaints about petroleum fuel odors and local citizens are  very upset about the situation. 


UPDATE March 17, 2015 (email from Ed Hickey summarizing conversation with Terracon consultant):

"Ben Bowers of Terracon was on the Gillys Ferron site yesterday.  He received payment from Mr. Benson for the previous limited site investigation. Here is his report:

1) Castle Valley SSV sent their vac truck out to the canal to suck up the water and product.  I do not know if they will switch out the absorbent booms or leave the current ones there.  Ben Says the booms are working quite well to capture any floating product, and the water is much cleaner after the second in-line boom.

2) Terracon has placed absorbent booms inside the drain box on the Gillys property.  This will accomplish the same thing of skimming product, but upstream of the storm water drains around the east side of town that are the source of fumes.

3) The french drain on Gillys property is of limited length, originally installed to cut-off water draining from a swampy area to the north that is now a park. The french drain with the gasoline-laden water will be plugged completely so water doesn't enter the storm drain. The water will back up somewhere, but it is not thought to be an issue right now. The plug will not be installed until next week, hopefully done at the same time as #4. In the interim, the booms will have to suffice.

4) Terracon will put together a cost proposal to dig a hole along the french drain and install a vertical culvert to collect the french drain water and product. This will provide a place to skim the product off when necessary. It is an alternative to an oil-water separator. Also, the excavation will determine if product has also migrated along the utility line fill.  Mr. Benson will have to approve this cost and work before Terracon does it.  If he approves, this will be done next week."

name: Utah Co - Mercury Spill in Garage
incident_summary:
Resident had used a carburetor tuner and was replacing it to shelf in the garage when the mercury spilled out.  Mercury spilled to work surface and concrete floor.  Mercury dispersed on the concrete.  A laptop computer was on the work surface.  Residents contacted and received advice from LHD about appropriate action.  Residents purchased sulfur, proceeded to clean impacted area, scooped mercury into cracks of concrete garage floor, and  spread the sulfur on it.  Resident brought laptop into the house today, opened it and discovered beads of mercury on the laptop.  Residents did further research online, and re-evaluated the circumstances (mercury was tracked from the garage into the house) and called for additional advise and assistance to determine where mercury may have been tracked into the residence.  Residents have bagged and removed Items that are known or suspected of being contaminated.  
18:41 Resident callback to DO - surface top on which the laptop was resting in garage is a deep-freeze.  Residents have treated the garage area as "off-limits" since spill, have not parked in the garage, etc.  First contact with LHD was today at about 14:00.
title_eventname: Utah Co - Mercury Spill in Garage

name: UPDATE Loa - Tanker Rollover - Gasoline Spill
incident_summary:
David Romero received a call from Richard Mosley, State Fire Marshall, reporting a tanker truck rollover in Central Utah, unknown location.  They reported ~4000 gallons of gasoline/diesel spilling to the roadway with unknown impacts.

Nick Tingey with Petroleum Wholesale called the NRC and DEQ and is reporting the truck is only seeping product and only a few gallons have spilled.  Impacts are confined to the roadway.  Wayne Co Hazmat, Fire and Police are all onsite.  Petroleum Wholesale will have a pumper truck there within an hour to remove the product from the tanker to anther truck.

  From NRC Report - CALLER STATED DRIVER LOST CONTROL OF HIS TRACTOR TRAILER WHICH
  CAUSED MATERIAL TO RELEASE ONTO THE GROUND. CALLER STATED TRACTOR
  TRAILER WAS CARRYING A MIXTURE OF DIESEL FUEL AND GASOLINE AND DOES
  NOT KNOW AT THIS TIME WHAT THE MATERIAL WAS THAT RELEASED.

UPDATE - I received a call from RIchard Mosley (State Fire) @ 4:30PM with an incident update.  The tanker lost approximately 6,000 gallons of gasoline/diesel.  UDOT built up berms 4-5 ft high around the spill area to keep runoff contained if it rains.  No waterways are nearby or impacted. The spill location is 1.5 miles east of the summit heading east toward Loa at MP 42.5.  The diesel tanker spilled to the north side of Hwy 24 and gasoline to the south side of the highway.  Spackman Environmental is onsite and is cleaning up the spill.
title_eventname: UPDATE Loa - Tanker Rollover - Gasoline Spill

Caller does not know at this time if remedial contractor has been procured to mitigate.
title_eventname: Hunter Trucking/Sevier Valley Oil (Null RP Substituted)

The diesel from the tank flowed to a storm drain.  Sprinklers were going at the time.  The Fire Dept. dammed & diked the storm drain and recovered about 50 gallons of a water/fuel mix.   The passenger-side saddle tank was partially buried.  About 80 gallons of a water/fuel mix was recovered from this tank.  Antifreeze, transmission oil, and waste oil were also likely discharged in the accident.  Envirocare has been called for clean-up.
title_eventname: Salt Lake City - Diesel spill from truck accident

name: Weber County Semi Truck Accident
incident_summary:
The caller reported a single vehicle accident on the 5600 South off ramp to I-15 in Roy.  The vehicle was a semi truck that lost its brakes and crashed.  The crash resulted in an engine fire.  It is assumed that all engine fluids were released, diesel fuel, oil, antifreeze.  Some of the fluids entered a storm drain before the fire department could block it.  Fire department placed absorbent on the asphalt to absorb the fluids.

As the truck was leaving the road it struck a Rocky Mountain Power power pole causing the transformer on the pole to fall and rupture releasing all of its oil.  The transformer was manufactured in 1953 so it may have contained PCB oil.  Rocky Mountain power was on the scene and secured the transformer and took soil samples to determine if there are PCBs.  Those at the scene are treating the scene as if there are PCBs as a precaution.

Roy City storm water personnel and Envirocare were on scene to begin clean up.

UDOT and Roy City Fire were also on scene.  The Incident Commander was Brandon Storey from Roy Fire.  The Roy Fire incident number is 19RO21411.

At the time of the report the caller did not know who the responsible party was.  That information will be provided later.

The male brought the mercury from home in Ogden and consumed it at the location in Logan. WMHD has been notified that there might be some exposure in Ogden, and will be alerted if anything comes up.

name: Logan Sewage Break
incident_summary:
was called by Logan City regarding a pressurized sewage line that was leaking into a catch basin at a parking lot.  The location is approximately 1800 South Hwy 89 at the old Parker used car lot.  The leak was caused by Underground Solutions Drilling Company doing some work in that area where they fractured the sewer line.  The sewer line is owned by Thermo Fischer.  The fracture was probably caused on July 18th but did not appear until July 23rd.  An onsite investigation was conducted by myself and Tom Dickeson of Logan City on July 23rd. 
 
It was noted during the investigation that the drilling company was bringing in some digging equipment to repair the damaged pipe and they were working on it at that time.  The sewer pipe as told to me by Tom is probably 1 1/2 inches in diameter and I observed just a small amount of sewage coming out of the leak.  The surfacing sewage was draining into the catch basin area where there was only a small amount, probably less than 30 gallons and diluted by the water table.  The sewage was contained the the catch basin area and was not moving into the storm drainage or irrigation ditches.  The area of the sewage is industrial with no likelihood of exposure to people.  At this time it is decided that no further action is needed by the health department.
 
Sincerely,
 
Richard Worley, LEHS

name: Dye Test release

The dye was introduced into a drain near the loading dock area at about 9:30.  The floor drain tested is separated by a wall and is not impacted by runoff near the loading dock. On Monday (01/20/09) crew used a backhoe to scrap and stockpile the affected soil for shipment to the local landfill.  Darin Brown of the Tri-County Health Department was on site to observe the soil removal.  Soil remains on site pending analytical results required for disposal at landfill.

name: EPA Region VI (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Semi was transporting a load of radioactive construction debris from Houston Texas to the Envirocare facility in Clive, Utah.  Vehicle was involved in a rollover in Spanish Fork Canyon on SR-6 along an area commonly refered to as the  "Red Narrows."  Location is the southeast corner of Utah County.  UHP Hazmat Officer on-scene conducted radiological monitoring and determined that integrity of the containment of material was maintained - monitoring showed negative readings for radiation.  Saddle tank with 150 gallon capacity was ruptured in the incident.  An estimated 30 to 100 gallons of diesel entered the river.  Upon notification to DEQ/DWQ, DWQ indicated that due to the level of industrial activity the water is for all intents and purposes the waterway does not have fish and is "sterile."  SR-6 has been shut-down.  Diesel spilled to a flowing seep/spring that flows through a culvert beneath the road and into Soldier Creek.  Crew captured ~3 gallons of fuel.  

UPDATE 9/17/02 14:11 - Information provided by DNR indicates the following… "The last stream survey done in that area was somewhat downstream, but present then were redside shiners, leatherside chubs, suckers, sculpin and trout."  DNR-DWR  will mobilize a representative to the scene to take photos and see if there is any evidence of wildlife loss.
