name: Howell Trucking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
From Dennis Ingram of DOGM and Scot Ghan with BBC (Scott's phone number is 970-744-8128).  He was scrambling to get all the details also.  Howell Trucking lost a truck with a pup trailer carrying production water off a dirt road in the Rabbit Gulch area north of Starvation Reservoir.  Reported location (approximate) is attached via a Google Earth placemark.  This happened yesterday afternoon.  Not sure how much was released, but it did run for about 1/4 mile apparently, so maybe 100 bbls or so until we know better.  It was reported that surface water was not impacted.  
 
The truck was carrying Bill Barrett Corp's production water, so even though the fault was Howell Trucking (pulling off the road to let somebody pass, and pulled too far off the road) BBC is addressing the assessment and cleanup with their environmental consultant who should be onsite today.  This spill is in a source protection area for Starvation Reservoir, which is a drinking water source.  I am going to visit the site this afternoon to make sure it did not reach the reservoir.  I was told it did not but I think we need to confirm that, and see how close it did come.  From Google Earth it looks like it was something like 1.3 miles to the reservoir from the spill site.  Apparently a dry wash, I would like to confirm that also.  I will send out a report late today when I know more.
 
 -Scott

name: Emery County Complaint

The City is requesting the help of the County/State to confirm that Mr. Jacobsen has properly drained fluids from these vehicles prior to burial, and if it is confirmed that fluids remain in these vehicles then that Mr. Jacobsen will be required to remove fluids and remediate any soil or groundwater contamination related to this "art" installation.

name: Production Water Spill
incident_summary:
This spill was reported to DERR via email from Scott Hacking.  The spill was originally reported to the Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) on Monday, March 31, 2014 by Scott Ghan with Bill Barrett Corp.  Scott Ghan reported that a pipeline break surfaced leaving the UDWR 14-29-36 BTR well to the west, approximately sixty to seventy yards down that pipeline and then ran down across the access road and then north into a winter range field owned by the Division of Wildlife Resources (DWR).  Scott Gahn estimated they lost more than a hundred barrels of production water.  Besides DOGM, he notified the DWR and since the minerals are Tribal, the Tribe was also notified.  Because of DOGM's hundred barrel or major event rule, Scott Gahn notified DOGM immediately about this spill event.

Scott Hacking investigated the spill site today at around 1 PM.  The pipeline break had been fixed and the repair trench was still open.  There was a cleanup crew on-site (Chapman Construction) that was removing the contaminated soils.  The production water ran an estimated 300 feet north into the nearby rangeland (owned by DWR) , and two containment berms/excavations had been constructed at the terminus.  No surface water was impacted.  LTE Environmental will collect soil confirmation samples at the cleanup site.  Cleanup is well underway.

Beth Thomas, BethT7@yahoo.com,;
We were cleaning trash out of the Jordan River via canoe yesterday morning with Splore...and encountered an area on the river that had a very stron oil smell.  We then noticed a lot of oil on the water and in the river itself.  The oil continued all the way to where we exited....which was just outside the bird refuge.  Who do we report this to?  What do we do?  The Splore Guides can provide more info on exact location as we are not as familiar with the river.....but we did notice the refineries right by there (we could see them from the river shortly after passing the strong oil smell)

Eric Bonin, 801-454-4128, eric@splore.org;
My name is Eric Bonin and I’m the Salt lake Program manager for Splore. We have been running trips on the Jordan River this summer for our clients and clean up trips for volunteers. Yesterday we came across something unusually and alarming to our Guides and participants. It was described to me as follows:
A very strong oil smell.  We then noticed a lot of oil on the water and in the river itself.  The oil continued all the way to where we exited....which was just outside the bird refuge. Two spots where there was a smell of oil. And two areas where oil was leaking into the river.
 My Guides describe the areas as follows:
1.      Behind a car lot after a wooden pipe across the river.
2.      One by the Questar gas line crossing the river. The one with the huge gate around it.
After looking at the Google map we decided them to be at the two location on the map.(To include as extra link in incident email.

John Rosswog, 801-618-5332, johnrosswog@yahoo.com;
I was canoeing on the Jordan River yesterday and there was sizable amount of oil in the water.   I think it was around 2500 North (North Salt Lake area) on the river and for a good quarter of a mile the oil smell was really, really strong. name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Update December 29 11:30 a.m. Neil Taylor>>>>>>>>>>>
On December 28, the Davis County Health Department requested that DEQ monitor the Cedar Springs Condominiums once more to ensure post-remedial action, mercury vapor concentrations remained below EPA action levels.

Monitoring was conducted December 29, beginning at 10 a.m., by Neil Taylor with DEQ and Delane McGarvey and David Spence with the Davis County Health Department.

Mercury vapor concentrations ranged from approximately 50 ng/m3 on the condominium's lowest floor to 99 ng/m3 on the condominium's highest floor.  All mercury vapor concentrations were below the 300 ng/m3 concentration recommended by EPA and CDC for continuous occupancy by adults and small children.


UPDATE: Friday 12/22/06 23:00
Units continue to be cycled through heating & venting.  Cursory mercury survey completed at 18:10 of all accessible units indicates levels continue to decline w/ exception to the unit in which the release occurred.  Some with "contractor applied heat" several with HVAC heat.  Two units remain inaccessible.  EPA START contractor on-scene at 17:40.  DEQ and START conducted a dual meter survey of all accessible units.  Resurvey indicates Hg levels may satisfy closure on most units except those not accessible and the subject unit.  START contractor reported newest data to Region 8 OSC for consideration and action.  OSC advised (1) that those units not accessible also be surveyed prior to advising final closure, and (2) that several additional action items, target areas/items identified by the survey in the subject unit be addressed.  

UPDATE: 16:00 12/22/2006
Hg levels in all but one condo are below 1000 ng/m3.   Heating and venting will continue toward a target level of 300 ng/m3.  Davis Co. Health has recommended health monitoring of all occupants.  Good progress is being made.  The true test will be to see if these levels hold when the venting stops.

UPDATE: 12:45 PM Friday, 12/22/06
An EPA OSC Start Contractor (URS) is responding out of San Francisco.  He will arrive this evening and will have START contractor assistance.  EPA will provide the almost-24 hr coverage we had for the last few days, we'll stay in the loop and provide assistance as necessary.  Heating and venting of the units is ongoing, generally levels are dropping.  

Update:  Friday, 12/22/06, 8:00 AM
Heating and venting continued through the night.  9 of 12 units have been screened.  Of the 9, all except one have high concentrations of Hg.  All residents voluntarily left for the night finding a place to stay on their own.  It appears that no one is home at three of units - those that have not been screened.  DEQ will work today with the county and condo assoc. to try and get names and contact info, access if possible.

UPDATE:  12/21/2006
EPA Contractor on site since ~ 5:30 PM.  They have been ventilating the common hall/stairs and removing carpeting in lower hall just outside the unit where the spill occurred.  Also have done some removal of materials within the unit, found an empty 8 oz container labeled Hg, likely source.  

There are twelve units in the building, three floors, 4/floor.  Davis Co. officials contacted the few people who were home tonight, they have all moved to relatives or friends for the night.  No one home at many of the units.  High readings were found in the few units they have been able to screen. Unsure if the high readings are from all the venting/air movement or chronic high levels from long-term exposure.  

Joyce Ackerman with EPA is still in Denver, looks like Sat at the earliest before she can get out.  She is in frequent contact with her contractor.  The contractor will likely vent through the night but it sounds like removal work will stop soon and begin again in the morning.

UPDATE 12/21/06 4:04 PM DERR SA Sec. Mngr.
At least one condo unit impacted, probably more. EPA-ERB is mobilizing out of Denver. However,DIA is closed due to snow so the OSC, Joyce Ackerman, and the Technical contractor, URS, will be delayed until at least 12/22.  EPA sent their local response contractor, Environmental Restoration, to the scene the evening of (12/21/06), UDEQ will provide oversight until Joyce can make it to town.  Alan V. Jones will be onsite the evening of 12/21/06.   

12/21/2006 11:00
DERR received a call late this morning from Davis Co. Health asking us to assist in monitoring a mercury spill at a Centerville residence.  Details are limited:  Mercury was discovered in a ground-floor unit.  Workers were replacing a water heater in a duplex unit when they noticed mercury on the floor beneath the water heater.  The building consists of an 12-unit condominium complex.  It has been reported that an individual present prior to the arrival of authorities may have attempted to use a regular vacuum in an attempt to remove the mercury.  Lincoln Environmental was contacted to conduct a cleanup, however, Lincoln does not possess the instrumentation necessary to provide appropriate monitoring capability for mercury vapor.  Davis County requested technical assistance from UDEQ to provide necessary monitoring capability.   A UDEQ Duty Officer has responded.  Additional information will posted via updates as it is made available.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
The caller was complaining of a "burning smell" or a "fertilizer" smell in the air in the neighborhood where she lives (12th East and 3rd South) and also in the area of the University of Utah.  She did not know the source of the odor, nor what exactly the odor was.  She did say, however, that it was making both her and her daughter sick with headaches.  Response:  I notified both Dale Keller with SLVHD and Bob Dalley with DAQ.  Dale drove up to the area where the caller lived to check out the odor.  I later talked with him and he told me he could smell a very faint, indistinguishable odor in the air, noticeable only because he was made aware of it.  His PID did not detect anything.  He contacted a few fire stations in the area and the Salt Lake Dispatch, none of which reported any calls complaining of odors.  As Bob Dalley had pointed out, the valley was undergoing an inversion and noisome odors are not unusual during such conditions.

Dale passed on the caller’s name and phone number to the Salt Lake Health Department, whose on-call nurse will contact the family first thing Thursday morning to follow up on any ill health affects or symptoms from the odor.  He pointed out to me that his ER crew has access to an on-call team of doctors, nurses, and epidemiologists to deal with such health affects with the public.  All that Dale has to do is page them and they are available 24-7 for incidents in the Salt Lake Valley.

name: Pipeline leak in Book Cliffs
incident_summary:
The phone number for Slate Resources is (435) 781-1870.   Hector reported the spill on Monday the 9th, around 1pm.   His phone number is  (801) 259-6110.

David Hackford of DOGM visited the site Tuesday morning at approximately 9am, and he reported that the 8-inch diameter pipeline was leaking a small amount of natural gas under relatively low pressure, and that some condensate liquids had leaked out of the pipeline and covered a small area of ground near the pipeline.  Dave called Slate River's contractor (the "pumper", not sure who that was) and told them to fix the leak ASAP.  

SITLA staff (Sonja Wallace, Jim Davis and Scott Bartlett) and I also visited the site at approximately 11:30am on Tuesday, and found things as Dave had described.  The contractor had not responded yet to fix the leak, but it was raining at the time and weather was a factor in getting equipment to the scene.  The leak was small and not too serious, due to the low pressure in the line at the time.  The condensate spill was very localized, as Dave had described.  We did not collect any samples due to the very localized nature of the condensate spill, which had only run about 5 or 6 feet from the pipeline.  The spill is small and should be very easy to clean up.

Surface water was not affected, the nearest would be Willow Creek, which is over 3 miles away from this location.  It was raining at the time, so there was some stormwater runoff.

Darrin knows about this spill, he was going to join us for our site visit but had another commitment at the time.

The easement for the pipeline is held by Slate River Resources, LLC, 418 E Main, Vernal, 84078.  The easement was approved in February of 2006.  It is described as an 8-inch natural gas gathering pipeline that transports gas from wells in the Agency Draw area to market.  It crosses trust land in Section 2, T13S, R20E, and terminates in Section 35, T12S, R20E, where it connects to another pipeline.

name: Sevier County - Damaged Mositure Density Gauge
incident_summary:
On November 14, 2013, the Division of Radiation Control was notified that a moisture density gauge was run over by a vehicle.  A gauge operator from Hales Sand and Gravel was at a temporary job site to perform soil moisture density measurements. After taking a moisture density measurement the gauge operator left the gauge sitting on the ground while he walked away to talk to the roller operator. The gauge was left in the backing up path of a grader and was run over.

After everyone was cleared out of the area, the Radiation Safety Officer of Jones & Demille Engineering was contacted to provide a survey instrument.  At the time of the incident the radioactive sources were in the safe shielded position.  After the gauge was run over, the gauge was broken into two pieces; the source rod was separated from the shielding block but was still in one piece. Upon arrival, the Radiation Safety Officer verified that the radioactive sources were still intact and attached to the source rod.  Additional shielding was added and the damaged gauge was placed into a transportation container and removed from the job site.  The site was surveyed and no residual contamination was detected.
title_eventname: Sevier County - Damaged Mositure Density Gauge

name: Parowan - Contaminated mine tailings
incident_summary:
Justin Wayment, Parowan city attorney, received a packet of information from a John Anderson, regarding hazardous mine tailings that Mr. Anderson entered into a contract with a Mr. Eric Flippo, to transport from Arizona to Parowan.

Mr. Anderson believes that no permits have been acquired to receive or treat the tailings, and that they are being stored improperly.  He has previously hired at least one individual, Roger Bowers, a geologist, to manage sampling and analysis of the waste through a lab.  Mr. Anderson has also recently hired Hill West Environmental out of Park City, to conduct further investigation. Initial analysis is believed to indicate reportable quantities of several metals, including arsenic, beryllium, mercury, and many others.

To date, Mr. Anderson says he has transported 47 tons of the material.  Mr. Anderson was originally solicited to transport 1 million tons to the site, and is concerned about potential affects to the environment and people in the community.  Mr. Wayment, attorney for Parowan City, states that the city municipal well is located approximately 1/4 mile from the location of the waste pile.

name: Iron County Tar Pit Complaint
incident_summary:
Ms. Brown was walking her four dogs in the area of the map coordinates.  All four dogs became trapped in a pit containing a tar like material.  She estimates the pit to be approximately 20 feet by 30 feet.  She called the county sheriff's department for assistance.

Several deputies from the Iron County Sheriff's department along with officers the Cedar City Police department and the Cedar City Fire department arrived and the scene and were able to remove the dogs from the material.  According to Ms. Brown, three of the four dogs have been treated by a vet following the incident.

The pit is located near land owned by the Cedar Livestock Association and approximately 1/4 mile from some railroad tracks.  Ms. Brown thinks the material in the pit could be railroad generated waste but she is not sure of this.  At least one deputy told her that the material had been there since he was a kid, 20 to 30 years ago.

The paraffin wax crude gels in cold and did not penetrate the soils.  All impacts were within the oil containment area with no waterways impacted.

Envirocare responded and has completed cleanup activities removing crude and surface soils into roll-off containers.

<1,000 gallon reporting requirement for EPA notification.

name: UPDATE Cottonwood Heights -- Potential dumping
address: 2985 E. Cottonwood Parkway, Cottonwood Heights, UT
address_location: 2985 E. Cottonwood Parkway, Cottonwood Heights, UT
incident_summary: Complainant observed a white liquid with a smell like paint or another chemical that had been dumped into the stream bed of Big Cottonwood Creek.  The complainant stated that they walk the creek daily and did not see it yesterday, suggesting it had been dumped overnight.  UPDATE (11/7/2019, 22:00):  John Hoggan with the SLVHD called DERR to report that on investigation, the source of the discharge (white material with a chemical odor) originated from the east side of the Regence Blue Cross Blue Shield Bldg. at 2890 E. Cottonwood Parkway.  As of 18:30 on 11/7/2019, the discharge material had traveled from the BCBS Bldg. to approximately 350 feet down Big Cottonwood Creek.  Samples were collected from beneath a condenser unit at the BCBS Bldg. where the discharge material appeared to originate from, a storm drain box, and Big Cottonwood Creek.  John Hoggan then contacted Craig Laehn with Cambia Health about the discharged material and received a reply from John Bernatz, the Alliance Director with CBRE Global Workplace Solutions, Cambia Health.  Mr. Bernatz stated the effluent is an innocuous fluid similar to vegetable oil from the cooling towers due to flushing.

name: U Store It (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Greater than 20 pounds of mercury was found spilled from glass and plastic containers after a storage shed contents auction.  The renter did not pay their rent which led to the auction.  Salt Lake Valley Health will hold the storage company, auction winner or previous owner liable for hiring a cleanup contractor.   The auction winner is Dustin Service 535 E. Main, Castledale, (435) 749-2041.  DERR contacted Mr. Service in route to Castledale.  He is returning the unloaded materials back to U Stor It.  Utah OSHA was contacted as they may have a role in clearing the commercial site for employee use.  The person who abandoned the shed contents has reportedly been identified.

UPDATE 5/25/06@12:56 - TW Company, under contract with U Store It, is in the process today of cleaning mercury contamination directly outside the storage unit as well as within the storage unit.  About 1 quart of mercury was found spilled on the floor of the storage unit.  Eventually storage units to the sides and behind the contaminated unit will also be monitored.  Dustin Service (who purchased the contaminated unit contents) returned the potentially contaminated contents of the storage unit to U Store It in his closed storage trailer.  Mr. Service removed his potentially contaminated shoes and clothing, bagged these materials, and left them in the trailer before returning to his home in Castledale.  His truck cab will eventually be monitored for contamination.  Initial monitoring of the trailer gave readings of 10,000 ng/m3.  U Store It has agreed to dispose of the trailer contents.  Salt Lake County Health Department received permission from Ita Williams for response staff to monitor the Williams home.  EPA will use the DEQ Lumex monitor, as their unit batteries are low.  The home will be monitored at 1:30 p.m. today.

UPDATE 26May06@16:15 - Paul Peronard, OSC, EPA, reports the incident response is complete.  TW Company, cleanup contractor for UStoreIt, completed work this afternoon.  TW will dispose of the storage unit/trailer contents and investigation derived waste.  The trailer containing the storage unit items was screened and cleared for release.  A second trailer, earlier suspected to be contaminated, was screened and found to be mercury free.

name: Performance Painting Co. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller witnessed employee or representative of above named PRP dumping gasoline down a storm drain at the date and time recorded above. Caller estimates it was 2-5 gallons.  Caller attempted to approach the actor who hastily finished and drove away.  in a company vehicle (Utah license 320-UWJ).   Caller said he could smell gasoline eminating from the drain.  Storm drain is located about 40 feet from PRP's bay door and in the middle lot bewteen two identical warehouse facilities.  Caller witnessed a similar unrelated incident back in Nov. 08.  Caller believes the material dumped was paint thinner.  Facility is approximately one mile from Utah Lake.
UPDATE 1/29/09 @ 11:17 - UCHD visited location 1/28/09, 3:05 PM. Met with Mr. Scott Holyoak, Owner, Performance Painting Co. Mr. Holyoak was already aware of the incident and had done an internal investigation. He explained that a container of gasoline had been used to fill a piece of the companies equipment. A worker then wished to reuse the container and he filled it with soap and water to wash out the residual gasoline. Rather than properly disposing of the solution when finished, he dumped it in the storm drain. Mr. Holyoak stated that he is aware that this is an improper method of disposal and that he has already reprimanded the employee. He also stated that he plans to increase the frequency of proper waste disposal discussions during the company's periodic staff meetings.  Inspected the storm drain where the dumping had taken place. Drain is an approx. 3'x3' sump-type vault. Did not note any petroleum odors or observe excessive pooling or sheens of what might be gasoline on the vault's standing water surface. Gasoline that may have entered drain appears to be of a de minimis amount.

name: Diesel Spill Hospital Central Plant Bldg
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a diesel fuel release from a backup emergency generator on the roof of the central plant building.  They believe the release resulted from an overfill control malfunction.  Diesel overflowed onto the gravel and asphalt roof, into a roof drain and down into a storm drain.  Estimated volume of release is 5 gallons.  The release has been secured.  Crew has deployed absorbents.  They believe they will have to replace that portion of the roof material that is impacted. name: Utah Metal Works (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: The reporting party lives at 855 W. 1500 N., but also owns nearby residences at 866 W. Everett Ave. and 854 Everett Ave.  He has the following complaints about Utah Metal Works (UMWs) and the general area surrounding that firm:  (1) surface water (with an oily sheen, but which may also be a breeding site for mosquitoes) ponds in the street area immediately north of UMWs following storm events, (2) UMW frequently moves heavy equipment across Everett Ave. (a SLC street) without using a flagman, (3) UMW frequently drives large track hoes on Everett Ave. (which is a paved SLC street), and leaves large track hoes and other heavy equipment parked on city streets overnight (at the east end of 1500 N.) without warning lights, (4) there is a nasty odor and probable contamination from the UMWs operations that burn insulation from electrical wire and smelt scrap metal, and (5) the SLC concrete sidewalk north of UMWs has been covered with soil or destroyed by UMWs activities.  In addition, surface water in the drainage ditch (which flows west) located on the north side of Everett Ave. at 866 W. frequently has waste oil in it which he thinks it is being placed into the ditch further to the east.  He is also concerned about the containerized chemicals (reportedly purchased from HAFB) and wastes stored at 905 W 1500 N. (owned by Norman Fife) where vehicles and junk are also parked or stored on the public road.  I advised the reporting party that DS&HW is involved in a PCB cleanup on the UMWs site and DERR CERCLA Branch is conducting a Site Re-Assessment of UMWs.  The reporting party is anxious to provide further information regarding his complaints; he can best be reached via telephone early in the morning or late in the evening.

Caller waited until he got home to call in his concerns.  No material reached the storm drain.  The released material was not identified as to content by the caller. Lund called back to report (20:00 hrs) that no attempts to clean up material was being made until he arrived on the scene and made inquiries.  The facility has a lab and these personnel told Lund the material was a process rinsate material that contained Benzophenone (CAS 119-61-9, 30-60%), sodium hydroxide, Ristone-R, and has a high Ph (basic) value of 12 or higher.  Lund felt some of the plant employees were less than forthcoming and uncooperative while he was there. address: Approx. 3.3 miles East of Monticello UTM (N 4193092, E 651208)
address_location: Approx. 3.3 miles East of Monticello UTM (N 4193092, E 651208)
incident_summary:
San Juan Co Emergency Management received notification last night from the County Sheriff who received notification from a UHP Sargeant.  Suspect at least three heavy-duty plastic totes (type encaged in re-bar style shell) were dumped/anbandoned from or near the bridge along Highway 491 that passes over Vega Creek.  UHP reported an odor of diesel fuel.  Vega Creek eventually empties into Montezuema Creek which discharges into the San Juan River.  The totes appear to be empty.

UPDATE 1/29/13 14:42 - From San Juan Co Emergency Mngt: Totes were discovered coincidentally.  There are four.  Scene evidence indicates the containers were dumped, let roll down to their present location or otherwise abandoned.  Markings on totes include: "Mobil Delvac 1300", "Advantage Foamer HD 1" (used in drilling operations; generic internet search shows this material to be 2-Butoxyethanol).  The container with foamer has 10-15 gallons of residual and a sample was collected.  Handwritten notes dated 2012 were afixed to the totes indicative of volumetric numbers.  Investigators were not able to determine the meaning.  Totes appear to be on highway right-of-way.  Both sides of the right-of-way are bounded by private property.  A sheen was observed on both the north and south sides of Highway 491.  Totes have 275 gallon capacity.

UPDATE 1/31/2013 - US EPA has determined that the information provided on an MSDS for at least one of the materials identified as being dumped meets the criteria as a hazardous waste as defined under RCRA.

UPDATE 2/15/13 10:51 from County EM - EPA OSC was on-scene yesterday.  Additional evidence indicates that the totes were drained intentionally with piping from the road down to the water.  EPA will proceed with cleanup.  Due to weather, that will likely commence next week.  EPA has tentatively assumed possession of the totes. County law enforcement is investigating commercial history of the totes to distributor.  History is is not clear beyond the distributor.

UPDATE 2/19/13 16:40 from County EM - EPA is on-scene with two USCG personnel and a 20-man contract hazmat/removal team.  The investigation team suspects the material(s) in the totes is not consistent with material identification of the labeling.  Removal team is planning logistics.  Samples have been collected and sent for analysis.  EPA has taken possession of initial samples collected by local authorities and totes.

name: Alcoa Extrusions Corp. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Breakdown of scrubber unit.  Facility has two 250-gallon 50% solution sodium hydroxide tanks heated to between 160-180 degrees Fahrenheit.  Heating generates NaOH mist that is then passed into influent air flow feeding the scrubber unit.  Permit requires a flow rate of NaOH of no less than 40gal/min.  Screen in valve became plugged which dropped the rate of flow to 38 gal/min. hence this report.  Decreased flow rate may cause the pH in the scrubber to fluctuate and and bump the emissions to levels that are outside of permit values.   NaOH is used to clean dies of aluminium after extrusion process.  Although the flow rate is back within compliance limits -at 42 gal/min.- it is still below the normal rate of 50-55 gals/min. at which the unit typically operates.  The caller believes there still exists an obstruction in a valve in the system causing the reduced flow rate and has a crew investigating.  The caller anticipates that they will take the scrubber off-line today to correct the situation.  The Off-line/On-line process causes permit level exceptions  - caller will reports these when they occur.

name: North Davis Sewer Upset
incident_summary: Good afternoon Dan, I hope all finds you well. I would like to report a potential plant process upset. While performing a chlorine tank inspection I had the maintenance staff drain the District’s scrubber over a period of 10 hours into the effluent to repair some leaks we have been dealing with between the tank and the isolation valves. It appears I may have miss calculated the overall effect it would have on the plant at our current flow. I felt our dilution effect would minimize the effect of the caustic. Early this morning we had a call in for low chlorine residual, which when the responding operators performed a field residual we were still good to go and the meter was just not functioning. When the lab pulled our regulatory residual sample and PH grab we were ok but have approached the upper limit of our permit on PH. As of the time of this e-mail we have not seen any numbers that would be a violation but three of the numbers  (BOD5,TSS, and E-Coli) will not be known until Friday and next Tuesday. I know for a fact it has caused some sloughing of our biomass on our trickling filters and biotower.  I will keep you posted on the above potential upset as the numbers are received.

name: Red Butte - Chevron Pipeline Oil Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported that oil had been seen in the Liberty Park Lake.  The Fire Dept. arrived on-scene during the phone call.  Fire Dept. personnel informed DERR that a pipeline had ruptured at Red Butte Gardens and crude oil had flowed into Red Butte Creek and Liberty Park Lake.  An incident command post had been established and Battalion Chief Carsen was named as the Incident Commander (801-550-0108).  Police and Salt Lake Public Utilities were also on-scene.  A fire was reported in connection with the crude oil spill of unknown causes but it is speculated that the source might have been from lightening strikes that occurred in the area.  Chevron Pipeline later reported that the ruptured pipeline was 10 inches in diameter and had been shut down.  Chevron reported to the NRC that the spill had reached the Jordan River.  Joseph White with Chevron reported that the pipeline is buried and the exact location of the rupture will not be known until the pipeline is excavated.  At that time Chevron engineers will be able to calculate how much oil was released based on the size of the rupture, time of release, and the rate of flow.  Chevron has clean-up crews on-site and more crews from North Salt Lake are being mobilized.  EPA Region 8 has been notified.  On-scene coordinator, Tien Nguyen, is expected to arrive in Salt Lake City on 6/12/10 at 20:30 hours.  He can be reached at 303-886-1637. UPDATE (6/12/10, 11:15):  Eric McCauley with the Legacy Nature Preserve (801-520-2505) called with concerns about the crude oil spill impacting the wetlands.  UPDATE (6/12/10, 19:30):  Bob Carey with Homeland Security (801-544-5957) requested a representative from water quality attend a meeting at the Salt Lake City EOC on 06/13/10 at 10:00 to discuss how far downstream the oil plume has gone since there have been conflicting reports.

name: Ogden Compass Minerals Diesel
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting the release of ~500 gallon of diesel fuel from a fuel truck as the result of a fire. The fuel and water was released to soils and containment on site, but some escaped the containment. They deployed booms and dykes to contain the release. It made it to a ditch and culvert that connects with the East Ditch and from there to their UPDES outfall to the Great Salt Lake. They are going to sample to identify if any got past the countermeasures in the culvert,  and continue cleanup. Lincoln Environmental was on site assisting with cleanup. Caller will notify NRC

Results of sampling to be reported to DEQ, and forwarded to WMHD.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller left message - states smelling awful odor and believes business neighbor may be dumping down the drain.  Numerours attempts have been made to contact the caller.  Line has been either busy or unanswered.

name: Murray - Wastewater backup
incident_summary: Caller reported a wastewater back-up that impacted a storm drain and approximately 500 gallons entered the Jordan River.  Release has been secured.  The SLVHD were on scene to monitor clean-up.  Clean-up will be complete around 4 p.m.  Caller was advised to contact the NRC.

name: Consolidated Freightways (Null RP Substituted)

name: Mercury Spill - Utah County
incident_summary: Substance thought to be mercury spilled on a couch in a residential house that has children present.  Caller was instructed to attempt to remove as much mercury from the couch as possible using an eye dropper, and to keep children and people away from the couch.

name: Peck  Rock (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports the repeated dumping of some type of hazardous waste in a pit less than 100 yards west of the address location in the Peck Rock facility..  The local fire department has been on-site and conducted some of field tests.  The local health department has also been on-site but the dumping reportedly continues.  A strong chemical smell comes into their home.

Update---From NRC report and EPA OSC  Steven Way ---Several people have gone to doctors and the hospital as result of exposure to the chemical smell.  The mayor and 911 system has been used several times by many people in the neighborhood.  

The fire marshal ( Tam Hay) indicates that he went to the site last weekend.  He says the smell starts about 8:30 p.m. and stings your eyes and throat.  He says the smell is quite strong.

The local health department and the fire marshal requested that we bring in EPA to provide a more robust monitoring capability.  We (Dale, Brent, Neil) have coordinated this request for EPA assistance with Matt Sullivan with the Division of Solid and Hazardous Waste because a possible source of the smell is a nearby construction landfill (Peck Rock).  He will be the point person with EPA. 

The EPA in responding OSC will be Al Lange.  He should be here within 24 hours.

Ralph Bohn with the Division of Solid and Hazardous Waste visited the landfill on the evening of August 3.  He reports that there appears to be a fire in the working face of the landfill.  Al Lange will be on site by the evening of August 4.

Update - Matt Sullivan will be joining the EPA OSC and representatives from the Utah County Health Department to visit the Peck Rock landfill this evening.  The landfill owner will be given an opportunity to develop a plan to identify and extinguish the landfill fire.  EPA resources will likely be available if the landfill owner does not have the capability.

Ralph Bohn indicates that there is a very strong smell of fire downwind of the landfill.  It is not a chemical smell.  The fire is not visually observable.

name: Spanish Fork - Unknown Chemical Release
incident_summary: Caller reported that an unknown chemical vapor sent 11 students from the college to the hospital.  Students were cleaning their work stations when they reported feeling dizzy and nauseous. The release was initially believed to be a carbon monoxide leak but Questar Gas was able to rule out the possibility. The release is currently believed to be related to a possible chemical exposure from the cleaning chemicals. The affected students were taken to the hospital and the school evacuated as a precautionary measure. The Spanish Fork Fire Dept. was on-scene.

name: Ethylene Glycol Release
incident_summary:
Caller reported that 1030 gallons of ethylene glycol were released at a well site approximately 8 to 10 miles southwest of Myton.  The RQ for ethylene glycol is 5000 pounds.  The caller reported that it weighs 9.29 pounds per gallon making the release over 9568 pounds.

The glycol ran off the well site and down a road and into a dry drainage, there was no water in the drainage at the time.  It then flowed approximately 150 feet down the drainage.  Approximately 200 gallons entered the drainage.  The drainage was dammed and the flow stopped.  They used a pump truck to suck up all the liquid in the drainage then began to remove the contaminated soil.  The soil will be stockpiled at the well site then transferred to Environmental Energy Inovations where it will be remediated.

The well site was number 8-33-8-16 and is located south east of the north east quarter quarter of section 33, 8 south 16 east.

name: This is a Drill.  Truck Accident Near Leeds
incident_summary:
THIS IS A DRILL                            THIS IS ONLY AN EXERCISE
 
Semi-tractor trailer pulling double trailers is hit by a gust of wind and overturned at approximately I-15, mile marker 20 (37.206368°N 113.394840°W). 
 
The saddle tanks of diesel are ruptured and flowing toward/into a stream that discharges into Quail Creek Reservoir and State Park less than 1/2 mile downstream. There is a sheen on the water. The trailers have DOT placards Flammable Liquids UN 1090, Corrosives UN 1790, UN 2031 and UN 1789. There are multiple drums that appear to be leaking, including drums with red labels others with black and white labels. Near some of the drums that appear to be leaking there are mist clouds of white vapors and others are putting out red fumes. There are more than 20 drums near the water that may be compromised. Several close bystanders appear to be coughing or choking.
title_eventname: This is a Drill.  Truck Accident Near Leeds

Some of the oil did enter a storm drain.  Pads were placed on the ground and in the stom drain and a vac truck has been dispatched to assist.

name: Hydraulic Oil 50 gal. - Hurricane
incident_summary:
Location is unknown.  Address given was for St. George, but this address could be in Hurricane, Ivins or New Harmony.  Location update has been requested. 

Caller is reporting a spill of approximately 50-gallons of hydraulic oil from a ruptured line on a residential garbage truck.

Water was seen in the area around the storm drain but this is believed to have come from one of the trucks at the construction site that was carrying water.  A clean-up company has been called to assess and clean up the spill.

name: SLC Airport - Fuel in Storm Drain
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a small fuel spill that was detected in the airport storm drain system.  The source of the spill is unknown but is likely Jet A.

A sheen was observed today in the wet well near the airport outfall.

The airport fire department was notified and EnviroCare was contracted for cleanup.  450 gallons of water was vacuumed out of the adjacent canal and absorbent booms were placed in the canal.  The canal is on airport property and is upstream of their oil water separator before it leaves the airport.  

Ken will try to identify the source asap, but likely from the storm event over this past weekend that washed residual product into the system.  He is not concerned of additional fuel getting to the system at this time.

name: Layton - Possible oil contaminated soil

Caller contacted Layton City but the city did not observe anything unusual about the soils.  Caller believes additional testing of the soils may be warranted. name: Juab Co - Tractror Rollover
address: I-15 Approximately 2 miles north of Sevier River bridge
address_location: I-15 Approximately 2 miles north of Sevier River bridge
incident_summary: Richard reported that a gasoline tanker with a 10,000 gallon trailer and a 4,000 gallon pup had rolled into the median of I-15.  The 4,000 gallon tanker was burning and the fire was impinging on the the 10,000 gallon tank.  The fire departments from Levan and Scipio did not have enough water supplies to prevent a BLEVE so they had backed off one mile and closed I-15 in both directions while they waited for additional support or a BLEVE.  All product that may have been leaking from either tank was burning so it was not believed that there was any potential impact to any water bodies.  At 10:07 PM Mr. Joe Butler ((863) 559-4306 cell, (863) 533-2000, ext 270 office) from American Compliance Technologies contacted me to report that his company had been hired to respond as the clean up contractor.  He had dispatched a crew from Salt Lake to the scene.  He was going to call the NRC.  On the morning of Jan. 14, 2013 I spoke to Mr. Butler again.  He reported that the fire departments were successful in extinguishing the fire.  His crew reported that there was no product on the ground, that anything that had leaked had burned.  At approximately 11 AM they had planned to off-load any remaining product from the tankers and his crew would be on-site to assist and clean up any spilled product.

name: unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:

A homeowner with the address of 765 Richmond Drive in Silver Summit Utah found mercury underneath his home entry carpeting. name: Petroleum Wholesalers (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported the release of 900 gallons of gasoline into a storm drain.  A customer at the Chevron noticed a strong odor of gasoline at 09:00 and notified 911.  Local Fire Dept. and SLVHD responded to the scene to find small standing puddles and staining to indicate a recent gasoline spill.  2-3 downgradient storm drains were inspected.  Vapors were detected inside the drains.  No free product was seen inside the drains indicating spill likely moved through the storm-water system and into Mill Creek.  Records inside the the Chevron and the bill of lading from the fuel delivery driver indicate that there are 900 gallons of gasoline unaccounted for.  Store records indicate that the tank overfill alarm went off for 6 minutes.

RESPONSE:  SLVHD has hired a contractor to clean out the 2-3 downgradient drains as a precaution.  Case will be referred to the County DA.

UPDATE 1 2/26/09 07:28:  Information received in an e-mail from Eric Larson (DNR).  Ray Loken (District Conservation Officer - Central Region) walked Mill Creek both above and below 2300 East in Salt Lake City.  In the stretch between 2300 east and 1945 east he found and photographed 5 dead brown trout.  Above 2300 east only live fish were found.  The stream was flowing swiftly and was narrower and deeper in places that could easily flush dead fish further downstream or lodge them under water where they coul not be found.  One of the trout was in the process of swallowing a younger relative when it died and several of the fish looked seriously undernourished.  There were no detectable odors or visible sheens in the water.

name: Bergman transportation (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Company vehicle was hit by another truck causing a spill of diesel and fuel gas.  Approximately 200 to 400 gallons was spilled in the median.  Caller states soil is frozen and DOT indicated cleanup would began after the holiday weekend.
--------------------Update-----------------------------
I am slowly getting more information on the gasoline/diesel fuel spill on I-15.  It appears that the trucking company out of California (TPG) is taking the lead on the clean up.  It was their tanker truck that was struck by a Werner truck, which caused the major spill.  According to their records for what was pumped out of the wrecked tanker truck, they estimate about 400 gallons of a gasoline and diesel mixture was lost.  I guess the tanker was struck right at the seam between the diesel and gasoline storage compartments causing both products to be spilled.
 
According to Brad Johnson from TPG, they have sampled the soil at the spill site and are waiting for results of those initial samples.  He is working on getting an encroachment permit from UDOT so they can access the spill site and remove the soil.  Brad plans to use local contractors for that work.  He also asked if there was somewhere local that could take the contaminated soil and I suggested that he find a suitable place to land farm it until the soil is treated to a level where the Iron County landfill could accept it.  Maybe this is a question for Jon Parry?  Will that work Jon?  Or do we need to do something different?
 
In addition to the tanker spill, the Werner truck that crashed into the tanker also lost some diesel fuel when his truck jack knifed and ruptured one of his fuel tanks.  I'm not sure of the amount of diesel lost from this truck.  I am trying to get contact information for the Werner truck from the UHP trooper that helped take the accident report.
 
I will continue to follow up on this and I am open to suggestions for telling them what should be done with the contaminated soil.
 
John Chartier

name: Salt Flats - Unexploded Ordinance Tooele

Caller stated there is approximately 5 pounds of explosive in the ordinance discovered on the Salt Flats.  HAFB will dispose of (detonate) the ordinance on-site and will not transport.  

The Tooele County Sheriff Dept called HAFB EOD to report the discovery earlier today.  HAFB is working with Tooele County EMS, the FAA and other agencies for proper approvals and the DEQ line is on his list to call.  

ADDITIONAL INFO...

MAP LOCATION IS NOT ACCURATE AND COORDINATES WERE NOT AVAILABLE.

Also, Justin Beard, HAFB EOD will follow up on Monday with a formal report to all agencies involved.

The incident report was forwarded to Marty Gray with DAQ.

Based on an internet search the Running Horse Pipeline Company appears to be part of Navajo Nation Oil and Gas.

Duc Nguyen, EPA Region 8 OSC, received  a call from local emergency management at about 1530 hours.  He then spoke with Jim Hook with Bluff FD. Jim informed him that a Bluff FD rep responded.  Duc said the release from a 16" pipeline owned and operated by the Navajo Reservation, Running Horse Pipeline.  They reported that it did not enter the river but is about 150 yards away.  They said the contractor is "on top of it" and has it secured the release unless it rains and then it could possibly be carried to the river.  Duc did not know the volume of the release. 

Additional information indicates this release occurred from a gathering system line and flowed approximately 400+ feet to the northeast from the point of release.

name: South Salt Lake Jmac Radiator
incident_summary:
Online citizen complaint was forwarded Denver OSHA office to DWQ. Edited report included.
1-800Radiator which is the same location as Jmac Radiator. The place is a toxic wasteland. There are  buckets, ect on the dock and all over the place. Workers are exposed to the fumes every day and are always very bad. The fumes in the hallway to the bathroom make you sick on Saturdays, and the bathroom sink fumes are extemely noxious at ALL times, getting worse when water is added. Everyone is exposed to this.  The owners father (Jerry McKenna) has been coming in every Saturday and pumping the sludge tank. The shop manager, Keith Lewis, was informed two weeks ago of this 2 weeks ago. (so they can't claim they didn't know). It was suspected that they were pumping the tank into the sewer drain, but was confirmed today (April 6). The hose from the sludge tank was being pumped directly into the toilet in their back bathroom. The water in the toilet was brown and was 100% from the sludge tank. This was captured on video. Jerry McKenna caught they tape being made and was told it would be turned into the EPA, he may have covered his tracks. Greg McKenna has been fined before for violating the clean water act at their location in Ogden. He has no concern for the wellbeing of people, just money. In addition- the parking lot drain is always flooding when it rains and you can see all the oil\etc floating in it. Workers are exposed to dust from them blowing things out on the dock (like a diesel air cooler that covered everything in our warehouse with black soot) and from them painting on the dock, and also heavy metal dust.The dock by the radiator shop is often covered in white\silver powder. In Dec their shop flooded after Jerry came in and pumped the tank on a Saturday. Monday morning everyone arrived and the radiator shop was flooded, it even went through the walls into the warehouse. Employees got very sick, one ended up in the hospital with pneumonia and half their hair has fallen out and has bones\muscles pains. They submitted a hair test for toxic metals in February and in addition to lower levels of other toxic metals it showed high levels of tungsten, lead and uranium. Employees have probably been exposed to methyl glycol, benzene, toulene, xylene, etc.etc. There is a pregnant girl up front who has had a very difficult pregnancy and been sick alot also. Currently the shop service writer has been in the intensive care unit for 2 months (most likely related to weight and diabetes but could have also been influenced by toxins as he eats his lunch back by the radiator shop).

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
An employee at a McDonald's Restaurant (3900 South 1100 East, 265-9771) found a glass gar of mercury inside a WalMart bag in the McDonald's parking lot.  The employee brought the jar into the restaurant, and accidentally dropped it, releasing mercury on the floor of the work area.  

Response: Rolf Larsen (w/SLVHD) responded to the scene, shut down the McDonald's, and took readings with a Jerome meter of 170-300 micrograms/cubic meter.  About 1/4 to 1/2 cup of mercury was released.  TW was called to do the cleanup.  S.L. Fire Dept. was also called.  Fortunately, the employees had not attempted to vacuum the mercury.  

By Sunday morning, after TW had already done two cleanups, Jerome readings were still high (up to 107).  More mercury was found in a stainless steel lower wall.  TW performed a third cleanup.  

Rolf was going to get readings to below 10 microgm/cu. meter before allowing the McDonald's to reopen.

By Sunday afternoon at 4pm, Rolf had readings of below 10 ug/m3 in the work and customer area, and below 1.0 ug/m3 in the play area.  The restaurant re-opened Sunday evening.  

Rolf is going out this afternoon (Monday) to do a follow-up visit and make sure readings are still below 10 ug/m3.

UPDATE 9/12/07 by  J. D. Keetley: Rolf Larsen (w/SLVHD) re-visited the McDonald’s restaurant Monday (9/10) and took more readings for mercury vapors.  He reported the values were about the same as previously, but they were not down to the ATSDR recommended level of 3 ug/m3.  Kevin Okleberry went there Tuesday (9/11) and took more readings: they were still above 3 ug/m3, generally in the 4, 5, and 6 ug/m3 range.

They will continue to monitor the site today (9/12) to see if levels drop to below 3 ug/m3.

UPDATE 9/18/07: Kevin Okleberry w/SLVHD reported that all levels at the McDonald's restaurant were below the 3 ug/m3 threshold as of yesterday, Monday, Sept. 17.

name: Harper Excavating (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reported that as they were driving through Parley's Canyon on I-80, there were billowing clouds of dust across the Interstate apparently coming from the Harper Quarry located right off the highway at around mile marker 131.

Response:  SLVHD, UHP, and DAQ were notified that evening of the situation.  UHP said they would send someone up there to investigate;  SLVHD and DAQ said they would contact Harper about it on Monday.

name: Springville - Ammonia Release
incident_summary:
Caller reported an update to National Response Center (NRC) regarding Incident Report #1063247.  In the initial NRC Report  #1063247, Nestle Foods reported that the mechanical plate in a plate freezer tilted causing a release of anhydrous ammonia to the air/atmosphere.  The updated information indicated that 75 lbs. of ammonia was released during the event.  

The updated information was received in NRC Incident Report #1063852.

name: Union Pacific Railroad Roper Yard (Lane Sheppick) (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Union Pacific Railroad Roper Yard (Lane Sheppick)
incident_summary: Skimmer drain line plugged on an oil-water separation tank causing release of an approximately 20 gallons of an oil-water mixture.  Release was discovered this morning and believed to have occurred some time last night.  UPRR Critical Call Center  was notified 9 minutes ago.  Contractor Pacific West is on-site to remediate.  Spill was fully contained and did not impact surface waters.
title_eventname: Union Pacific Railroad Roper Yard (Lane Sheppick) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Andy Costa (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Two truck trailers were found abandoned in an industrial park along Wallace Rd.  The trailers contained  40 fifty-five gallon drums (polymer and steel type) with unknown material inside each.  One drum had split and was leaking a small amount (4 0z) of material (powder) out of the trailer door and onto the ground.  A local fire department hazmat team abated the hazard.  SLVHD personnel gathered a sample and delivered it to he state lab for characterization.  The sample will be tested for heavy metals and ph.  The material released is described as a green and brown solid.  DERR was called by the EPA (Johanna Miller) OSC in Denver, she is monitoring this event and offered help if SLVHD would request assistance.  DERR relayed this info and the OSC phone number to SLVHD.

name: Used Engine Gear Oil Spill
incident_summary: 330 Gallon tote of used drilling rig engine gear oil was being off-loaded with a fork-lift for transfer to a facility used oil tank.  The tote slipped off the forks, tipped and spilled.   Incident occurred within a concrete and asphalt and bermed containment area.  An estimated five to ten gallons splashed to soils outside of the containment.    Cleanup is underway.  As of this time upwards of 200 gallons have been recovered.    Absorbents and floor-dry have been deployed.  Contaminated soils are being excavated and drummed for disposal.   No impact to surface waters or sewers.

name: FedEx (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: 200 gallons of diesel fuel spilled from a truck’s saddle tanks during a crash.  50 gallons of the spill impacted soil  adjacent to I-215.  The spill was remediated by TW company.

name: THATCHER CHEMICAL (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A RELEASE OF CHLORINE OCCURED WHEN A LINE RUPTURED ON AN EMPTY TRAILER.  THE VALVE WAS STUCK AND IT TOOK A FEW MOMENTS TO CLOSE.   THE TRAILER WAS IN THE SCRUB DOWN FACILITY.  THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS CALLED.          SUBSTANCES RELEASED: CHLORINE RELEASE

name: 50 Gallons Hydraulic Spill at Simplot
incident_summary: A hose on a loader broke spilling 30-50 gallons of hydraulic oil to the soil. The soil will be excavated and hauled off for disposal.

name: Davis County - Used Oil @ Grease Monkey shops
incident_summary: During on on-site inspection by DWMRC staff, they witnessed an employee at Grease Monkey #951 (Centerville location shown on attached map) washing the shop floor with water and then  using a squeegee to push the wash water outside onto the concrete apron surrounding the facility.  The wash water was contaminated with used oil and possibly antifreeze.  Black staining on the concrete shows that in the past the wash water would either flow into a storm drain located in their parking lot or flow, off of their property, into the public road gutter and then into the gutter storm drain.  The facility manager stated the was how employees always washed down the shop.  Grease Monkey # 796 (at 2142 West 1800 North, Clinton) also has black stains on the concrete which run from the shop bay doors to the storm drains.
title_eventname: Davis County - Used Oil @ Grease Monkey shops

name: Duchesne County Treated Injection Water Release
incident_summary:
The caller reported that a buried, steel pipeline leaked 107 barrels of treated injection water that ran off the well site and into a dry drainage.  It flowed down the drainage and into a stock water pond that was full to capacity causing the pond to breach and allowing the injection water and contaminated stock water to flow approximately 5049 additional feet down the dry drainage.

The well number is 22-6-9-17.

The line has been shut in and isolated.

No water bodies besides the stock pond were impacted.

Clean up will include removing all contaminated water from the pond and flushing the pond and drainage with approximately 200 barrels of fresh water.  Nathan Hall is overseeing the clean up.
title_eventname: Duchesne County Treated Injection Water Release

name: SLC Airport - Jet fuel release
incident_summary: Caller reported that during refueling of a private jet, approximately 9 gallons of jet fuel vented off from the wing. Caller estimated that 2 gallons of fuel entered a nearby storm drain. TAC Air personnel responded by placing booms inside the sotrm drain box to isolate and contain the release. Ken Pratt (SLC Airport) was additionally notified of the release.

name: Salt Lake Co - Potassium Permanganate
incident_summary: Driver observed material leaking from a container.  Yard personnel were notified and investigated.  Tote inside a container released contents potassium permanganate.  Totes were stacked.  Heavier tote partially crushed bottom tote.  Estimated volume of release is 100 gallons.  Cleanup contractor, Pacific West is enroute to remediate.

name: Roosevelt - Condensate release
incident_summary: Caller reported that a truck rollover resulted in the release of 5-7 bbls. condensate.  Rollover caused a valve on the truck to open, resulting in the release.  Responsible party is awaiting Blue Stakes clearance before excavating impacted soils.  Responsible party agreed to provide a clean-up report to the Tri-County Health Department within 30 days.

name: McNeilus (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Parking brake on vehicle (refuse truck) was either not functioning/set properly.  The vehicle rolled down slope and jumped a curb.  The curb ruptured the fuel tank causing the release of an estimated 43 gallons of diesel fuel.  Release was entirely to asphalt.  Fuel was wholly contained on ashpalt and did not impact surface waters nor storm/sanitary sewers.  Tank has 75 gallon capacity, company estimates tank held 3/4 full at the time of the incident.  Release estimate based on volume recovered.  TW Co. responded and is performing remediation.  Release is being secured using absorbants.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Residents in a house remodeled into 4 apartments complained of strong gas like odors on Sat. morning, especially the north side apartments.  Questar was called and they investigated the site and determined the odor was not due to leaking natural gas.  Questar thought the odor was more like gasoline.  Bear River HD was called to investigate (Keith Larson) and he obtained high hydrocarbon readings with his instruments both inside the house and in the soil outside on the north side.  BioWest was called in to mitigate and remediate.  The residents were evacuated and BioWest dug a 20’ x 3’ x 3.5’ trench.  The soils were overstocked and are being landfarmed at the site.  The residents have been allowed to move back in late on Monday (11/06).  The PRP has not been determined but evidence suggests that this dumping may have been going on over a long period of time.  The amount of the release is unknown and the cause is unknown at this time.  The local fire dept. and police department have investigated.  Notified Local Fire Dept.

name: Potential Release - Tractor Trailer Truck Accident
incident_summary:
THE CALLER IS REPORTING A POTENTIAL RELEASE OF HEPTANE (UN 1206) AND
  CORROSIVE CLEANERS (UN 3266) HYPOCHLORITE SOLUTION (UN 1791).  THE

  STATED THAT INTERSTATE 80 WAS SHUT DOWN DUE TO THE ACCIDENT.

  CALLER STATED THE HEPTANE WAS TRANSPORTED IN TWO (02) 55 GALLON
  DRUMS, HYPOCHLORITE SOLUTION WAS IN TWO (02) 5 GALLON PAILS/BUCKETS,
  AND CORROSIVE CLEANERS WERE IN TWO (02) 5 GALLON PAILS/BUCKETS AS
  WELL.
title_eventname: Potential Release - Tractor Trailer Truck Accident

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: The owner of property at 1680 South Redwood Road noticed a gasoline smell in what was supposed to be clean fill.  The driver of the fill hauler was Paul Mechan (638-4359).  The property owner followed the haul truck back to what appears to be a LUST removal at 1478 South 300 West.

name: Ethanol spill near Bountiful
incident_summary: Tanker overturned causing pup to spill ethanol. Unknown amount spilled to asphalt and in storm drain. Storm drain and spill has been burmed by fire department. Environmental Restoration will transfer load.

name: Silver Eagle Refining Storm Water Deluge
incident_summary: Refinery draining was deluged by precipitation.  Storm system flows to separator.  Petroleum product on drainage found an ignition source, flashed and extinguished.  This event occurred on-site.  Facility crew has been working to remediate.  System discharges to A-1 Canal and South Davis Sewer District.  Facility notified South Davis Sewer District and is monitoring; they reported to PRP that they have not seen anything.  Davis County Health was aware of this incident when notified by DEQ and is active in response.
title_eventname: Silver Eagle Refining Storm Water Deluge

name: Phillips Petroleum (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Sulfur recovery unit down at 15:15  The SRU interlocked as a result of a blown fuse on a board associated with the IR thermal sensor.  Feed was out of the unit for approximately 20 minutes during the period from 15:15 to 15:40 on 1/6/96.             Instrument and Electronics personnel were called to the plant to assist in restarting the unit and to determine the cause of the fuse fault.

name: Union Pacfic Railroad (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Material identified as adhesive UN1133 (paint-related) was released from product packaging inside rail shipping container.  An amount desecribed only as a few gallons was released to asphalt and contained.  Pacific West was contracted to remediate.  PRP reports no exposures, no impact to waterways.

name: Summer's Auto Wrecking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Individual reported poor waste practices of Summer's Auto Wrecking.  Materials such as motoroil, battery acid, radiator fluid were poured over ground in significant quantities. Venting of air conditioners was another common practice.  Individual was hoping that someone would inspect the facility.  DERR contacted SL Co. Health Dept. and SHW.

name: Salt Lake Co -
incident_summary: Caller alleges intentional leaking, spilling and dumping by active pouring, opening of hoses, etc.  Caller claims materials released include diesel fuel, engine oil (new and used), hydraulic oil, and anti-freeze.  Facility has 40-50 semi-trucks many of which are left to leak out.  Caller alleges hundreds of gallons.  Facility has brand new building and is located next to the county landfill.  Facility is the last building on the left driving northbound on Legacy View Blvd.  Caller answered in the affirmative when asked if the facility was near to the wetlands and canal which courses along the south boundary of the Salt Lake Landfill.  Per an NRC report: materials cited also include paint thinner and turpentine and several additional pieces of alternative info.

name: Holly Refinery - Possible release of benzene above
title_eventname: Holly Refinery - Possible release of benzene above

name: Wasatch County -- RV in Jordanelle Reservoir
incident_summary: A mobile home rolled into Jordanelle Reservoir, releasing an unknown amount of oil or fuel which created a light sheen on the surface of the water.  Central Utah Water Conservancy District has responded and deployed booms to contain the sheen and is trying to contact the responsible party.
title_eventname: Wasatch County -- RV in Jordanelle Reservoir

name: SLC - Release of Used Oil
address: UPRR rail spur at 600 North Overpass
address_location: UPRR rail spur at 600 North Overpass
incident_summary: Caller reported that a vac-truck was transferring used oil to a rail car. Towards the end of the transfer the hose kicked out of the rail car and sprayed used oil to the surrounding rail ballast, asphalt, and concrete.  Containment pans beneath the rail car captured some of the used oil. No surface water or storm drains were released. Total quantity released was estimated to be less than 25 gallons. Clean Harbors sent a field crew to remediate the release.

name: Sandy -- Diesel Fuel Spill on I-15
incident_summary: Semi truck hit what was believed to be a crowbar in the road, puncturing a saddle tank and releasing an estimated 110 gallons of diesel fuel onto the pavement and the side of the road.  No waterways or storm drains were impacted.  Sandy FD and UDOT Incident Management contained spill and cleaned up excess fuel.  Envirocare was contacted by company and responded to location.  UDOT will supervise cleanup.
title_eventname: Sandy -- Diesel Fuel Spill on I-15

name: Groendyke Trucking (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: A tanker hauling hydrofluoric acid has rolled over on a isolated section of I-70 near Green River.  No acid has leaked to this point.  Only one person lives within a one mile perimeter of the spill and that person has been evacuated.  UHP is reportedly on the scene.  A contractor will off load the acid into another tanker.

name: Kennecott Process Water Release
incident_summary: Caller is reporting that at 04:35 they noticed water coming from the ground. The line located there is the Slag Mill Concentrate Line. The line was shut in and the release secured. and they spent the day attempting to locate the leak. They currently don't have an estimate of how much was released. The release occurred near the Slag Pot Cooling Area . The surveyed the area and did not find any surface flow from the area. Will notify DEQ of anything changes. Samples were collected for analysis. Will contact permitting authorities Tuesday for updates.

name: HOCIM Cement Company Inc. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports that at start up of the plant this morning there was an opacity excedence for over 2 hours.  The plant has been down for 15 days due to an annual shutdown for maintenance.  Upon start up the main baghouse takes some time to achieve optimal operating efficiencies.  The plant is running at normal permitted levels now.   Partial calcine material in stack released from burning process of plant production cycle.
title_eventname: HOCIM Cement Company Inc. (Null RP Substituted)

name: West Haven - Diesel Spill
incident_summary:
Caller stated that an SUV lost control and hit one of the saddle tanks of a semi truck (with JB Hunt Transportation) causing the tank to rupture loosing all of its diesel. Approximately 50 gallons of diesel were released onto the roadway and nearby soil. Craig Jorgensen with Weber-Morgan Health was on scene along with Bren Edwards with UDOT. EnviroCare was dispatched to remediate and they are done with the cleanup. No waterways or storm drains were impacted. 

UPDATE: Dimensions of hard surface impacted are approximately 800ft long by 30ft wide. 
Bill Talbott (812-629-4023) with Premium Environmental (the spill management company for JB Hunt) also dispatched Lincoln Environmental who confirmed that cleanup has been completed.

name: Sewer Connected to Storm Drain past 2-3 years
incident_summary:
Homeowner called to report a sewer connection that was connected to a storm drain near his house.  A new home is being built next door to a home where they tore out the driveway to repair the connection.  The caller asked the workers what was going on and they told him the sewer line from the home had been connected to the storm drain.  Caller said they seemed to be in a big hurry to fix the connection and get it covered back up.

After thinking about it over the weekend, he had to call and report it to someone.
title_eventname: Sewer Connected to Storm Drain past 2-3 years

name: Farmington Canyon - Fuel Release
incident_summary: Caller reported a private citizen rolled a Snow Cat machine along Skyline Road below Bountiful Peak resulting in the release of fuel, motor oil, hydraulic fluids, and antifreeze. Machine rolled off the road in the area of Farmington Lake.  Other Snow Cat machines nearby were able to upright the machine and remove it from the area.  USFS personnel were notified of the incident and sent a crew to inspect the area on 2/8/18.  Area is covered in snow and was only accessible by snowmobile.  Release was reported as close to but not in Farmington Lake. The lake is reportedly frozen at this time.  Quantities released are unknown however a potential 30-40 gallons of fuel may have been released. No remedial actions have been taken.  Contact for the USFS for the incident is Polly Bergseng (801) 733-2686.

name: Thatcher Chemical (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Two compounds - Soda Ash and Sulfur Dioxide were being mixed when it created a reactive mixture of Sodium Bi-sulfite which was too strong for the scrubbers and was released into the atmosphere.  Employees estimate about 1 pound of chemical was released.  Six persons reported breathing the fumes; two were taken to the hospital, though not serious (supposedly).  Police, fire and HazMat teams responded.

name: Western Metals (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that Western Metals was loading junk vehicles through the crusher when one of the vehicles gas tank was punctured igniting a fire at the facility.  Local Fire Dept. arrived on-scene to a large fire.  Approximately 20,000 gallons of fire suppression water was used to extinguish the fire.  While inspecting the facility afterward the BRHD noticed a distinct gasoline odor in the air.  Concerned that additional fuel inside other vehicles may not have burned off in the fire and had migrated off-site with the fire suppression water through a storm drain and entered a nearby drainage ditch, the BRHD and local Fire Dept. deployed pads and booms inside the ditch to contain any potential releases.  The BRHD did not see a sheen on the water in the ditch.

name: Weber Co Diesel Release
incident_summary: Ten gallons of diesel fuel was released from a transfer line while refueling a locomotive.  Fuel spilled to ballast.  Response crew will remediate with granular absorbents.  No impact to surface waters or storm drains.

name: Uinta County - Hydraulic Oil Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a spill of approximately 85-90 gallons of hydraulic fluid from a 1.5" hydraulic line on Hitachi EX18 shovel.  Release occurred in one of the pits.  Crew shut down the equipment.  After shovel is repaired they will walk it off the area of impact to perform cleanup.  No impact to surface waters.  Facility has 100 ton haul truck to which they deposit excavating contaminated soils.  When full that will be delivered to Uinta County Landfill for disposal.

name: WVC - Riter Canal Diesel Release
incident_summary: A resident was walking his dog along the Riter Canal near 5600 West 2550 South when he noticed a storng diesel odor. John Hoggan (SLCo Health Dept.) and Randy Peterson (WVC Public Works) responded to the scene and observed diesel product in the canal. SLCo Health and WVC are attempting to determine where the diesel contamination entered into the canal. The source of the release is unknown.

name: Smith/Croger Bakery (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports that a freezer line or coil carrying anhydrous ammonia broke and released 100-150 pounds of material.  The plant was evacuated at 0518.  Layton FD is on scene, and has measured 220 ppm ammonia in the outside air.  Weather: Rainy, 60 F.

Bruce Brown with Davis County Health Department will send an investigator to the scene.

UPDATE: Davis Co. Health reports that their inspector arrived at the scene and the ammonia was contained for the most part in the building.  Building will be vented and cleared of released material.   The dept. of agriculture inspector was on scene and will inspect the freezer to see if anything in the freezer is contaminated.

name: Crude oil spill in Provo River, Utah County
incident_summary:
Tanker truck roll over in Provo Canyon is releasing crude into the Provo river.  An estimated 1000 gallons of crude has made its way to the river at about mile marker 13, about 1 mile down from the Sundance turnoff in Provo canyon.
Fire department is reportedly on sight.  EPA has dispatched an emergency contractor.
EPA is attempting to get additional info from fire department about responsible party. 

UPDATE (12/1/15 - dtu):  On Saturday 11/28/2015, the NRC was notified by the following entities:

State Fire Marshall's Office called NRC #1134430 at 10:26 a.m.
Provo dispatch center called NRC #1134433 at 10:54 a.m.
Savage Services (RP) called NRC #113448 at 2:29 p.m.
title_eventname: Crude oil spill in Provo River, Utah County

name: La Rancherita Food Vendor (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Employee for South Salt Lake witnessed a curbside taco vendor discharging their waste water directly into a storm drain.  Darren said they had been warned of this action once already.  Vendor is parked on west side of 300 West.

Response: I notified Kevin Oakleberry with the SLVHD and he will look into the problem.
title_eventname: La Rancherita Food Vendor (Null RP Substituted)

name: Vernal - Hydraulic oil release at Simplot
incident_summary: Caller reported that a hydraulic line on a rotary drill rig ruptured releasing an unknown quantity of hydraulic oil (current best guess estimate is 50-75 gallons).  Once the line is repaired and the oil reservoir tank is refilled, the released quantity will be determined.  The release impacted the overburden soils beneath the drill rig before two small plastic swimming pools could be placed as temporary secondary containment to contain the release.
title_eventname: Vernal - Hydraulic oil release at Simplot

name: resident (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports an elderly woman called to have the Health Department check out her husbands chemistry lab in their home.  The husband was once an active chemist working from home, but has now been diagnosed with Alzheimer's.  The SLVHD identified 200 grams of crystallized Picric Acid.  The SLVHD called in HazMat Team 6 and is in the process of calling the bomb technicians.  DERR provided the number of UDEQ/SHW, Allen Moore, in anticipation of a request to detonate an explosive.   The SLVHD noted the evacuation distance for the substance is 330 feet.

name: Altamont - Used oil release
incident_summary: Caller reported a 3.7 gallon used oil spill to a dry creek bed.  The spill had been cleaned up at the time of the call to DERR.  Caller said the contaminated dirt was taken to IWM disposal site.  Caller reported the spill to DOGM.

name: Salt Lake Co.: Used oil release at Kennecott
incident_summary: Caller reported an estimated 150-gallon used oil release onto a sealed hard surface inside a building.  The cause of this spill was due to a mechanical O-ring failure on piping.  The spill was completely contained and did not impact the environment.  Cleanup is underway.
title_eventname: Salt Lake Co.: Used oil release at Kennecott

incident_summary:
The caller reported a spill of approximately 75 gallons of diesel fuel from a saddle tank due to a traffic accident.

The accident was reported to be on Bangerter Highway just north of 7000 S.  The caller did not know whether the accident was in the northbound or southbound lanes.

There was no threat to water bodies or drains.

name: Utah Co - Rollover SR-6 Diesel/Xylene
incident_summary: Tractor-trailer rollover went down the embankment.  Wreck caused release of diesel fuel, and flammable liquid (xylene).  Xylene was contained in three (330 gallon) totes being transported in the trailer.   All three are leaking: one had drained, a second has significant leak and third has less significant leak.  Lincoln Environmental has been called out to do the cleanup.   Actual volume of diesel fuel release is unknown at this time.  UHP and County Fire Marshal responded to the scene.  Roadway is closed to facilitate access by Lifeflight.

name: Diesel Fuel Spill near Green River
incident_summary: A traffic accident caused the rollover of a semitruck and the release of about 75 gallons of diesel fuel to the soil. The impacted soil will be excavated.
title_eventname: Diesel Fuel Spill near Green River
