name: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water
incident_summary:
Caller reported a release of 145 barrels of treated injection water that ran off the right-of-way into a dry drainage ditch. Clean-up is underway with the line currently isolated. Completion of the repair is planned for Monday, July 10, 2017. No waterways were impacted. 

Caller also contacted Nathan Hall with DEQ, Amy Doebele with DOGM, and Randy Bywater with the BLM.

name: Diesel fuel spill near Howell
incident_summary: Truck struck guardrail puncturing a saddle tank and spilling an unknown amount of diesel fuel to the soil. Envirocare has responded and will clean up the spill.

name: Gary Clark (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Storage container described as 100 gallon capacity cement box, with yellow grease overflowed via overflow valve into drainage ditch and into slow moving water.  Spill created a sheen 4 feet wide and 1/4 mile long.  Smelled of rotten oils and lard.  A crew was brought in on 9/03/09 to remove contaminated soils.  Soil samples were sent to Utility Testing Laboratory (SLC).  Release rate was reeported as 10 gallons per day.  Quantity released 600 gallons.
If same incident, DWQ was notified last week of this from Davis County Health.

name: U.S. WEST COMMUNICATIONS (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: SPILL OF DIESEL FUEL #2 DIESEL FUEL 30 GAL.

name: Specialized Rail (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Semi traveling north through Wellsville (Sardine) Canyon lost control going down at the "big bend".  Crashed into Jersey barriers rupturing saddle tank and about 200 gallon of diesel spilled into soils along road.  Once snow stops, they will have TW Company come onsite and excavate contaminated soils.  Bear River Health was specifically concerned that DNR/DWR be contacted but was unable to do so over weekend.

name: Brenntag Pacific  (contact Shelly Thompson) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
A semi truck hauling 12.5% sodium hypochlorite (bleach) over turned on westbound I-80 at mile marker 168.  The spill has been contained in the median and in soil near wetlands and about 150 feet from the Weber River.  A cleanup contractor is enroute.  Summit County Health Department is on site with other responders.
***************Update*****************
Also spilled - 300 gallons of Cobra Tech - a mixture of sodium hydroxide and Sodium Polytriazole.  
*****************Update************************
Facility contact reported that the Cobra Tech chemical was not spilled and that less than a gallon of the bleach entered the wetland.

UPDATE #3 7/17/08 13:23:  Information from John Urquhart (CURA Emergency Services) calling on behalf of the RP.  Caller reported that TW Company was contracted to provide clean-up services and are currently on-scene.  The truck was transporting 9 totes of bleach.  TW Company is transferring remaining bleach inside the damaged totes into new totes and will then attempt to upright the overturned trailer.  Total quantity of bleach released was estimated at 200 gallons.  A small amount of diesel (3 gallons) and motor oil (10 quarts) was released to the roadway and was contained using absorbants.  See also NRC #877607.
title_eventname: Brenntag Pacific  (contact Shelly Thompson) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Davis County Chlorine Release
incident_summary:
The caller reported that the HAFB Fire Department responded to a release of chlorine from a cylinder at Building 782 Pump House.  The chlorine is used for water treatment.

The Fire Department stopped the leak using an A Kit.  The cylinder was full prior to the leak so it was weighed and it was determined that 29 pounds of chlorine was released.  The RQ for chlorine is 10 pounds.

There was no impact to any water or water bodies and nobody was injured.

The caller had not notified the NRC but was going to after this call.

Note that the map location is just marking HAFB but not the exact location of Building 782.

name: Utah County Used Oil Spill
incident_summary:
Caller reported that early last spring her neighbor, Mr. Perez left a very full oil pan open to the elements in his driveway.  In the late autumn her healthy bushes which once thrived in the strip between their driveways died.  She is convinced that the cause was oil from the oil pan.

She reported this issue to her Homeowners Association (HOA) and the Local Health Department.  The HOA dug up the bushes and will plant new ones this spring.  She reported that in the trench where the bushes were dug up you can see a darker area of soil which her son says looks like oil staining.  There is no smell of oil and no oil staining of the neighbors driveway that would indicate a release of oil that ran into the soil.

She would like the soil in the trench tested.

name: Thatcher Chemical Nitrite Acid Release

name: World Class Auto (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Anonymous caller filed a report with the National Response Center reporting the release of automotive fluids to the storm drains and soils at World Class Auto - an automotive repair/oil change operation.  Caller reported that floor drains at the facility are covered in oily sludge.  Handling of used oils and other wastes is generally poor.  The drains inside the oil-change bays are pumped to a storage tank outside the building.  The drain line connecting the drain to the tank has ruptured, releasing the oil directly into the soils.  Caller reported that at one point these oils surfaced at the southwest corner of the building (near the exits for the oil-change bays).  Owner then covered the area with a small strip of asphalt to hide the release.  Caller also states that a sewer manhole in the back of the store is not regularly inspected by the city.

UPDATE 4/2/2009 15:23:  Information from Boyd Stringham.  Utah County Health Department visited site 4/2/2009. Met with Rod Martin, owner. Mr. Martin walked UCHD through facility's oil collection and storage process. As oil is collected it is temporarily stored in an approx. 100 gal. steel tank inside the facility. This tank is equipped with a pump and 1 -1/2 in. quick-connect hydraulic  hose which is pressurized as needed for transfer of oil to another approx. 500 gal. outside tank (attached photo). This tank is also steel and is situated above ground within a concrete block berm area. The facility contracts with Emerald Oil to empty the oil tank, as well as barreled anti-freeze, at approx. 2-month intervals. Mr. Martin also explained and pointed out the ruptured drain line in question. A permanent steel line (1 inch?) was originally installed during facility construction between the inside tank and outside tank. On one occasion while still using this line for transfer it was noted that oil surfaced near the outside tank. It was discovered that the line had ruptured. Use of the line was discontinued and transfers are now completed using the portable hydraulic line. Soil near the outside tank was impacted during this event but it appears to be a de minimis amount. Other heavy staining on asphalt or soil surfaces in the area of the tank was not noted. Standing oils and/or fluids in the outside tank's berm were not noted. "Floor drains" in oil change area are self-contained sumps which are cleaned out as needed. Current oil handling practices, including draining of filters, and general shop maintenance appeared to be within acceptable standards.  Oil absorbents are readily available within the shop for spills.  UCHD did not note other oil-related violations during the visit. Mr. Martin also stated that he suspected the reporting party to be a recently dismissed employee.

name: unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
This was a nasty crash, a really hot fire resulted and apparently burned most of the crude oil.  The truck crashed rounding a curve between Emma Park and the Carbon Power Plant on US-191 along Willow Creek. The truck driver was killed in the crash.  This was Uintah black wax crude, so it clumps in the water and will help the cleanup.  The tanker and pup was carrying approximately 280 barrels of crude.  Unknown how much escaped to Willow Creek, but you can see crude oil balls for several miles downstream.  We are thinking that most of the crude burned.  There was a rainstorm last night after the crash which raised the creek level and washed contamination further downstream.  Now that the creek waters have receded there are crude oil balls in the rocks on the sides of the stream downstream.  EnviroCare staff (cleanup contractor) are onsite beginning the assessment and cleanup.  Dave Ariotti has been coordinating with all the involved parties.  Craig Myers, OSC with EPA (303-808-1738) was at the site this morning to do an assessment.  The tanker was hauling crude for the Foreland Refining Corp, Pete Ipson is the contact (801-231-4456).  Terrie Wright (435-636-7624) with Southeast Public Health is acting as the local PIO.  Dave and I collected water samples this morning at the first boom below the crash site.  There are two booms in place at this point.  The spill was apparently on private ground but not far from a BLM parcel.


>>> On 9/16/2011 at  8:12 AM, David Ariotti wrote:

Two skirted booms deployed 2 mi. Below wreck.  11:00 pm.  Raise in creek from storm moved product downstream.  Est 1.5 mi of stream and bank impacted.  More info when I have coverage. 
-----Original Message-----
David Ariotti (435) 636-7724 reports that the accident is located on SR 191 approximately 8 miles above the carbon power plant and four miles upstream from the confluence of the Price River and Willow Creek.  Black wax crude oil has been released in to Willow Creek.  He estimates no more than 10 barrels has reached the creek.  Most of the material is burning off.  He has checked approximately 3 miles downstream and found no evidence of spilled material.  He believes the solidified crude is being caught up on banks, weeds and pools.  Willow Creek enters the Price River downstream from the drinking water treatment plant, so there is no threat to the drinking water supply.
<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<update>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

incident_summary:
Caller reports that about 100 gallons of ‘dialectric fluid’ (mineral oil, PCB’s are less than 50 ppm concentration) and water was recovered from soil and asphalt at the scene of an accident.  A truck (lost brakes) crashed into a pad mounted transformer (owner not determined at this time) and knocked it over, moving it 35 feet off its base.  UP&L was called in as the UHP officer thought the transformer belonged to UP&L.  UP&L called in PacificWest Environmental Services to mitigate and remediate. 

UPDATE: 1700, 4/3/06: After the PacWest team had arrived at the scene, a UDOT employee arrived and claimed that UDOT owned the transformer.  (the transformer was laying on its side with the ID plate down)  The PacWest team was ordered back to home base, but they had built a small berm to catch mineral oil leaking from the transformer.  A small creek runs close to the site and is at risk.  This info was reported to the DERR, who then informed UDOT of the potential risk to state waters.  The DERR called DWQ and left a message on their 24/7 line.  The UHP case # is 2362, but as of 0830 on 04/04/06 the case info was not available from the UHP as the investigating officer was in court and not available.  UDOT is following up on obtaining the truck company information.  UDOT is remediating.

UPDATE 14:30 04/04/06, from Helen Sadik-MacDonald of UDOT: I was on-site this morning.  The semi-truck with flatbed ran over the pad-mounted transformer that operated I-70 lighting for the Mountain Dell turn-off.  Power was out overnight, may be out another day.  The transformer was dragged approximately 75 feet before vehicle came to a stop in a jack-knife position.  A plug at the base was broken off, sealed with plug n-dike by Hazmat team and continued to drip approximately 2ml/min after it was placed in a secondary containment.  The shed supervisor responded last night with berming dirt to protect the drainage to Mtn. Dell.  By morning, oil had leaked through secondary containment that was cracked.  TW Corporation responded to scene by order of trucking company at 10:15 April 4, 2006 and commenced excavation.  UP&L removed transformer and containment into another containment and returned with it to their facility on North Temple near Redwood Rd.  Salt Lake City watershed folks arrived early this morning and stayed for commencement of clean up.  All parties were concerned the clean up should not be delayed as rain is pending.  Fortunately, the ground was relatively dry, the berm that had been placed by UP&L yesterday had not been reached by leaking oil, and absorbents placed by shed crew including bermed dirt, had collected pooled oil.

name: America's Best (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
The building manager for Eagle Plaza hired the company America's Best Tree Landscaping to prune some trees.  Sometime over the weekend, the pruning machine blew a hydraulic line.  About 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid were released and got into a storm drain.

Response:  The pruning company workers merely put sawdust on the spill.  I have notified SLVHD and DWQ.  The manager for America's Best, Eric Berensen (573-1099) so far has not been notified.

Update 8/29/06: Rolf Larsen with SLVHD reported that the manager for the America’s Best tree pruning company, Eric Berensen, was contacted and decided, after much discussion, to hire the contractor E.T. Technologies to clean up the hydraulic spill that his company had caused at the Eagle Plaza parking lot over the weekend.

The contractor showed up on-site Monday (the 28th) around 5 pm and placed a sealer on the affected asphalt that soaked in and sealed off the asphalt from further degradation.  They also spread a mixture onto the asphalt that contains biological “bugs” that will eat and degrade the hydraulic fluid remaining within the asphalt.  Part of the parking lot asphalt will likely have to be replaced as well.

The hydraulic fluid apparently did NOT get into any drainages.  It flowed into the first storm drain box in the parking lot and then into a second drain box in the street, but there was no hydraulic fluid that was found downstream in a third drain box nor was any found at the point where the water enters Big Cottonwood Creek.

name: Sanish Fork septic Dumping
address: 1819 S Main Street, Spanish Fork Utah
address_location: 1819 S Main Street, Spanish Fork Utah
incident_summary:
This report was received through the EPA by email. Text included.
Hi Jude,
 
I just spoke with a citizen, Darwin Bundy, about a portable toilet company directly dumping the waste into the river.  He said the business is along the Jordan River, but everything else he described about the location and other info I’ve found indicate it’s the Spanish Fork.  He said he used to be acquainted with a relative (he thought the nephew) of the owner, Don Butler.  He was at the business years ago and saw a pipe out back on the east side of the building.  He asked the nephew what it was, and the nephew said it was supposed to be hidden.  The nephew said the company used it to dump the portable toilet waste into the river.  Darwin could not recall the specific road, but he said it was on the highway that goes north and south between Spanish Fork and Salem and it then goes west to Payson.  He said the business is in Spanish Fork.  Darwin said he called someone at EPA about this issue years ago and never heard back, and he was driving by the other day, which prompted him to call again.  He doesn’t know if the business is still owned by Don Butler or if the practice is still going on.  Darwin said you are welcome to call him for information.  801-380-7118
 
Here’s some more information I found on what appears to be the company.
· Name: Home Away Portable Toilets
· Address: 1819 S. Main St. (Hwy 198), Spanish Fork, UT
· Google Aerials and Street View show portable toilets outside and the Spanish Fork River along the east side of the property.  The toilets on Street View indicate the company is named Almost Home.
· Utah County Assessor Information: This address is owned by Leah Butler.
· Utah Secretary of State business search: Almost Home Enterprises in Spanish Fork shows Margie Butler as the registered agent at 1817 S. Main St. in Spanish Fork.

UPdate 02/05/2014
I spoke with the complainant today who advised me the information he has is over 10 years old.  He explained he called again after he recently drove by the place.  I advised him that EPA CID conducted an investigation, presumably from the information he previously reported, that resulted in Nicholas Butler being criminally charged in 2002 for a Clean Water Act violation.  According to the electronic records, the case was resolved through a guilty plea.  SA Mike Bergin investigated the case.

name: GSL Minerals Oil Release
incident_summary:
On June 30th, sometime between 2:30 AM and 5:30 AM, a hose on a recirculating pump ruptured and about 1600 gallons of heavy oil was released.   The recirculating pump is as part of the heating circuit that keeps the oil at about 160 degrees Fahrenheit so that it will flow.  The majority of the oil lost was contained within the primary and secondary containment for the oil storage tanks.  About 300 to 400 gallons was sprayed outside of the containment area onto the ground.  Of the oil sprayed outside of containment, less than 5 gallons flowed into our drainage ditch, which discharges into the Great Salt Lake more than a mile downstream of the spill.
 
Upon reaching the water, the heavy oil clumped into tar balls that float on top of the water and tend to cling to the banks of the ditch.  Absorbent booms that were already in place in the ditch prevented the oil from migrating more than 100 yards downstream.   Additional booms were placed in the stream to absorb the oil.   Inspection of the drainage ditch showed no evidence of oil beyond the initial 100 yards.  Inspection of the discharge point, Outfall 001, showed no evidence of either tar balls or oil sheen.
 
GSLM has hired an outside contractor to remediate the spill, including removal of oil (tar) from the ditch.

name: Siemans (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Representative at Lakeside Power Plant project construction site called to determine the reporting requirements associated with a a release (of hydrazine; material was indentified by the caller after inquiry).  Caller alleges a very dilute solution as residual in pipe residue following a water and steam flush.  A sample has been collected and submitted for chemical analysis.  Caller will call back (must go to a meeting).  
UPDATE 12:48 - Pipe connection came loose causing release of an estimated 100 gallons of a diluted hydrazine solution.  Caller termed this incident suspicious because the clamps securing the hose connection require significant force to release.  Release happened during night shift.  Original product hydrazine is 35% before dilution.  Material was released to soils.  Other releases have occurred by all were to concrete.  The later were vacuumed with a shopvac and deposited into a holding tank on-site.  The project is perforned under an associated wetlands permit due to its proximity to wetlands, etc.  
UPDATE 15:10-16:10 - Followup notification to record that EDTA ammonia is another component of the piping rinsate effluent.  Area of soils impacted, estimated at 40ft x 60ft., has been scraped.  Soils have been stages in containment area under final disposition is determined.  Three remedial soil samples have been collected for hydrazine analysis: (1) background, (2) pre-excavation, and (3) post excavation.  Two liquid samples were collected.  One sample was collected from between the two gas turbine units from liquids discovered prior to the introduction of chemicals to the lines to be flushed.  The second liquid sample was collected from the spill prior to vacuum recovery.  Due to unique analyte (hydrazine) results are anticipated in about 10 days.

Caller related that the location described places the vessel in Box Elder county (about five miles north of the county line across the lake). State Parks personnel are believed to be on-scene or acting in some response capacity. 

UPDATE 14:38 from Bear River Health - Fuel is gasoline and fuel storage consists of two 700-gallon tanks. Boat is fully engulfed.  Park Service is on-scene and remains at a distance; they believe the boat may explode.    Nobody was on-board. 

UPDATE 18:59 Utah State Parks Public Affairs Coordinator - Salt Lake State Park harbor master responded on water to brine shrimp support boat fire.  Antelope Island State Park Ranger also responded on-water in separate vessel.  Park personnel were in contact with Box Elder Sheriff's Office during time on-water. Likely it is a mid-vessel fuel tank (~600 gallons) burning. There two, completely full, intact 750 gallon fuel tanks located at the bow with small number of 5/10 gallon propane tanks next to fuel storage tanks.  Company was contacting private helicopter about dropping lake water onto the vessel in attempt to extinguish. 

UPDATE 19:38 - Utah State Parks Public Affairs Coordinator - Fire has been extinguished and the vessel has been towed back to the originating harbor.
title_eventname: Box Elder Co - Vessel Fire on GSL

name: Wayne G. Brierley (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported that a large pool of gasoline exists in the site area on the shallow groundwater.  Gasoline plume has been encountered several times by Layton City officials while in process of installing or reparing utility lines.  Site was formerly occupied by a service station which had tall, cylindrical AGST's extending 2'-3' into the soil.  Site is now occupied by Ron Jaques Auto Sales.  Site is located about 3/4 - 1 mile SW of Layton Hills Mall on the east side of Main Street. A Taco Time restaurant is next to site and Young Chevrolet is across street from site.  I-15 is immediately east of the site.  Davis County Health Dept. believes there is high potential of fire from the gasoline (the gasoline in an open trench on-site caught fire on one occasion) and a high potential that gasoline vapors will enter nearby houses and businesses.  Gasoline odors have been smelled in the adjacent Taco Time.  Wayne Brierley has owned site since 1976.  Jim Mason, Asst. Layton City Manager (546-8502) has worked closely with Layton City Fire Dept. and is aware of the city's previous actions related to the gasoline plume.  He reported that groundwater from the site is believed to impact irrigation ditches.  Paul Zahn (LUST) has agreed to take initial lead on the site to determine if owner will voluntarily remediate site. Site could eventually be referred to WQ based on LUST/WQ MOU.

incident_summary: Caller reported a fire that started in a trailer resulting in several hazardous materials being released including 4-5 gallons of an insoluble water proofing agent, 5 gallons of mineral spirits, 5 gallons of gas, and some caulking agent. name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller observed what appears to be motor oil flowing along the street curb.  Area of visual stain begins two houses up, shows a 6-inch wide swath and flows for approximately two city blocks down to 1300 East.  Caller suspects it likely enters a storm drain down stream which would feed into Emmigration Creek.  Caller noted on-going contruction work and believes the material originated with a piece of construction equipment.  Believes vehicles will be back tomorrow (6/16).

name: Rosevelt Top Stop Release
incident_summary: Release occurred at a Top-Stop facility.  PRP as identifed, was refueling both diesel saddle tanks on a tractor.  When driver discovered second line releasing he shut the line.  An estimated 25-60 gallons of diesel was released.  An estimated volume of thirty-one gallons flowed from the containment pad and entered a nearby creek.  Fire Dept responded.  Response crew has deployed booms and absorbents.  Contractor (Envirocare) out of Salt Lake has been mobilized (E.T.A. is several hours).

The pole had apparently rotted and strong overnight winds knocked the pole and the transformers down onto an asphalt parking area.  UP&L crews arrived on-scene to clean-up the released mineral oil.

name: Diesel from Refrig Trailer
incident_summary: Caller is making notification on behalf of client (PRP).  PRP was notified by facility personnel this morning of an event that occurred on Saturday 9/7/2013.  PRP has trailer w/refrigeration unit staged at yard of Motus-Link.  Trailer was blown over by strong winds.  Fuel system on refrigeration unit was ruptured and diesel was released to asphalt. The reporting party indicated that there didn't appear to be  infiltration into the ground.

name: UPDATE Grand Co Well Release
incident_summary:
Dan Jarvis is reporting that there is a welll out of control at location in Grand County. Bart Kettle with DOGM isl on sceene and estimates the flow between 75 and 100 bbls/hour. SW Energy is the PRP and has a crew on site working to repair the well. The suspected cause is a failed casing. 

The Crude oil, produced water mix is flowing towards the Green River in a dry wash. DOGM is requesting a DE on site to look over this incident. Number was passed along to Dan Jarvis and he will contact him directly. I will also contact DE office.

Dave Cunningham will also contact Dave Ariotti regarding release. Dave Cunningham will notify local EMS through the Sheriff office.

Update: SW Energy is a company out of SLC, and acording to DOGM records they have a contact number of 801-532-6664, with Richard Smoot as the primary. This is not confirmed. Local Resources 
UPDATE 5/24/14 10:30:  DOGM reports rain is washing the spilled oil into the Green River.  On-site contractor says they do not have adequate resources to stop the spill.
